title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
順天府鄉試錄序
聖天子重明麗正化天下成文明
之治已閱十年餘維時
上下交孚明德光顯萬象煥新故
日月星辰麗乎天而天之文
以著百穀草木麗乎土而地
之文以弘易書詩禮春秋之
===
經麗乎人而人之文以宣朗
况京師首善當離明之地萬
邦承式環拱仰瞻文化興行
洋中溢外視四方尤甚盛焉
經曰
聖人南面而聽天下嚮明而治此
之謂也乃成化甲午秋適當
punctuated:
順天府鄉試錄序
聖天子重明麗正，化天下，成文明之治，已閱十年餘。維時上下交孚，明德光顯，萬象煥新。故日月星辰麗乎天，而天之文以著；百穀草木麗乎土，而地之文以弘；《易》、《書》、《詩》、《禮》、《春秋》之經麗乎人，而人之文以宣朗。况京師首善，當離明之地，萬邦承式，環拱仰瞻，文化興行，洋中溢外，視四方尤甚盛焉。《經》曰：「聖人南面而聽天下，嚮明而治。」此之謂也。乃成化甲午秋，適當
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination

The Sacred Son of Heaven, with redoubled brightness cleaving to the correct, has transformed all under Heaven and achieved an administration of civilized brilliance for more than ten years now. At this time, superior and inferior trust one another, luminous virtue shines forth gloriously, and all phenomena are renewed in splendor. Therefore, the sun, moon, stars, and constellations cleave to Heaven, whereby the patterns of Heaven are made manifest; the hundred grains, grasses, and trees cleave to the soil, whereby the patterns of Earth are expanded; and the Classics of the Changes (Yi), Documents (Shu), Odes (Shi), Rites (Li), and Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) cleave to humankind, whereby the patterns of humanity are proclaimed and illuminated. How much more so in the Capital, the premier place of moral excellence, situated in the region of Li brightness! The ten thousand states receive its model, encircling it in reverence and looking up to it in admiration; cultural transformation flourishes and spreads, brimming within and overflowing without, flourishing far more abundantly than in the four quarters. As the Classic says: "The sage faces south and listens to all under Heaven, facing the light to govern." This is what is meant. Now, in the autumn of the jiawu year of the Chenghua reign (1474), it happens to be…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
觀文取士之期先是大學選
歲貢之英京學及府州縣學
擇弟子員之傑內外羣有司
援官儒吏士兵校之賢而業
文者總千六百人有奇及時
以来分類以竢於是府尹臣
簡奏
===
請考試官
上委其柄於左庶子臣淳修撰臣
健其同考則教諭臣安臣廣
臣奎臣義臣廣烈訓導臣謹臣
深臣瓚皆起自徵聘監試則
監察御史臣福臣釗提調則
府丞臣川皆簡自
punctuated: 觀文取士之期。先是，大學選歲貢之英，京學及府州縣學擇弟子員之傑，內外羣有司援官儒、吏士、兵校之賢而業文者，總千六百人有奇，及時以来，分類以竢。於是，府尹臣簡奏請考試官。上委其柄於左庶子臣淳、修撰臣健；其同考則教諭臣安、臣廣、臣奎、臣義、臣廣烈，訓導臣謹、臣深、臣瓚，皆起自徵聘；監試則監察御史臣福、臣釗；提調則府丞臣川，皆簡自
translation_en:
…the scheduled time for examining literary writings and selecting scholars. Prior to this, the National University selected the finest of the Annual Tribute Students (suigong), the capital school and the prefectural, subprefectural, and county schools chose the most outstanding of their student員 (diziyuan), and the various civil and military authorities inside and outside the capital recommended worthy official scholars, clerks, subofficial functionaries, and military officers and soldiers who practiced literary composition. In all, they numbered more than one thousand six hundred men, who arrived on time and were grouped by category to await the examination. Thereupon, Your Servant Jian, the Prefect of Shuntian, submitted a memorial requesting the appointment of Examiners.

His Majesty entrusted this authority to Your Servant Chun, Left Mentor of the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent (zuo shuzi), and Your Servant Jian, Senior Compiler (xiuzhuan) of the Hanlin Academy. As for the Associate Examiners—Instructors (jiaoyu) Your Servant An, Your Servant Guang, Your Servant Kui, Your Servant Yi, and Your Servant Guanglie, together with Assistant Instructors (xundao) Your Servant Jin, Your Servant Shen, and Your Servant Zan—all were summoned by invitation from the provinces. For Surveillance Officials (jianshi), there were Investigating Censors (jiancha yushi) Your Servant Fu and Your Servant Zhao; and for Proctor, Vice Prefect (fucheng) Your Servant Chuan—all selected directly by…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
宸衷前期十日監試提調已入
院舉按
國章作新士氣惟和惟慎戮力
奮庸凡宿弊之蠹於前者一
時悉革而至公之道京師共
見焉臣等以八月庚寅
陛辭往蒞其事相與倡合庶官
===
對天矢心申嚴禁戒辛卯甲
午丁酉凡三試之於千六百
人中獲中選者百三十有五
人遵
制額也因鏤其氏名與其文之
純粹而超等者彙成鄉試錄
用上塵
punctuated: 宸衷。前期十日，監試、提調已入院，舉按國章，作新士氣，惟和惟慎，戮力奮庸，凡宿弊之蠹於前者，一時悉革，而至公之道，京師共見焉。臣等以八月庚寅陛辭，往蒞其事，相與倡合庶官，對天矢心，申嚴禁戒。辛卯、甲午、丁酉，凡三試之，於千六百人中獲中選者百三十有五人，遵制額也。因鏤其氏名，與其文之純粹而超等者，彙成《鄉試錄》，用上塵
translation_en: …the Imperial Mind. Ten days beforehand, the Surveillance Officials and the Proctor had already entered the examination compound. Conducting proceedings according to state statutes and renewing the morale of the scholars, they were harmonious and circumspect, joining forces and exerting themselves in service. All the chronic abuses that had caused harm in the past were completely eradicated at once, and the way of utmost impartiality was witnessed by all in the capital. On the gengyin day of the eighth month, your servants took leave of the Throne and went to oversee the affair. Together we led and united the various officials, swearing our hearts before Heaven and reiterating strict prohibitions and warnings. On the xinmao, jiawu, and dingyou days, we tested them in three sessions in all. Among the one thousand six hundred candidates, we obtained one hundred and thirty-five who were selected to pass, in compliance with the quota set by imperial decree. Accordingly, we have engraved their surnames and given names, along with their essays that are pure and of superior grade, compiling them into a Record of the Provincial Examination, so as to humbly present it above for…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
乙夜之覽下為來世之光故事
有序所以言作者之意臣竊
惟自有天地即有人文世運
流行相為表裏唐虞三代之
隆卓已漢唐宋以來在盛時
則文用顯明逮季世則文隨
委靡寧不繫於當時繼明照
===
四方觀文以化成天下之責
有未備歟洪惟我
太祖高皇帝完三光五嶽之氣振
起斯文如伏羲之文之古焉
時則人文光復於洪武
太宗文皇帝闡五經四書之旨亨
昌景運如帝堯之文之煥焉
punctuated: 乙夜之覽，下為來世之光。故事有序，所以言作者之意。臣竊惟：自有天地，即有人文，世運流行，相為表裏。唐、虞、三代之隆，卓已；漢、唐、宋以來，在盛時則文用顯明，逮季世則文隨委靡。寧不繫於當時繼明照四方、觀文以化成天下之責有未備歟？洪惟我太祖高皇帝，完三光五嶽之氣，振起斯文，如伏羲之文之古焉，時則人文光復於洪武；太宗文皇帝，闡《五經》、《四書》之旨，亨昌景運，如帝堯之文之煥焉，
translation_en:
… His Majesty's late-night reading above, and to serve as a glory for future generations below. By precedent there is a preface, whereby the intent of the compilers is expressed.

Your servant humbly reflects that ever since heaven and earth came into being, there has been human culture (renwen); as the fortunes of the age flow on, the two correspond as outer form and inner substance. The flourishing of the eras of Tang [Yao], Yu [Shun], and the Three Dynasties stood peerless indeed. From the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties onward, in times of prosperity literary culture was manifest and bright, whereas by the declining years of an era literary culture grew listless and decadent along with them. Was this not bound up with a failure at the time to fulfill completely the responsibility of succeeding in brilliance to illuminate the four quarters, and of observing cultural patterns so as to transform and perfect the realm?

Vast indeed was our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu, the Hongwu Emperor), who brought to completion the vital energies of the Three Luminaries and the Five Sacred Peaks, reviving this culture of ours so that it had the antiquity of the culture of Fuxi; at that time, human culture was gloriously restored in the Hongwu era (1368–1398). The Grand Ancestor, Emperor Wen (Taizong, the Yongle Emperor), elucidated the purport of the Five Classics and the Four Books, causing the great destiny of the dynasty to prosper and flourish, so that it had the brilliance of the culture of Sovereign Yao; …

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
時則人文大豐於永樂
列聖相承昭回制度舒廣
國華又如成周之文之郁郁焉
時則人文增益於宣德正統
之間我
皇上繼體守成厲志
經帷晉明道德垂衣
===
禮殿渙汗絲綸而尤惓惓於科
目得賢焉斯則繼明成化之
責豈不全備而無遺哉然臣
深念今四海之内人文日盛
則風氣日開風氣日開則俗
尚日侈其盛也汪洋俊逸或
有乖於理其開也流麗縱橫
punctuated: 時則人文大豐於永樂。列聖相承，昭回制度，舒廣國華，又如成周之文之郁郁焉；時則人文增益於宣德、正統之間。我皇上繼體守成，厲志經帷，晉明道德，垂衣禮殿，渙汗絲綸，而尤惓惓於科目得賢焉。斯則繼明成化之責，豈不全備而無遺哉！然臣深念今四海之内，人文日盛則風氣日開，風氣日開則俗尚日侈。其盛也，汪洋俊逸，或有乖於理；其開也，流麗縱橫，
translation_en: … At that time, cultural refinement flourished greatly during the Yongle era. The successive sacred emperors inherited the throne one after another, brilliantly illuminating the institutional systems and expanding the glory of the state, again like the rich and splendid culture of the accomplished Zhou dynasty; at that time, cultural refinement was further augmented during the Xuande and Zhengtong eras. Our Emperor has succeeded to the line and maintained the achievements of his predecessors, dedicating his will to the Classics mat-lectures, advancing and clarifying the Way and its virtue, governing with folded robes in the halls of ritual, and issuing imperial decrees like flowing sweat, while being especially earnest about obtaining worthy men through the examination system. In this, how could the responsibility of continuing the radiance and accomplishing transformation not be completely fulfilled without anything left out? Yet your servant deeply reflects that within the Four Seas today, as cultural refinement grows more flourishing by the day, intellectual trends become more open by the day; and as intellectual trends become more open by the day, popular fashions become more extravagant by the day. In its flourishing, writing is vast and spirited, yet at times deviates from principle; in its openness, it is flowing, ornate, and unrestrained, …

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
或有蕩於氣而其侈也言人
人殊遂并體製皆訛矣又况
士流學文惟初試是詳而餘
試或畧主司亦因而俯就焉
此古道之所由未復而今日
濟時之急務所當先者歟肆
臣等欽承
===
明詔懋圖救起以一之而雪其
鑑平其衡判妍媸輕重於毫
釐之際遍閱三試兼採所長
彼襲陳腐者文趣陋退之而
進其術業精明者焉好新竒
者文辭巧黜之而陟其志意
中和者焉習怪誕者文義野
punctuated: 或有蕩於氣；而其侈也，言人人殊，遂并體製皆訛矣。又况士流學文，惟初試是詳，而餘試或畧，主司亦因而俯就焉。此古道之所由未復，而今日濟時之急務所當先者歟！肆臣等欽承明詔，懋圖救起以一之。而雪其鑑，平其衡，判妍媸輕重於毫釐之際，遍閱三試，兼採所長。彼襲陳腐者，文趣陋，退之，而進其術業精明者焉；好新竒者，文辭巧，黜之，而陟其志意中和者焉；習怪誕者，文義野，
translation_en:
…sometimes allows their vital energy to run unchecked; and in its extravagance, everyone's words differ from everyone else's, until the very stylistic forms themselves have all become corrupted. Moreover, when scholars study composition, they pay close attention only to the first session of the examination and tend to neglect the remaining sessions, while the examiners in charge likewise lower their standards to accommodate them. Is this not the reason why the ancient Way has not yet been restored, and the urgent task for remedying the times that ought to be put first today?

Therefore, we, your servants, having reverently received the illustrious edict, have striven to rescue and revive literary standards so as to unify them. Wiping clean our mirror and leveling our balance, we judged beauty and ugliness, weight and lightness down to the finest hair's breadth, thoroughly reviewing all three examination sessions and drawing together the strengths of each. Those who merely repeated stale platitudes, whose literary purport was vulgar, we rejected, while advancing those whose scholarship and mastery were refined and clear; those who delighted in novelty and oddity, whose phrasing was merely clever, we dismissed, while promoting those whose aims and thoughts were balanced and harmonious; those who practiced the bizarre and preposterous, whose literary meaning was crude, …

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
奪之而予其態度端良者焉
趨庬雜者文格冗抑之而揚
其性情簡潔者焉慕麤豪者
文質散罰之而賞其制作謹
嚴者焉約而裁之俾規矩準
繩之不越無悖文之理也啓
而通之俾光芒勢焰之不沈
===
無晦文之氣也整而肅之俾
紀綱法度之不失無壞文之
體也若此者皆以救起人文
使無過不及之弊而一歸宿
於聖人之道之中惟如是則
今日之文參諸天地而無愧
驗諸
punctuated: 奪之，而予其態度端良者焉；趨庬雜者，文格冗，抑之，而揚其性情簡潔者焉；慕麤豪者，文質散，罰之，而賞其制作謹嚴者焉。約而裁之，俾規矩準繩之不越，無悖文之理也；啓而通之，俾光芒勢焰之不沈，無晦文之氣也；整而肅之，俾紀綱法度之不失，無壞文之體也。若此者，皆以救起人文，使無過不及之弊，而一歸宿於聖人之道之中。惟如是，則今日之文，參諸天地而無愧，驗諸
translation_en: … we denied them, and granted selection to those whose demeanor is upright and virtuous; as for those who pursue heterogeneity, whose literary structure is verbose, we suppressed them, and elevated those whose disposition is concise and pure; as for those who admire crudeness and bombast, whose literary substance is scattered, we penalized them, and rewarded those whose composition is careful and rigorous. We restrained and trimmed them so that the compass, square, level, and plumb line would not be transgressed, avoiding any violation of the principles of writing; we opened up and cleared the way for them so that their brilliance and momentum would not be submerged, avoiding any obscuring of the vitality of writing; we ordered and disciplined them so that guiding rules and legal measures would not be lost, avoiding any corruption of the form of writing. All of these measures are meant to rescue and revitalize literary culture, ensuring that there are no flaws of excess or deficiency, and bringing everything back to its proper resting place within the Way of the Sages. Only when it is thus can the writing of today stand alongside Heaven and Earth without shame, and be tested against…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
祖宗列聖而有光其於繼明普照
庶幾萬一之助而文明治化
之大成錐歷千萬世尚何遺
憾歟諸君子於此以文成名
獲膺眾舉行將試南宮對
大廷亦有位矣則凡所以弘文
明恭順之德上應於
===
重華協
帝之
君而履元吉者可不自勉乎必也
恒麗乎中務依乎正力體陽
道之剛而不牽制於陰道之
柔則
君臣同德克壽斯文於永久
punctuated: 祖宗列聖而有光，其於繼明普照，庶幾萬一之助，而文明治化之大成，錐歷千萬世，尚何遺憾歟！諸君子於此以文成名，獲膺眾舉，行將試南宮、對大廷，亦有位矣。則凡所以弘文明恭順之德，上應於重華協帝之君，而履元吉者，可不自勉乎！必也恒麗乎中，務依乎正，力體陽道之剛，而不牽制於陰道之柔，則君臣同德，克壽斯文於永久，
translation_en:
… the Ancestors and the succession of Sage Emperors with glory. In continuing the brightness that illuminates all, this may perhaps offer one ten-thousandth of a help; and in the great completion of civilized governance and transformation, even if it passes through ten million generations, what regret could remain!

Having achieved fame through literature here and won recommendation by the multitude, you gentlemen are about to be examined in the Southern Palace [Metropolitan Examination] and reply in the Great Court [Palace Examination], and so you too will hold office. Then, in all by which you broaden the virtues of cultured brightness and reverent compliance, responding above to a Sovereign of "double radiance in harmony with Di [Shun]" and treading the path of supreme auspiciousness—how could you not exert yourselves! You must constantly cleave to the mean, strive to rely on correctness, and vigorously embody the firmness of the Yang way without being hampered by the softness of the Yin way. Then Sovereign and minister will be of one virtue, able to give long life to This Culture in perpetuity; …

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
國家有無疆之休諸君子亦有
無窮之聞否則文浮於質或
并其質皆泯泯無足觀而日
流汙下焉斯則沒世無聞之
可疾假科目以患人之當咎
者其玷斯文庸有既乎敬書
此於錄元用考驗諸君子以
===
他日云
奉政大夫左春坊左庶子黎淳
謹序
punctuated:
國家有無疆之休，諸君子亦有無窮之聞。否則，文浮於質，或并其質皆泯泯無足觀，而日流汙下焉，斯則沒世無聞之可疾、假科目以患人之當咎者，其玷斯文庸有既乎？敬書此於錄元，用考驗諸君子以他日云。
奉政大夫、左春坊左庶子黎淳謹序。
translation_en:
… the state will enjoy boundless blessings, and you gentlemen will also achieve endless renown. Otherwise, if literary refinement exceeds substance, or if even the substance itself is utterly obliterated and unworthy of note, degenerating daily into baseness, then one will suffer the disgrace of dying with one's name unknown and bear the blame for using the examination system to bring harm to others—would there ever be an end to the blemish thus brought upon This Culture of Ours (siwen)? I respectfully write this at the head of the record in order to test and verify the conduct of you gentlemen in days to come.

Respectfully prefaced by Li Chun 黎淳, Grand Master for Governance (Fengzheng dafu), Left Mentor of the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent (Zuo chunfang zuo shuzi).

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
成化十年順天府鄉試
提調官
嘉議大夫順天府府尹邢簡〔居敬陜西咸寧縣人甲戌進士〕
中順大夫順天府府丞丁川〔大容浙江新昌縣人甲申進士〕
考試官
奉政大夫左春坊左庶子黎淳〔太樸湖廣華容縣人丁丑進士〕
翰林院修撰儒林郎劉健〔希賢河南洛陽縣人庚辰進士〕
同考試官
山東濟南府臨邑縣儒學教諭徐安〔志仁福建閩縣人庚午貢士〕
===
河南汝寧府光州固始縣儒學教諭章廣〔孝寛江西南昌縣人癸酉貢士〕
浙江温州府平陽縣儒學教諭陳奎〔文璧直隸寶應縣人己卯貢士〕
直隸安慶府桐城縣儒學教諭朱義〔仲宜浙江仁和縣人己卯貢士〕
湖廣武昌府興國州大冶縣儒學教諭顏廣烈〔士忠江西安福縣人戊子貢士〕
湖廣黄州府麻城縣儒學訓導朱謐〔元肅浙江會稽縣人丙子貢士〕
應天府儒學訓導賀深〔宗濬江西永新縣人壬午貢士〕
湖廣辰州府儒學訓導沈瓚〔廷器直隸崑山縣人壬午貢士〕

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
子曰參乎吾道一以貫之曾子曰唯
尊賢育才以彰有德
脩身則道立尊賢則不惑親親則諸父昆
弟不怨敬大臣則不眩體羣臣則士之
報禮重子庶民則百姓勸来百工則財
用足柔遠人則四方歸之懷諸侯則天
下畏之
===
易
乾道變化各正性命保合大和乃利
剛巽乎中正而志行柔皆順乎剛是以小
亨利有攸往利見大人
是故形而上者謂之道形而下者謂之器
易曰憧憧往来朋從爾思子曰天下何思
何慮天下同歸而殊塗一致而百慮天
下何思何慮日往則月来月往則日来
日月相推而明生焉寒往則暑来暑往
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

子曰：「參乎！吾道一以貫之。」曾子曰：「唯。」

尊賢育才，以彰有德。

脩身則道立，尊賢則不惑，親親則諸父昆弟不怨，敬大臣則不眩，體羣臣則士之報禮重，子庶民則百姓勸，来百工則財用足，柔遠人則四方歸之，懷諸侯則天下畏之。

易

乾道變化，各正性命，保合大和，乃利。

剛巽乎中正而志行，柔皆順乎剛，是以小亨，利有攸往，利見大人。

是故形而上者謂之道，形而下者謂之器。

《易》曰：「憧憧往来，朋從爾思。」子曰：「天下何思何慮？天下同歸而殊塗，一致而百慮。天下何思何慮？日往則月来，月往則日来，日月相推而明生焉。寒往則暑来，暑往
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said, "Zeng! My Way is threaded together by a single principle." Master Zeng said, "Yes."

"Honor the worthy and nurture the talented, so as to distinguish those who possess virtue."

"When one cultivates the person, the Way is established; when one honors the worthy, one is not perplexed; when one treats relatives with affection, the uncles and brothers bear no resentment; when one respects the great ministers, one is not confused in judgment; when one is considerate toward the whole body of officers, the scholars repay courtesy heavily; when one treats the common people as one's children, the hundred surnames are encouraged; when one attracts the hundred artisans, wealth and resources are sufficient; when one is gentle toward people from afar, the four quarters turn toward him; when one cherishes the feudal lords, the whole world stands in awe of him."

Book of Changes (Yi)

"As the Way of Qian transforms and changes, each thing rectifies its nature and destiny; preserving and uniting the great harmony, it is thus advantageous […]."

"The firm enters into centrality and correctness and its will is carried out; the yielding all follow the firm. Therefore there is small success; it is advantageous to have somewhere to go, and advantageous to see the great man."

"Therefore, what is above form is called the Way; what is below form is called a vessel."

"The Changes says: 'Unsettled in coming and going, only your friends follow your thoughts.' The Master said: 'What need has the world for thought and deliberation? In the world, all return to the same place though by different paths; all reach the same destination though through a hundred deliberations. What need has the world for thought and deliberation? The sun goes and the moon comes; the moon goes and the sun comes; sun and moon impel each other and light is born therefrom. Cold goes and heat comes; heat goes…'"

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
則寒來寒暑相推而歲成焉
書
簫韶九成鳳凰來儀夔曰於予擊石拊石
百獸率舞庶尹允諧帝庸作歌曰勅天
之命惟時惟幾
若金用汝作礪若濟巨川用汝作舟楫若
歲大旱用汝作霖雨
志以道寧言以道接不作無益害有益功
乃成不貴異物賤用物民乃足犬馬非
===
其土性不畜珍禽奇獸不育于國不寶
遠物則遠人格所寶惟賢則邇人安
罔不明德慎罰亦克用勸
詩
麟之趾振振公子于嗟麟兮麟之定振振
公姓于嗟麟兮麟之角振振公族于嗟
麟兮
朱芾斯皇室家君王
王命仲山甫式是百辟纘戎祖考王躬是
punctuated:
則寒來，寒暑相推而歲成焉。

《書》
《簫韶》九成，鳳凰來儀。夔曰：「於！予擊石拊石，百獸率舞，庶尹允諧。」帝庸作歌，曰：「勅天之命，惟時惟幾。」
若金，用汝作礪；若濟巨川，用汝作舟楫；若歲大旱，用汝作霖雨。
志以道寧，言以道接。不作無益害有益，功乃成；不貴異物賤用物，民乃足。犬馬非其土性不畜，珍禽奇獸不育于國。不寶遠物，則遠人格；所寶惟賢，則邇人安。
罔不明德慎罰，亦克用勸。

《詩》
麟之趾，振振公子，于嗟麟兮！麟之定，振振公姓，于嗟麟兮！麟之角，振振公族，于嗟麟兮！
朱芾斯皇，室家君王。
王命仲山甫，式是百辟，纘戎祖考，王躬是
translation_en:
… then the cold comes; cold and heat push each other on, and the year is completed thereby.

Book of Documents (Shu):
When the nine parts of the Xiaoshao music have been performed, the male and female phoenixes come to display their stately bearing. Kui said, "Oh! When I strike the sounding-stones and tap the sounding-stones, the hundred beasts lead one another on to dance, and all the chiefs of the officials become truly harmonious." The Emperor thereupon made a song, saying, "Attend carefully to the mandate of Heaven, at every moment and in the smallest things."

"Suppose me to be metal: I will use you as a whetstone. Suppose I am to cross a great stream: I will use you as a boat and oars. Suppose a year of great drought: I will use you as a copious rain."

"Keep your will at rest in the Way, and receive words according to the Way. Do not do what is unprofitable to the injury of what is profitable, and then your merit will be achieved. Do not value strange things to the contemning of useful things, and then the people will have a sufficiency. Dogs and horses that are not native to the soil, do not keep; precious birds and strange beasts, do not rear in the state. When you do not prize things from afar, people from afar will come to you; when what you prize is only the worthy, those who are near will be at peace."

"Make illustrious virtue and be cautious in punishments in every case, and thereby also manage to encourage the people."

Book of Odes (Shi):
The feet of the lin—the noble sons of our prince, ah, the lin! The forehead of the lin—the noble grandsons of our prince, ah, the lin! The horns of the lin—the noble kindred of our prince, ah, the lin!

His red kneecovers are resplendent—in the ancestral house a lord and king.

The king gave charge to Zhong Shanfu: "Be a model to all the princes; continue the work of your great ancestors; the king's own person do you …"

"Bright, bright is the Marquis of Lu, able to make bright his virtue. Having built the Pangong 泮宮 college, the Huai Yi 淮夷 tribes submit. text:

處父盟〔文公二年〕秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕晉侯伐秦
〔文公四年〕
禮記
凡三王教世子必以禮樂樂所以脩內也
禮所以脩外也禮樂交錯於中發形於
===
外是故其成也懌恭敬而溫文立太傅
少傅以養之欲其知父子君臣之道也
是故天時有生也地理有宜也人官有能
也物曲有利也
君在不佩玉左結佩右設佩居則設佩朝
則結佩齊則縼結佩而爵韠
人生而靜天之性也感於物而動性之欲
也
第貳場
punctuated:
宋世子佐、淮夷會于申。〔昭公四年〕
戊辰，諸侯盟于葵丘。〔僖公九年〕
晉人及姜戎敗秦于殽。晉人敗狄于箕。晉人、陳人、鄭人伐許。〔並僖公三十三年〕及晉處父盟。〔文公二年〕秦人伐晉。〔文公三年〕晉侯伐秦。〔文公四年〕
禮記
凡三王教世子，必以禮樂。樂所以脩內也，禮所以脩外也。禮樂交錯於中，發形於外，是故其成也懌，恭敬而溫文。立太傅、少傅以養之，欲其知父子、君臣之道也。
是故天時有生也，地理有宜也，人官有能也，物曲有利也。
君在，不佩玉。左結佩，右設佩。居則設佩，朝則結佩。齊則縼結佩而爵韠。
人生而靜，天之性也；感於物而動，性之欲也。
第貳場
translation_en:
…the Heir Apparent Zuo of Song, and the Huai Yi met at Shen. [4th year of Duke Zhao]
On the wuchen day, the feudal lords made a covenant at Kuiqiu. [9th year of Duke Xi]
The people of Jin and the Jiang Rong defeated Qin at Yao. The people of Jin defeated the Di at Ji. The people of Jin, the people of Chen, and the people of Zheng attacked Xu. [All in the 33rd year of Duke Xi] [The Duke] made a covenant with Chufu of Jin. [2nd year of Duke Wen] The people of Qin attacked Jin. [3rd year of Duke Wen] The Marquis of Jin attacked Qin. [4th year of Duke Wen]
Record of Rites (Liji)
Whenever the Three Kings instructed their heirs apparent, it was always by means of rites and music. Music is that by which the interior is cultivated; rites are that by which the exterior is cultivated. When rites and music interpenetrate within, they manifest themselves in the outward form; therefore, when a man's education is complete, he is harmonious and joyful, respectful, reverent, gentle, and refined. They established the Grand Mentor and the Junior Mentor to nurture him, desiring that he understand the way of father and son, ruler and minister.
Therefore, the seasons of heaven have their generative forces, the configurations of earth have their suitabilities, the offices of men have their capacities, and the diverse nature of things has its utilities.
While his ruler and father are alive, the son does not wear his jade pendants hanging loose. On the left he ties up the jades, and on the right he wears the practical appendages. In private retirement he wears the pendants loose; at court he ties them up. When fasting, he ties up the pendants with their cords and wears a dark-red knee-cover.
That man is still at birth is his Heaven-conferred nature; that he is moved when affected by external things is the desire of his nature.

問：古之言治者，至堯、舜極矣。然孟子論其道，乃曰「孝弟而已矣」。豈二帝之為君，外孝弟無餘道歟？堯、舜，人倫之至也；若禹、

Discourse:

Edict, Mandate, and Memorial [candidates select one]:

Third Session
Five Policy Questions:
Question: In antiquity, discussions of good governance reached their pinnacle with Yao 堯 and Shun 舜. Yet when Mencius (Mengzi 孟子) discussed their Way, he said it was "filial piety and fraternal duty, and that is all." Could it be that in ruling as sovereigns, the Two Emperors had no other Way beyond filial piety and fraternal duty? Yao and Shun were the perfection of human moral relationships; as for Yu 禹, …

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
湯文武之為君皆法堯舜者其道亦皆
止於孝弟歟聖人有身教有言教孝弟
乃身教之大者若言教則五經暨我
朝大誥三編為善陰隲孝順事實五倫書備
矣其言孝弟與孝弟兼備之人可槩舉
歟欽惟
皇上嗣登
大寶十年以来至孝尊
親上隆懽于
===
慈極彝倫惇叙下疏愛于
天潢其孝弟與堯舜同一致也引今天下之
民納諸唐虞之世將其道又復還隆古
而無爽焉矣然孝弟之外尚有所當従
事者歟夫致中和以極於天地位萬物
育隆禮于
上帝以至於鳳凰降龜龍假風雨節寒暑時正
心正朝廷以底於中國奠安四夷順服
皆當今時務尤急者亦惟孝弟是本歟
punctuated: 湯、文、武之為君，皆法堯、舜者，其道亦皆止於孝弟歟？聖人有身教、有言教，孝弟乃身教之大者；若言教，則《五經》暨我朝《大誥三編》、《為善陰隲》、《孝順事實》、《五倫書》備矣。其言孝弟與孝弟兼備之人，可槩舉歟？欽惟皇上嗣登大寶，十年以来，至孝尊親，上隆懽于慈極；彝倫惇叙，下疏愛于天潢。其孝弟與堯、舜同一致也。引今天下之民納諸唐、虞之世，將其道又復還隆古而無爽焉矣。然孝弟之外，尚有所當従事者歟？夫致中和以極於天地位、萬物育，隆禮于上帝以至於鳳凰降、龜龍假、風雨節、寒暑時，正心、正朝廷以底於中國奠安、四夷順服，皆當今時務尤急者，亦惟孝弟是本歟？
translation_en:
… Tang, Wen, and Wu as rulers all took Yao and Shun as their models—was their Way also limited solely to filial piety and fraternal respect? The sages taught through both personal example and spoken precepts. Filial piety and fraternal respect are the greatest aspects of teaching by personal example; as for teaching by spoken precepts, these are fully set forth in the Five Classics as well as our dynasty's Three Compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao sanbian), Secret Merit of Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi), True Records of Filial Piety and Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi), and Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu). Can you give a general account of their sayings on filial piety and fraternal respect, as well as the individuals recorded in them who embodied both virtues?

With reverence we reflect that since His Majesty succeeded to the Great Treasure ten years ago, with utmost filial devotion he has honored his parent, lavishing joy above upon the Empress Dowager; and by warmly ordering the constant human relationships, he has extended affection below throughout the imperial clan. His filial piety and fraternal respect are completely identical with those of Yao and Shun. Leading the people of the world today into an age like that of Tang and Yu [Yao and Shun], his Way is about to restore that of high antiquity without the slightest discrepancy. Yet beyond filial piety and fraternal respect, are there still other matters to which one ought to attend? To achieve equilibrium and harmony to the point where heaven and earth are in their proper places and the myriad things are nourished; to exalt the rites to the Lord on High so that phoenixes descend, tortoises and dragons appear, wind and rain are regulated, and cold and heat come in their proper seasons; and to rectify the mind and rectify the court so as to bring about the peaceful stabilization of the Central States and the obedient submission of the four border tribes—all of these are the most urgent affairs of the present day. Are they, too, rooted solely in filial piety and fraternal respect? …

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
諸士子強學待問必有能明之者試備
陳之
問理之在天下萬古一致不可易者也然
在堯舜禹曰執中在湯武曰建中建極
在孔子又曰一貫何言之不一歟孔子
承羣聖之統以淑人傳後門人若曾子
子貢既皆告以一貫矣何賢如顏子乃
不之告而但詳於答問仁之語歟孔門
以求仁為要既仁矣其於一貫之旨可
===
相入歟曾子一傳而子思之中庸以誠
為要再傳而孟子之七篇以性善養氣
為至何又不及仁與一貫歟周子奮起
孔孟絕學之後作太極圖以明是理圖
之說曰無極而太極曰中正仁義而主
靜其於孔孟之言有相契歟兩程子嘗
親受是圖於周子至其教門人乃毎以
敬言而未嘗一及是圖又何歟夫學能
會聖賢之言而一之此特知之事耳然
punctuated:
諸士子強學待問，必有能明之者，試備陳之。

問：理之在天下，萬古一致，不可易者也。然在堯、舜、禹曰「執中」，在湯、武曰「建中」、「建極」，在孔子又曰「一貫」，何言之不一歟？孔子承羣聖之統，以淑人傳後，門人若曾子、子貢，既皆告以「一貫」矣；何賢如顏子，乃不之告，而但詳於答問仁之語歟？孔門以求仁為要，既仁矣，其於「一貫」之旨可相入歟？曾子一傳而子思之《中庸》以誠為要，再傳而孟子之《七篇》以性善、養氣為至，何又不及仁與「一貫」歟？周子奮起孔、孟絕學之後，作《太極圖》以明是理。圖之說曰「無極而太極」，曰「中正仁義而主靜」，其於孔、孟之言有相契歟？兩程子嘗親受是圖於周子，至其教門人，乃毎以敬言，而未嘗一及是圖，又何歟？夫學能會聖賢之言而一之，此特知之事耳。然
translation_en:
You scholars have studied diligently and await questioning; surely there are those among you able to clarify these matters. Try to set them forth in full.

Question: Principle in the world is uniform across ten thousand ages and cannot be altered. Yet with Yao, Shun, and Yu it was called "holding fast the Mean"; with Tang and Wu it was called "establishing the Mean" and "establishing the Supreme Standard"; and with Confucius it was again called "one thread binding all together." Why was their wording not uniform? Confucius inherited the succession of the line of sages in order to cultivate people and transmit the Way to posterity. As for disciples such as Master Zeng (Zengzi 曾子) and Zigong 子貢, he told them both of the "one thread." Why, then, to one as worthy as Master Yan (Yanzi 顏子) did he not speak of it, instead elaborating only in his replies to questions about humaneness (ren 仁)? The school of Confucius took seeking humaneness as essential; once one is humane, can one enter into the purport of the "one thread"? In the first transmission from Master Zeng, Zisi's 子思 Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong 中庸) took sincerity as essential; in the second transmission, Master Meng's (Mengzi 孟子) Seven Chapters (Qipian 七篇) took the goodness of human nature and the nourishing of vital energy (qi 氣) as the ultimate. Why did they in turn not touch upon humaneness and the "one thread"? Master Zhou (Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤) rose up vigorously after the learning of Confucius and Mencius had been broken off, and composed the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji tu 太極圖) to elucidate this Principle. The Explanation of the Diagram says, "The Ultimateless and yet the Supreme Ultimate," and says, "Centrality, correctness, humaneness, and righteousness, while taking tranquility as fundamental." Does this tally with the words of Confucius and Mencius? The two Masters Cheng (Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤) once personally received this Diagram from Master Zhou, yet when it came to teaching their own disciples, they always spoke in terms of reverent seriousness (jing 敬) and never once mentioned this Diagram—why was that? Now, when learning is able to bring together the words of the sages and worthies and unify them, this is merely a matter of knowledge. Yet…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
猶有行焉必身心聖賢而思與之齊乃
其至也諸士子潜心義理有年於前所
謂聖賢之言必能會而一之矣其思齊
之工夫次第亦有可商確者歟朱子嘗
答吕伯恭書稱程子兩言雖約入德之
門無踰於此今可舉其言而明其旨歟
凡此皆知行之大學聖賢之學者門徑
之所必由不可以不之講也幸悉陳之
毋讓
===
問易道流行天地間至於泰則小往大來
吉且亨也人君治天下能遂其泰何幸
如之然聖人釋泰乃若有不自滿者既
謂無平不陂又慮陰皆失實何若是之
加懼歟豈以泰之為卦變二四則至於
豐可憂變上下則入於否不利聖人深
恤將来而預圖保之其設戒深矣惟九
二一爻乃人臣之正位上應六五之賢
君為得其中聖人於此立法以包荒用
punctuated:
猶有行焉，必身心聖賢，而思與之齊，乃其至也。諸士子潜心義理有年，於前所謂聖賢之言，必能會而一之矣；其思齊之工夫次第，亦有可商確者歟？朱子嘗答吕伯恭書，稱程子兩言雖約，入德之門無踰於此，今可舉其言而明其旨歟？凡此皆知行之大，學聖賢之學者門徑之所必由，不可以不之講也。幸悉陳之，毋讓。

問：易道流行天地間，至於泰，則小往大來，吉且亨也。人君治天下，能遂其泰，何幸如之！然聖人釋《泰》，乃若有不自滿者：既謂「無平不陂」，又慮「陰皆失實」，何若是之加懼歟？豈以《泰》之為卦，變二、四則至於《豐》可憂，變上下則入於《否》不利，聖人深恤將来而預圖保之，其設戒深矣。惟九二一爻，乃人臣之正位，上應六五之賢君，為得其中；聖人於此立法，以包荒、用
translation_en:
…there is still the matter of practice: only when one embodies the sages and worthies in body and mind, and strives to equal them, does one reach the ultimate. You scholars have immersed your minds in moral principles for years, and with regard to the teachings of the sages and worthies mentioned above, you must already be able to synthesize and unify them; as for the effort and sequence of striving to equal them, are there also points that can be discussed and settled? Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹], in a letter replying to Lü Bogong [Lü Zuqian 呂祖謙], once praised two sayings of Master Cheng, stating that although brief, no gateway to entering virtue surpasses them. Can you now cite those words and elucidate their meaning? All of these are the great essentials of knowledge and action, the pathway through which those who study to become sages and worthies must pass, and which cannot go unexamined. Please set them forth in full, without holding back.

Question: The Way of Changes flows between heaven and earth; when it reaches the hexagram Tai (Peace), the small departs and the great approaches, which is auspicious and prosperous. When a ruler governs the world and can achieve such peace, what fortune could compare to this! Yet when the Sage explained Tai, it was as if he remained unsatisfied: he both said "there is no plain not followed by a slope," and worried that "the yin lines have all lost their substance." Why did he show such heightened apprehension? Could it be because in the hexagram Tai, if the second and fourth lines change, it turns into Feng (Abundance), which is cause for worry, and if the upper and lower trigrams are inverted, it enters into Pi (Obstruction), which is unfavorable—so the Sage felt deep concern for the future and planned in advance to preserve it, thus setting down profound warnings? Only the Nine in the Second place is the proper position of a minister, corresponding above to the worthy ruler at the Six in the Fifth place, thereby attaining the mean. Here the Sage established a model, taking "embracing the uncultivated," "relying on…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
馮河不遐遺朋亡四者為治泰之道其
盡之歟夫包容荒穢妨乎奮發改革不
遺遐遠礙於不昵朋比四者豈相為用
歟方
今正泰寧之世也試舉一二切時之務請計
策焉夫世道久安則法度弛而習成誕
慢欺蔽矣驟然改之近患先起可不包
以大量乎然如賞功勳則官爵愈濫賑
災傷則財賦愈乏若此類當徧包歟人
===
情久逸則紀綱縱而下趨委靡陵替矣
恬然安之將来愈甚可不革以猛力乎
然如禦外侮或克捷罕聞去貪殘或反
訐貽累若此類當勇决歟眾志久寧則
變故少而無復深謀矣遠而慮之必周
庶事豈可遺遐遠乎然如恤兵民或畧
夫隱微用賢才或棄夫僻陋若此類當
普及歟時勢久順則人情肆而至於私
昵惡德矣約而正之必絕黨與豈可私
punctuated: 馮河、不遐遺、朋亡四者，為治泰之道，其盡之歟？夫包容荒穢，妨乎奮發改革；不遺遐遠，礙於不昵朋比。四者豈相為用歟？方今正泰寧之世也，試舉一二切時之務，請計策焉。夫世道久安，則法度弛而習成誕慢欺蔽矣；驟然改之，近患先起，可不包以大量乎？然如賞功勳，則官爵愈濫；賑災傷，則財賦愈乏。若此類，當徧包歟？人情久逸，則紀綱縱而下趨委靡陵替矣；恬然安之，將来愈甚，可不革以猛力乎？然如禦外侮，或克捷罕聞；去貪殘，或反訐貽累。若此類，當勇决歟？眾志久寧，則變故少而無復深謀矣；遠而慮之，必周庶事，豈可遺遐遠乎？然如恤兵民，或畧夫隱微；用賢才，或棄夫僻陋。若此類，當普及歟？時勢久順，則人情肆而至於私昵惡德矣；約而正之，必絕黨與，豈可私…
translation_en:
… "fording the river without a boat," "not neglecting the distant," and "losing one's朋 [factional companions]"—do these four serve as the complete way of governing in a time of Great Peace (Tai)? Now, tolerating what is wild and impure hinders vigorous reform, while not neglecting the distant gets in the way of not being partial to factional associates. How can these four work complementarily with one another?

At present, we are right in an era of peace and tranquility. Let us raise one or two urgent matters of the day and ask for your policy plans regarding them. When the ways of the world have long been peaceful, laws and regulations slacken, and habits of arrogance, negligence, deception, and concealment take shape. If one abruptly alters them, immediate troubles will arise first; how could one not tolerate them with great magnanimity? Yet, for example, in rewarding meritorious service, official ranks become ever more lavishly bestowed; in relieving disasters and famine, revenues and finances become ever more depleted. In cases of this kind, ought we to tolerate everything across the board?

When human sentiments have long enjoyed ease, discipline and order loosen, and those below sink into listlessness and decline. If one complacently rests in this, it will grow even worse in the future; how could one not reform it with vigorous force? Yet, for example, in repelling foreign aggression, victories are seldom heard of; in removing the greedy and cruel, they sometimes counter-accuse and bring trouble upon others. In cases of this kind, ought we to act with bold decisiveness?

When the minds of the multitude have long been tranquil, crises are few and there are no longer any deep plans. To take long-range thought, one must attend comprehensively to all affairs; how could one neglect what is distant? Yet, for example, in showing compassion to soldiers and civilians, the hidden and lowly are sometimes overlooked; in employing worthy talents, those in remote and humble places are sometimes cast aside. In cases of this kind, ought we to extend our reach universally?

When the trend of the times has long been favorable, human inclinations grow unbridled to the point of private partiality and wicked conduct. To restrain and rectify them, one must cut off factional cliques; how could one privately…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
朋比乎然如禁奢侈則害於近戚限田
產則妨於貴家若此類當斷行歟包荒
者仁之量馮河者義之勇不遐遺者智
之周不朋比者禮之節諸士子盡輸誠
直而悉言之斯誠吾
君吾相所喜聞而樂從者也
問學莫大於復性性學不可以不講也孔
子曰性相近而孟子曰性善孔孟之言
何以不同歟且孟子道性善先儒以為
===
擴前聖所未發然亦有所本歟性善之
㫖宜足以破百代之惑何以猶有性惡
善惡混及三品之誤至張程之說出而
始定歟大抵古今論性者其說有二曰
天地之性曰氣質之性天地之性直指
性之本體盖專以理言固不待於辯說
矣而氣質之說則不能無可疑也先儒
謂氣質之稟或不能齊解之者曰氣有
清濁質有美惡然氣之與質何以别而
punctuated:
朋比乎？然如禁奢侈則害於近戚，限田產則妨於貴家，若此類當斷行歟？包荒者，仁之量；馮河者，義之勇；不遐遺者，智之周；不朋比者，禮之節。諸士子盡輸誠直而悉言之，斯誠吾君吾相所喜聞而樂從者也。
問：學莫大於復性，性學不可以不講也。孔子曰「性相近」，而孟子曰「性善」，孔、孟之言何以不同歟？且孟子道性善，先儒以為擴前聖所未發，然亦有所本歟？性善之㫖，宜足以破百代之惑，何以猶有性惡、善惡混及三品之誤，至張、程之說出而始定歟？大抵古今論性者，其說有二：曰天地之性，曰氣質之性。天地之性，直指性之本體，盖專以理言，固不待於辯說矣；而氣質之說，則不能無可疑也。先儒謂氣質之稟或不能齊，解之者曰「氣有清濁，質有美惡」，然氣之與質何以别？而
translation_en:
…in factional collusion? Yet, if curbing extravagance harms close imperial relatives, or limiting landholdings impedes noble families, should measures of this sort be carried out decisively? "Embracing the untamed" (baohuang) is the magnanimity of humaneness; "fording the river without a boat" (pinghe) is the courage of righteousness; "not neglecting the distant" (bu xiayi) is the thoroughness of wisdom; and "not engaging in factional collusion" (bu pengbi) is the restraint of ritual propriety. Let all you scholars pour forth your sincere and forthright views and state them in full; this is truly what our Sovereign and our ministers will be glad to hear and happy to follow.

Question: In learning, nothing is greater than returning to one's original nature; the study of human nature cannot go unexamined. Confucius said, "By nature, men are nearly alike," whereas Mencius said, "Human nature is good." Why do the words of Confucius and Mencius differ? Moreover, when Mencius spoke of the goodness of human nature, former Confucians held that he expanded upon what earlier sages had left unexpressed; yet did his teaching also have a basis in earlier tradition? The doctrine of the goodness of human nature ought to have sufficed to dispel the doubts of a hundred generations; why, then, were there still the errors that human nature is evil, that good and evil are mixed within it, and that it falls into three grades, until the theories of Zhang Zai 張載 and the Cheng brothers 程顥、程頤 appeared and the matter was finally settled? Generally speaking, among those who have discussed human nature in ancient and modern times, there are two doctrines: one is called the "nature of Heaven and Earth," and the other is called the "nature of psychophysical endowment" (qizhi zhi xing). The "nature of Heaven and Earth" points directly to the original substance of human nature; since it speaks exclusively in terms of principle (li), it certainly requires no further debate or explanation. Yet the doctrine of psychophysical endowment cannot be altogether free of doubt. Former Confucians stated that psychophysical endowments cannot be uniform, and commentators have explained this by saying, "Vital force (qi) is either clear or turbid, and physical substance (zhi) is either fine or coarse." How, then, is vital force to be distinguished from physical substance, and…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
清濁美惡之說何以相配歟近世儒者
有謂受氣於父之時有清有濁成質於
母之時有美有惡其果確論歟先儒又
謂理只是善氣却有惡以為性本善之
證夫理氣非二物也以分善惡則岐而
為二矣何以見其合一之妙歟蔡西山
主張氣質太過其意以為理終抝氣不
轉而陳了翁又謂氣質之用狹道學之
功大朱子兩不以為然其論果安定歟
===
諸士子窮理修身以聖賢為歸此而不
知則冥行矣願明辨之毋諉曰性與天
道不可得而聞也
問衆言淆亂折諸聖故孟子語夷惠斷以
孔子後之作史者胡不折衷以聖人之
言使自定歟夫春秋尊君父如褒會首
止正儲鮇躋僖公逆祀敢干紀乎然若
漢安帝嗣殤帝乃禰和帝周世宗父柴
氏乃禰郭威宋濮安懿王或稱皇親或
punctuated:
清濁美惡之說何以相配歟？近世儒者有謂受氣於父之時有清有濁，成質於母之時有美有惡，其果確論歟？先儒又謂理只是善，氣却有惡，以為性本善之證。夫理氣非二物也，以分善惡，則岐而為二矣，何以見其合一之妙歟？蔡西山主張氣質太過，其意以為理終抝氣不轉；而陳了翁又謂氣質之用狹，道學之功大。朱子兩不以為然，其論果安定歟？諸士子窮理修身，以聖賢為歸，此而不知，則冥行矣。願明辨之，毋諉曰「性與天道不可得而聞也」。
問：衆言淆亂，折諸聖。故孟子語夷、惠，斷以孔子。後之作史者，胡不折衷以聖人之言，使自定歟？夫《春秋》尊君父，如褒會首止正儲，鮇躋僖公逆祀，敢干紀乎？然若漢安帝嗣殤帝，乃禰和帝；周世宗父柴氏，乃禰郭威；宋濮安懿王或稱皇親，或
translation_en:
…and how do the theories of purity and turbidity, beauty and ugliness correspond to them? Some recent scholars have claimed that when one receives vital energy (qi) from the father, it is either pure or turbid, and when one's physical substance (zhi) is formed in the mother, it is either fine or coarse—is this truly an indisputable argument? Earlier scholars also stated that principle (li) is purely good, whereas vital energy (qi) involves evil, taking this as proof that human nature is originally good. Now, principle and vital energy are not two separate things; if we divide them according to good and evil, they diverge into two—how then can we perceive the subtlety of their unity? Cai Xishan (Cai Yuanding 蔡元定) overemphasized the physical endowment (qizhi), maintaining that principle ultimately cannot bend or transform vital energy; whereas Chen Liaoweng (Chen Guan 陳瓘) argued that the function of physical endowment is narrow while the efficacy of the Learning of the Way (daoxue) is great. Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹) disagreed with both of them; where then does the settled conclusion actually lie? You gentlemen investigate principle and cultivate yourselves, taking the sages and worthies as your ultimate standard; if you do not understand this, you will be walking in the dark. I hope you will clearly distinguish these matters, and not excuse yourselves by saying, "The Master's discourses on human nature and the Way of Heaven cannot be heard."

Question: When myriad words are confused and disorderly, one turns to the sages for judgment. Thus, when Mencius spoke of Bo Yi 伯夷 and Liuxia Hui 柳下惠, he decided the matter by appealing to Confucius. Why did later historians not find the just mean by consulting the words of the sages so that matters might be settled of themselves? Now, the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) honors the ruler and father: for instance, it praised the meeting at Shouzhi for rectifying the position of the heir apparent, and disparaged [?] the elevation of Duke Xi 僖公 as a reversal of the sacrificial order—how could anyone dare to violate the cardinal norms? Yet in cases such as Emperor An of Han 漢安帝 succeeding Emperor Shang 殤帝 but enshrining Emperor He 和帝 in the father's temple (ni 禰); or Emperor Shizong of Zhou 周世宗, whose biological father was of the Chai 柴 clan, enshrining Guo Wei 郭威 in the father's temple; or Prince Anyi of Pu 濮安懿王 in the Song dynasty, who was variably proposed to be addressed as "Imperial Relative" or…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
稱皇伯其確論何存春秋定臣子如誅
國夏圍戚罪莒人滅鄫敢瀆倫乎然若
張留侯本為韓後乃仕漢魏武帝本夏
侯氏後乃姓曹范魯公本臣周後乃臣
宋其定說何在春秋賞有功如嘉子突
救衛與蕭魚賞魏絳豈容心乎然若陳
湯康居之捷或非其构難李德裕維城
之績或拒其失信李重進殉周之心或
責其異志其常法何從春秋罰有罪如
===
貶宰咺歸賵許晋侯執曹伯豈加意乎
然若薄昭戕使之討或病其傷恩荀彧
諫魏之戮或譬之教盜王安石新法之
禍或原其有激其斷例何適春秋明王
霸如抑楚丘專封美葵丘明禁敢混真
乎然若漢宣帝雜霸唐太宗假仁宋太
祖心合堯舜均為未純王道其微旨何
居春秋辨夷夏如譏會戎于潛惡會楚
于齊敢越等乎然若趙武靈用夷變夏
punctuated: 稱皇伯，其確論何存？《春秋》定臣子，如誅國夏圍戚，罪莒人滅鄫，敢瀆倫乎？然若張留侯本為韓後乃仕漢，魏武帝本夏侯氏後乃姓曹，范魯公本臣周後乃臣宋，其定說何在？《春秋》賞有功，如嘉子突救衛，與蕭魚賞魏絳，豈容心乎？然若陳湯康居之捷或非其构難，李德裕維城之績或拒其失信，李重進殉周之心或責其異志，其常法何從？《春秋》罰有罪，如貶宰咺歸賵，許晋侯執曹伯，豈加意乎？然若薄昭戕使之討或病其傷恩，荀彧諫魏之戮或譬之教盜，王安石新法之禍或原其有激，其斷例何適？《春秋》明王霸，如抑楚丘專封，美葵丘明禁，敢混真乎？然若漢宣帝雜霸，唐太宗假仁，宋太祖心合堯舜，均為未純王道，其微旨何居？《春秋》辨夷夏，如譏會戎于潛，惡會楚于齊，敢越等乎？然若趙武靈用夷變夏，
translation_en: … referring to him as Imperial Uncle—where does the definitive judgment lie? The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) fixes the roles of subjects and sons: for instance, in condemning Guo Xia for besieging Qi and blaming the men of Ju for extinguishing Zeng, would it dare to profane human moral relations? Yet in cases such as Zhang, Marquis of Liu (Zhang Liang 張良), who was originally a descendant of Han but later served the Han dynasty; Emperor Wu of Wei (Cao Cao 曹操), who was originally of the Xiahou clan but later took the surname Cao; and Fan, Duke of Lu (Fan Zhi 范質), who was originally a subject of the Later Zhou but afterward served as a subject of the Song—where does the settled explanation lie? The Spring and Autumn Annals rewards the meritorious: for instance, in commending Zitu for rescuing Wei and approving the rewarding of Wei Jiang after the covenant at Xiaoyu, how could it harbor any private bias? Yet in cases such as Chen Tang's 陳湯 victory in Kangju, where some criticized him for stirring up trouble; Li Deyu's 李德裕 achievement at Weicheng (Weizhou), where some rejected it to avoid breaking faith; and Li Chongjin's 李重進 heart set on dying as a martyr for the Later Zhou, where some reproached him for harboring treasonous intent—what constant standard is to be followed? The Spring and Autumn Annals punishes the guilty: for instance, in censuring Administrator Xuan (Zai Xuan 宰咺) for bringing funerary gifts and approving the Marquis of Jin's seizure of the Earl of Cao, how could it impose arbitrary personal intent? Yet in cases such as the execution of Bo Zhao 薄昭 for murdering an envoy, which some faulted for injuring imperial grace; the death of Xun Yu 荀彧 for remonstrating against Wei, which some likened to teaching a robber; and the calamities of Wang Anshi's 王安石 New Policies, which some excused as having been provoked by circumstances—which precedent for judgment should be adopted? The Spring and Autumn Annals clarifies the distinction between the true king and the hegemon: for instance, in curbing the unauthorized enfeoffment at Chuqiu and praising the clear prohibitions of the covenant at Kuiqiu, would it dare to confound the genuine with the false? Yet in cases such as Emperor Xuan of Han mixing in the ways of the hegemon, Emperor Taizong of Tang feigning benevolence, and Emperor Taizu of Song whose mind accorded with Yao and Shun, all of whom are nonetheless regarded as not having attained the pure Kingly Way—wherein does the subtle purport reside? The Spring and Autumn Annals distinguishes between barbarian (Yi) and Chinese (Xia): for instance, in ridiculing the meeting with the Rong at Qian and detesting the meeting with Chu in Qi, would it dare to transgress the proper grades? Yet in cases such as King Wuling of Zhao (Zhao Wuling 趙武靈) using barbarian ways to transform the Chinese, …

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
魏孝文用夏變夷元世祖威行朔漠均
為夷狄之盛其要義何述斯皆主司所
素疑者請諸士子發至當歸一之論幸
毋泛及之而不言也
punctuated: 魏孝文用夏變夷，元世祖威行朔漠，均為夷狄之盛，其要義何述？斯皆主司所素疑者，請諸士子發至當歸一之論，幸毋泛及之而不言也。
translation_en: … Emperor Xiaowen of Wei (魏孝文) used Chinese ways to transform the barbarians, and Emperor Shizu of Yuan (元世祖, Khubilai Khan) extended his authority across the northern desert; all represent the flourishing of barbarian peoples—how should the essential principles regarding them be stated? These are all matters about which the examiners have long harbored doubts. We ask you gentlemen to set forth definitive and unified arguments, and hope that you will not merely touch upon them superficially without speaking to the point.

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人一百三十五名
第一名馬中錫直隸故城縣學生易
第二名方晟燕山前衛舍人書
第三名王敏萬全都司學軍生詩
第四名萬盛順天府學生春秋
第五名吳裕順天府學生禮記
第六□郭維藩直隸開州學生詩
第七□魏琮直隸遷安縣人監生書
===
第八□王琚太醫院醫士易
第九□曾韜直隸山海衛學軍生春秋
第十名張達順天府學增廣生禮記

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
四書義
子曰參乎吾道一以貫之曾子曰唯
王琚
同考試官訓導賀批連日閱卷能以一心貫萬
事融會成文者絕少惟此作深得聖賢傳授之旨是宜錄出
同考試官教諭朱批以一心貫萬事講聖人之道
理到者之言也非他卷所及
考試官修撰劉批會傳註之意為文非素有講
貫者不及此
===
考試官左庶子黎批一貫是聖人之心一理渾然後
容中道舊作皆以為一本萬殊不過泛論其理耳似乎不切刋
此篇使學者用心於傳註
聖人傳道原於一心之妙大賢契道應以一言
之速夫聖人之道以一心而貫萬事也大賢求
之事而未會諸心久矣其承聖傳也得不即應
以一言之速也哉昔吾夫子以曾子學將有得
一旦呼其名而告之若曰吾之所謂道者豈有
待於外哉盖吾之一心粹然是理之純全渾然
punctuated:
四書義

「子曰：『參乎！吾道一以貫之。』曾子曰：『唯。』」

王琚

同考試官訓導賀批：連日閱卷，能以一心貫萬事融會成文者絕少，惟此作深得聖賢傳授之旨，是宜錄出。

同考試官教諭朱批：以一心貫萬事講聖人之道，理到者之言也，非他卷所及。

考試官修撰劉批：會傳註之意為文，非素有講貫者不及此。

考試官左庶子黎批：一貫是聖人之心，一理渾然，後容中道。舊作皆以為一本萬殊，不過泛論其理耳，似乎不切。刋此篇，使學者用心於傳註。

聖人傳道，原於一心之妙；大賢契道，應以一言之速。夫聖人之道，以一心而貫萬事也。大賢求之事而未會諸心久矣，其承聖傳也，得不即應以一言之速也哉？昔吾夫子以曾子學將有得，一旦呼其名而告之，若曰：「吾之所謂道者，豈有待於外哉？盖吾之一心，粹然是理之純全，渾然
translation_en:
Expositions on the Four Books

"The Master said, 'Shen! My Way has one thread that runs right through it.' Master Zeng said, 'Yes.'"

Wang Ju 王琚

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor He 賀: In several days of reading papers, those able to synthesize the idea of a single mind running through ten thousand affairs into an essay have been exceedingly rare. Only this piece deeply grasps the purport of the transmission between sage and worthy; it is fitting that it be selected for publication.

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhu 朱: Explaining the Way of the sage in terms of a single mind running through ten thousand affairs—these are the words of one who has thoroughly arrived at principle, not something that other papers can match.

Comment by Examiner and Senior Compiler Liu 劉: Composing the essay by grasping the meaning of the commentary and notes—one who did not habitually study and master them thoroughly could not achieve this.

Comment by Examiner and Left Mentor Li 黎: "One thread running through" refers to the mind of the sage, in which a single principle is seamlessly whole, effortlessly hitting the Mean [reading 後容 as 從容]. Older compositions have all treated it as "one root and ten thousand manifestations," which is nothing more than a generalized discussion of its principle and seems somewhat imprecise. Publishing this essay will cause scholars to apply their minds carefully to the commentary and notes.

When the sage transmits the Way, it originates in the subtlety of a single mind; when the great worthy apprehends the Way, he responds with the swiftness of a single word. Now, the Way of the sage is to run through ten thousand affairs with a single mind. The great worthy had sought it in affairs without yet grasping it in his mind for a long time; upon receiving the sage's transmission, how could he not immediately respond with the swiftness of a single word? In the past, seeing that Master Zeng 曾子 was about to attain understanding in his learning, our Master one day called him by his personal name and told him, as if to say: "How could what I call the Way depend upon anything external? For my single mind is purely the unadulterated completeness of this principle, and seamlessly…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
是理之昭徹彼事之至也雖萬變吾惟此心以
貫之而其用自無不當豈事事布置之耶物之
来也雖萬殊吾惟此心以通之而其施自無不
宜豈物物雕刻之耶夫心之一萬殊一本道之
體也事物之貫一本萬殊道之用也曾子於其
用處盖已隨事精察而力行之但未知其體之
一耳是以聞夫子一貫之傳而即有一唯之應
焉盖謂之唯者應之速而無疑也吾想曾子於
是脫然有悟而一原春融豁然貫通而萬理氷
===
釋矣尚何纎芥之疑貳留滯于念慮哉雖然夫
子既以一貫告曾子矣而曾子之告門人乃以
忠恕忠恕學者事耳何以言聖道哉盖忠恕有
動以天者有動以人者動以天則忠者誠恕者
仁是即一貫之道動以人乃學者事然亦違道
不遠也曾子於俄然問答之頃能易一貫以忠
恕則其實有得乎聖道之傳也亦可以驗矣
尊賢育才以彰有德
魏琮
punctuated:
是理之昭徹。彼事之至也，雖萬變，吾惟此心以貫之，而其用自無不當，豈事事布置之耶？物之来也，雖萬殊，吾惟此心以通之，而其施自無不宜，豈物物雕刻之耶？」夫心之一，萬殊一本，道之體也；事物之貫，一本萬殊，道之用也。曾子於其用處，盖已隨事精察而力行之，但未知其體之一耳。是以聞夫子一貫之傳，而即有一唯之應焉。盖謂之唯者，應之速而無疑也。吾想曾子於是脫然有悟，而一原春融，豁然貫通，而萬理氷釋矣，尚何纎芥之疑貳留滯于念慮哉？雖然，夫子既以一貫告曾子矣，而曾子之告門人乃以忠恕。忠恕，學者事耳，何以言聖道哉？盖忠恕有動以天者，有動以人者。動以天，則忠者誠，恕者仁，是即一貫之道；動以人，乃學者事，然亦違道不遠也。曾子於俄然問答之頃，能易一貫以忠恕，則其實有得乎聖道之傳也，亦可以驗矣。

尊賢育才，以彰有德。
魏琮
translation_en:
…illuminated by this principle. When affairs arrive, though they change in ten thousand ways, I thread them together solely with this mind, and its functioning naturally lacks nothing appropriate—how could one arrange each and every affair separately? When things come, though they differ in ten thousand ways, I comprehend them solely with this mind, and its application naturally lacks nothing fitting—how could one carve and polish each and every thing separately?" Now, the oneness of the mind—ten thousand differences归ing to one root—is the substance of the Way; the threading together of affairs and things—one root branching into ten thousand differences—is the function of the Way. Regarding its function, Master Zeng (Zengzi 曾子) had indeed already closely examined each affair as it arose and strenuously practiced it, yet he simply did not know the oneness of its substance. Therefore, upon hearing the Master's transmission of the single thread, he immediately responded with a "Yes!" What is meant by "Yes!" (wei 唯) is responding quickly and without doubt. I imagine that at this moment Master Zeng was suddenly awakened, the single source melting like spring, and with a wide-open breakthrough, the ten thousand principles dissolved like ice—what slightest doubt or hesitation could still linger in his thoughts? Even so, after the Master had told Master Zeng about the single thread, Master Zeng in turn explained it to his disciples in terms of conscientiousness and reciprocity (zhongshu 忠恕). Conscientiousness and reciprocity are merely the business of learners; how could they describe the Way of the Sage? This is because in conscientiousness and reciprocity, there is that which moves by Heaven and that which moves by man. Moving by Heaven, conscientiousness is sincerity and reciprocity is benevolence—this is none other than the Way of the single thread. Moving by man is indeed the business of learners, yet even so, it is not far from the Way. That Master Zeng, in the brief moment of a sudden question and answer, was able to substitute conscientiousness and reciprocity for the single thread also serves to verify that he had truly attained the transmission of the Sage's Way.

"Honor the worthy and nurture the talented, to give distinction to the virtuous."
Wei Cong 魏琮

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭陳批育才亞於尊賢先儒有定
說矣而塲中忽畧者多惟此作分析明白故用錄出
同考試官教諭章批塲中作此題者往往槩以育
才為彰有德殊失本㫖獨此卷析理詳明必有學之士也
考試官修撰劉批尊賢貴德五霸之盛此作發
明盡矣
考試官左庶子黎批此篇講彰有德處明白可以想
見桓公尊王之心
諸侯隆有德者以禮而養有能者以恩所以明
===
貴德之義也夫人之有德不可不貴之也然非
待人有等則德與才混而無別矣又何以貴德
而使人知勸哉葵丘以此為諸侯盟誓其亦深
為世道計歟嘅自姬轍旣東王綱解紐幸而齊
桓創霸上尊周室講會葵丘壹明天子之禁觀
其再命之辭若曰人之躬行仁義此有德者也
而多材多藝足以泛應非有才者乎凡我同盟
之人於有德者當尊之以位而信使益篤彼有
才者則育之而收儲待用焉人之心得禮智此
punctuated:
同考試官教諭陳批：育才亞於尊賢，先儒有定說矣，而塲中忽畧者多，惟此作分析明白，故用錄出。
同考試官教諭章批：塲中作此題者，往往槩以育才為彰有德，殊失本㫖。獨此卷析理詳明，必有學之士也。
考試官修撰劉批：尊賢貴德，五霸之盛，此作發明盡矣。
考試官左庶子黎批：此篇講彰有德處明白，可以想見桓公尊王之心。

諸侯隆有德者以禮，而養有能者以恩，所以明貴德之義也。夫人之有德，不可不貴之也。然非待人有等，則德與才混而無別矣，又何以貴德而使人知勸哉？葵丘以此為諸侯盟誓，其亦深為世道計歟！嘅自姬轍旣東，王綱解紐，幸而齊桓創霸，上尊周室，講會葵丘，壹明天子之禁。觀其再命之辭，若曰：人之躬行仁義，此有德者也；而多材多藝足以泛應，非有才者乎？凡我同盟之人，於有德者當尊之以位，而信使益篤；彼有才者則育之，而收儲待用焉。人之心得禮智，此
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Instructor Chen's comment: That nurturing talent is secondary to honoring the worthy is an established teaching of the former Confucians, yet many in the examination compound overlooked it. Only this composition analyzed the distinction clearly, and therefore it has been selected for inclusion.
Associate Examiner Instructor Zhang's comment: Those in the examination compound who wrote on this topic often indiscriminately treated "nurturing talent" as part of "giving distinction to the virtuous," which completely misses the original purport. This paper alone analyzes the principles with clarity and detail; its author must be a scholar of true learning.
Examiner Senior Compiler Liu's comment: Honoring the worthy and prizing virtue marked the height of the Five Hegemons. This composition has elucidated the theme in full.
Examiner Left Mentor Li's comment: This essay explains "giving distinction to the virtuous" with great clarity, allowing one to envision Duke Huan's devotion to honoring the King.

When the feudal lords exalt the virtuous with ritual propriety and nourish the capable with grace, it is in order to make clear the principle of prizing virtue. Now, when a man possesses virtue, he must not fail to be prized. Yet if men are not treated according to rank and degree, then virtue and talent become muddled and indistinguishable—how then could one prize virtue and make others know to be encouraged toward it? When the covenant at Kuiqiu made this an oath among the feudal lords, was it not taking deep thought for the state of the world? Alas, ever since the tracks of the Ji royal carriage moved east, the royal纲 (bonds of rule) came undone. Fortunately, Duke Huan of Qi established the hegemony, honoring the house of Zhou above and convening the assembly at Kuiqiu to uniformly proclaim the prohibitions of the Son of Heaven. Looking at the words of the second injunction, it is as though he said: When a person personally practices benevolence and righteousness, such a one possesses virtue; and when someone has many abilities and arts sufficient to respond broadly to affairs, is such a one not possessed of talent? All of us who join in this covenant ought, with regard to those who possess virtue, to honor them with high position and place ever deeper trust in them; as for those who possess talent, we should nurture them, gathering and storing them up to await employment. When a person's mind has attained propriety and wisdom, such a one…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
有德者也而有猷有為足以兼濟非有才者乎
凡我同盟之人於有德者當崇之以爵而眷顧
益厚彼有才者則養之而造就成器焉若此者
豈有他哉誠以才不可使勝於德也故差等其
重輕以顯明賢者之仁義使人知德在所當勸
如有商之宅俊均為國用然三宅已授職而三
俊猶儲材也其彰德也為何如藝不可使浮於
行也故辨別其高下以昭著賢者之禮智使人
知德在所當勉如成周之人才俱在官使然好
===
德者錫福而有猷者但念之也其彰德也又何
如桓公雖假仁者然所言猶有先王之遺意焉
此所以獨盛於五霸歟大抵葵丘五禁初命三
事皆脩身正家之要而四命言用人五命言睦
鄰無非格言也故三王有霸誠王道之不幸而
春秋有霸亦世道之猶幸孟子指五霸為三王
之罪人又以五霸律今之諸侯并及大夫焉其
所感深矣况使孟子得用當時吾見霸功盡黜
而王道大行也噫
punctuated: 有德者也，而有猷有為，足以兼濟，非有才者乎？凡我同盟之人，於有德者當崇之以爵，而眷顧益厚；彼有才者則養之，而造就成器焉。」若此者，豈有他哉？誠以才不可使勝於德也。故差等其重輕，以顯明賢者之仁義，使人知德在所當勸。如有商之宅俊，均為國用，然三宅已授職，而三俊猶儲材也，其彰德也為何如？藝不可使浮於行也。故辨別其高下，以昭著賢者之禮智，使人知德在所當勉。如成周之人才，俱在官使，然好德者錫福，而有猷者但念之也，其彰德也又何如？桓公雖假仁者，然所言猶有先王之遺意焉，此所以獨盛於五霸歟！大抵葵丘五禁，初命三事，皆脩身正家之要，而四命言用人，五命言睦鄰，無非格言也。故三王有霸，誠王道之不幸；而春秋有霸，亦世道之猶幸。孟子指五霸為三王之罪人，又以五霸律今之諸侯，并及大夫焉，其所感深矣。况使孟子得用當時，吾見霸功盡黜，而王道大行也。噫！
translation_en: …one who possesses virtue; whereas one who has plans and capabilities sufficient to benefit the world at large—is he not one who possesses talent? All of us who have joined in this covenant ought to exalt the virtuous with noble rank and show them ever deeper favor; as for those with talent, we should nurture them and mold them into useful vessels." Why did he speak like this? For no other reason than that talent truly must not be allowed to surpass virtue. Therefore, he graded their relative importance so as to make manifest the benevolence and righteousness of the worthy, letting people know that virtue is what ought to be encouraged. Just as under the Shang dynasty, those in the "three positions" (sanzhai) and those of the "three abilities" (sanjun) were alike employed by the state, yet the former were already granted office while the latter were still held in reserve as talent—how great was such a display of honoring virtue! Accomplishment in the arts must not be allowed to exceed moral conduct. Therefore, he distinguished their higher and lower ranks so as to make illustrious the propriety and wisdom of the worthy, letting people know that virtue is what ought to be striven after. Just as in the flourishing Zhou dynasty, men of talent were all employed in official service, yet those who loved virtue were bestowed with blessings while those who merely had plans were only kept in mind—how great, again, was such a display of honoring virtue! Although Duke Huan only borrowed the guise of benevolence, what he said still retained the lingering intent of the Former Kings. Is this not why he alone was the most flourishing among the Five Hegemons? In general, among the five injunctions at Kuiqiu, the three matters of the first injunction were all essentials of cultivating the person and regulating the family, while the fourth injunction spoke of employing men and the fifth spoke of maintaining harmony with neighboring states—none of these were anything less than exemplary maxims. Thus, that the era of the Three Kings was followed by Hegemons was truly a misfortune for the Kingly Way; yet that the Spring and Autumn period had Hegemons was still a fortunate thing for the state of the world. Mencius pointed to the Five Hegemons as offenders against the Three Kings, and then used the Five Hegemons as a standard to measure the feudal lords of his own day, extending it even to the grandees; how deep were the emotions that stirred him! How much more so, had Mencius gained employment in his own time, would we have seen the achievements of the Hegemons completely dismissed and the Kingly Way practiced on a grand scale! Alas!

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
脩身則道立尊賢則不惑親親則諸父昆
弟不怨敬大臣則不眩體羣臣則士之報
禮重子庶民則百姓勸来百工則財用足
柔遠人則四方歸之懷諸侯則天下畏之
馬中錫
同考試官訓導賀批場中作此題者不失之泛
則失之畧是篇以序而著其效詞達意足非老學不能及
同考試官教諭朱批序九經之效辭簡當而理
明快結本一誠尤見學力
===
考試官修撰劉批中庸義平正明白亦善作者
考試官左庶子黎批近時學者穿鑿如講此題多
背經傳好異使然耳是篇只平説去義理便了錄之為學
者法
中庸之論九經也必以序而著其效焉夫九經
固有其序也然不因其序而詳著其效何以見
其切於天下國家之治也哉此孔子答哀公之
言而中庸引之謂夫為治莫要於九經而九經
莫先於脩身有天下國家者齊明盛服非禮不
punctuated:
「脩身則道立，尊賢則不惑，親親則諸父昆弟不怨，敬大臣則不眩，體羣臣則士之報禮重，子庶民則百姓勸，来百工則財用足，柔遠人則四方歸之，懷諸侯則天下畏之。」
馬中錫
同考試官訓導賀批：場中作此題者，不失之泛則失之畧。是篇以序而著其效，詞達意足，非老學不能及。
同考試官教諭朱批：序九經之效，辭簡當而理明快，結本一誠，尤見學力。
考試官修撰劉批：《中庸》義平正明白，亦善作者。
考試官左庶子黎批：近時學者穿鑿，如講此題，多背經傳，好異使然耳。是篇只平説去，義理便了，錄之為學者法。
《中庸》之論九經也，必以序而著其效焉。夫九經固有其序也，然不因其序而詳著其效，何以見其切於天下國家之治也哉？此孔子答哀公之言，而《中庸》引之。謂夫為治莫要於九經，而九經莫先於脩身。有天下國家者，齊明盛服，非禮不
translation_en:
"By cultivating the person, the Way is established; by honoring the worthy, one is free from doubt; by showing affection to relatives, uncles and brothers bear no resentment; by respecting the great ministers, one does not go astray; by being considerate to the whole body of officers, scholars make a heavy return of courtesy; by treating the common people as one's children, the hundred surnames are encouraged; by attracting all classes of artisans, wealth and resources are made sufficient; by dealing gently with men from afar, the four quarters turn toward one; by cherishing the feudal lords, all under Heaven stand in awe of one."

Ma Zhongxi 馬中錫

Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor He 賀: Those in the examination hall who wrote on this topic erred either through vagueness or through sketchiness. This essay sets forth the effects according to their sequence; its language is expressive and its meaning full—something only a seasoned scholar could achieve.

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Zhu 朱: In setting forth the effects of the Nine Standard Rules, the language is concise and apt while the reasoning is clear and incisive. Grounding the conclusion in "a single sincerity" especially shows the depth of his scholarship.

Comment by Examiner Senior Compiler Liu 劉: An exposition on the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) that is balanced, straightforward, and lucid—truly the work of a skilled writer.

Comment by Examiner Left Mentor Li 黎: Scholars of recent times are given to forced interpretations; when expounding on a topic like this, they mostly go against the Classic and commentary, simply out of a fondness for novelty. This essay merely explains it plainly, and the moral principles become immediately clear. We record it as a model for scholars.

When the Doctrine of the Mean discusses the Nine Standard Rules (jiujing 九經), it necessarily sets forth their effects according to their sequence. Now, the Nine Standard Rules inherently have their sequence; yet if one does not follow that sequence to set forth their effects in detail, how could one see how vital they are to the governance of the Empire, the state, and the family? These were Confucius's words in reply to Duke Ai 哀公, quoted in the Doctrine of the Mean. They mean that in governing, nothing is more essential than the Nine Standard Rules, and among the Nine Standard Rules, nothing comes before cultivating the person. When one who possesses the Empire, the state, and the family maintains purity and brightness, wears ceremonial robes, and does not [move] contrary to ritual…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
動以修身則道成於已而可為民表然必親師
取友而後修身之道進去讒遠色賤貨貴德以
尊賢則道資於人而心無所疑道之所進莫先
其家尊位重禄同其好惡以親親則不拂其欲
而諸父昆弟不怨由家以及朝廷官盛任使以
優大臣則信任專而臨事不迷焉忠信重禄以
體羣臣則恩意洽而士之報禮重焉由朝廷以
及其國時使薄斂以子庶民則勸民之道盡而
民相勸矣日省月試以來百工則勸工之道盡
===
而用不乏矣由其國以及天下送往迎来嘉善
矜不能以柔遠人也而四方歸之興滅繼絕厚
往薄来以懷諸侯也而天下畏之吁道以序而
盡效以類而應有天下國家者為治之道無以
加此謂之經也宜矣抑是章前言達道達德卒
歸之誠此言九經亦卒歸之誠蓋誠者實而已
矣道德而非誠則為虛器九經而非誠則為虛
文誠之道有天下國家者可得而暫離哉子思
子此引孔子之言以繼大舜文武周公之緒明
punctuated: 動以修身，則道成於已而可為民表。然必親師取友，而後修身之道進。去讒遠色、賤貨貴德以尊賢，則道資於人而心無所疑。道之所進，莫先其家。尊位重禄、同其好惡以親親，則不拂其欲而諸父昆弟不怨。由家以及朝廷，官盛任使以優大臣，則信任專而臨事不迷焉；忠信重禄以體羣臣，則恩意洽而士之報禮重焉。由朝廷以及其國，時使薄斂以子庶民，則勸民之道盡而民相勸矣；日省月試以來百工，則勸工之道盡而用不乏矣。由其國以及天下，送往迎来、嘉善矜不能以柔遠人也，而四方歸之；興滅繼絕、厚往薄来以懷諸侯也，而天下畏之。吁！道以序而盡，效以類而應，有天下國家者為治之道無以加此，謂之經也宜矣。抑是章前言達道、達德，卒歸之誠；此言九經，亦卒歸之誠。蓋誠者，實而已矣。道德而非誠，則為虛器；九經而非誠，則為虛文。誠之道，有天下國家者可得而暫離哉？子思子此引孔子之言，以繼大舜、文、武、周公之緒，明
translation_en: …acting contrary to ritual in order to cultivate his personal life, the Way is perfected in himself and he can serve as a model for the people. Yet one must draw near to teachers and choose friends before the Way of cultivating the personal life can advance. By dismissing slanderers and keeping away from seductive beauty, despising wealth and prizing virtue in order to honor the worthy, one draws upon others for the Way and one's mind has no doubts. In advancing the Way, nothing comes before one's family. By exalting their rank, giving them generous emoluments, and sharing their likes and dislikes in order to be affectionate toward relatives, one does not thwart their desires, and one's uncles and brothers bear no resentment. From the family one extends this to the court: by providing abundant subordinate officers for their tasks in order to treat the great ministers generously, trust in them is專 [undivided] and one is not confused when facing affairs; by showing loyalty and good faith and giving generous emoluments in order to identify with the body of lesser officials, favor and goodwill are pervasive and the scholars repay courtesy heavily. From the court one extends this to the state: by employing them only at the proper seasons and making imposts light in order to treat the common people as one's children, the way of encouraging the people is fulfilled and the people encourage one another; by daily inspections and monthly tests in order to attract the百工 [hundred artisans], the way of encouraging artisans is fulfilled and resources for use are never lacking. From the state one extends this to all under Heaven: by escorting them on departure and welcoming them on arrival, commending the good and sympathizing with the incompetent in order to be gentle with men from afar, the four quarters turn to him in allegiance; by restoring extinguished states and continuing severed successions, giving generously when they depart and requiring little when they come in order to cherish the feudal lords, all under Heaven stand in awe of him. Ah! When the Way is fulfilled in its proper sequence, its effects respond according to their kind. For those who possess the Empire, states, and families, the Way of governing cannot surpass this; it is fitting indeed that they are called the standard rules. Moreover, earlier in this chapter, when speaking of the universal ways and universal virtues, it ultimately traces them back to sincerity; here, when speaking of the Nine Standard Rules, it also ultimately traces them back to sincerity. For sincerity is nothing other than reality. If the Way and virtue lack sincerity, they are empty vessels; if the Nine Standard Rules lack sincerity, they are empty words. Can those who possess the Empire, states, and families depart from the Way of sincerity even for a moment? Master Zisi 子思子 here quotes the words of Confucius 孔子 to continue the heritage of the Great Shun 大舜, King Wen 文, King Wu 武, and the Duke of Zhou 周公, making clear…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
其所傳之一致盖聖人之道固不外乎誠也先
儒云誠者聖人之本其信矣乎
易
乾道變化各正性命保合大和乃利貞
馬中錫
同考試官訓導賀批題本正大失旨者多此篇
以理乘氣立說筆力蒼古置之高選允協輿情
同考試官教諭朱批作此題者類多蹈襲惟是
篇化腐為新理足而辭達讀之令人起敬
===
考試官修撰劉批此題場中作者多雷同陳腐
可厭而此作獨能脫去是之取爾
考試官左庶子黎批作易義不可馳騁要融會義
理於心然後寫出此篇得之
天道流行萬物得其理而全其氣此乾之利貞
也夫天道之有流行理之乘乎氣也萬物得是
理於有生之初而全是氣於已生之後則乾之
利貞也于是乎可見矣何以言之天道之流行
也或自陽而趨于陰或自陰而趨于陽其趨也
punctuated:
其所傳之一致，盖聖人之道固不外乎誠也。先儒云：「誠者，聖人之本。」其信矣乎！

易

乾道變化，各正性命，保合大和，乃利貞。

馬中錫
同考試官訓導賀批：題本正大，失旨者多。此篇以理乘氣立說，筆力蒼古，置之高選，允協輿情。
同考試官教諭朱批：作此題者類多蹈襲，惟是篇化腐為新，理足而辭達，讀之令人起敬。
考試官修撰劉批：此題場中作者多雷同陳腐可厭，而此作獨能脫去，是之取爾。
考試官左庶子黎批：作《易》義不可馳騁，要融會義理於心，然後寫出，此篇得之。

天道流行，萬物得其理而全其氣，此乾之利貞也。夫天道之有流行，理之乘乎氣也。萬物得是理於有生之初，而全是氣於已生之後，則乾之利貞也，于是乎可見矣。何以言之？天道之流行也，或自陽而趨于陰，或自陰而趨于陽，其趨也，
translation_en:
… the unity of what was transmitted, for the Way of the Sages indeed does not lie outside of sincerity. A former Confucian scholar said, "Sincerity is the foundation of the Sage." How true that is!

Book of Changes (Yi)

"The Way of the Creative (Qian) alters and transforms, so that each thing receives its true nature and destiny; it preserves and unites the Great Harmony—thus is it advantageous and贞 [correct and firm]."

Ma Zhongxi 

Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor He: The topic is fundamentally upright and grand, yet many missed its purport. This essay establishes its argument on the basis of principle riding upon vital force (qi). Its brushwork is vigorous and antique; placing it in the high selections truly accords with public sentiment.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Zhu: Those who write on this topic mostly fall into plagiarism and imitation. Only this essay transforms the stale into the fresh; its reasoning is sufficient and its expression lucid. Reading it inspires respect.
Comment by Examiner Senior Compiler Liu: In the examination hall, most who wrote on this topic were tediously identical and stale, yet this composition alone managed to break free of that—for this reason it is selected.
Comment by Examiner Left Mentor Li: In composing essays on the meaning of the Changes, one must not give free rein to extravagant rhetoric; one must thoroughly fuse the moral principles in one's mind and only then write them out. This essay has achieved that.

As the Way of Heaven flows and operates, the myriad things obtain its principle and keep its vital force whole—this is the "advantageousness and firmness" (li zhen) of the Creative (Qian). Now, that the Way of Heaven flows and operates is principle riding upon vital force. When the myriad things obtain this principle at the beginning of their coming into life, and keep this vital force whole after they have come into life, the advantageousness and firmness of the Creative can thereby be seen. How may we explain this? In the flowing operation of the Way of Heaven, at times it proceeds from yang toward yin, and at times from yin toward yang. In its proceeding, …

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
必有所漸漸乃變也其變也必有所成成乃化
也一變一化流行不息則雖無心於生萬物而
萬物不能以不生矣是故就其有生之初言之
分雖有飛潛動植之殊也而所賦所受之理隨
處充滿無少欠缺此之謂各正性命焉性命以
理言而氣無不在生物之本也就其已生之後
言之質雖有洪纖高下之異也而會合冲和之
氣隨在完固無少滲漏此之謂保合大和焉大
和以氣言而理無不寓生物之具也夫天道流
===
行無所不利而萬物各得其性命以自全如此
則貞下起元生生不已矣豈非乾之利貞也哉
抑又論之卦辭之利貞文王直以為占辭耳孔
子於是乃以天道言之盖乾道純乎陽乾即天
也下文又以聖人之利貞言之盖聖人純乎天
聖人即乾也雖其文義有非文王之舊者然聖
人之蘊因卦以發固並行而不相悖也此學易
者之所當知
是故形而上者謂之道形而下者謂之器
punctuated:
必有所漸，漸乃變也；其變也，必有所成，成乃化也。一變一化，流行不息，則雖無心於生萬物，而萬物不能以不生矣。是故就其有生之初言之，分雖有飛潛動植之殊也，而所賦所受之理，隨處充滿，無少欠缺，此之謂「各正性命」焉。性命以理言，而氣無不在，生物之本也。就其已生之後言之，質雖有洪纖高下之異也，而會合冲和之氣，隨在完固，無少滲漏，此之謂「保合大和」焉。大和以氣言，而理無不寓，生物之具也。夫天道流行，無所不利，而萬物各得其性命以自全如此，則貞下起元，生生不已矣，豈非乾之利貞也哉！抑又論之，卦辭之「利貞」，文王直以為占辭耳，孔子於是乃以天道言之，盖乾道純乎陽，乾即天也。下文又以聖人之利貞言之，盖聖人純乎天，聖人即乾也。雖其文義有非文王之舊者，然聖人之蘊因卦以發，固並行而不相悖也。此學《易》者之所當知。

是故形而上者謂之道，形而下者謂之器。
translation_en:
…necessarily proceeds by degrees, and this gradual progression is change (bian); its change necessarily reaches completion, and this completion is transformation (hua). With each change and each transformation flowing on without cease, although Heaven has no deliberate intention to give life to the myriad things, the myriad things cannot but be brought to life. Therefore, speaking of the very beginning of their coming into life: although their allotments differ as flying, submerged, moving, or planted things, the principle (li) that is endowed and received is everywhere fully present without the slightest deficiency—this is what is meant by "each rectifying its nature and destiny." Nature and destiny are spoken of in terms of principle, yet vital force (qi) is never absent from them; this is the root of generating things. Speaking of the period after they have come into life: although their physical substances differ in being large or small, high or low, the blended and harmonious vital force is everywhere intact and firm without the slightest leakage—this is what is meant by "preserving in union the Great Harmony." The Great Harmony is spoken of in terms of vital force, yet principle never fails to reside within it; this is the instrument for generating things. Now, the Way of Heaven flows forth with nothing that is not advantageous, and the myriad things each obtain their nature and destiny so as to preserve themselves intact like this; thus, beneath firmness (zhen) arises origination (yuan), creating and recreating without end. Is this not the "advantageous and firm" (li zhen) quality of the Qian hexagram! Moreover, if we discuss it further: as for the "advantageous and firm" of the hexagram statement, King Wen simply took it as a divination formula. Here, however, Confucius spoke of it in terms of the Way of Heaven, because the Way of Qian is purely yang, and Qian is none other than Heaven. In the text below, he goes on to speak of it in terms of the sage's being advantageous and firm, because the sage is purely Heaven, and the sage is none other than Qian. Although the meaning of the text here is not the old sense of King Wen, nevertheless the sage's profound thought was brought forth by means of the hexagram, and the two certainly proceed side by side without contradicting each other. This is what students of the Book of Changes (Yi) ought to know.

"Therefore what is above form is called the Way (dao), and what is within form is called an implement (qi)."

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
馬中錫
同考試官訓導賀批道器不相離作者往往析
而二之貫串成文超出衆作僅見此篇
同考試官教諭朱批道器之所以分只在一形上下
之間有分別而不相離此作得之必精於易者非初學可到
考試官修撰劉批分析道器名義言簡而意明
盖有見之士也
考試官左庶子黎批道器非二物此篇體認真切
深於易者也
===
聖人即一形有無之別而示人道器之名夫有
形之中有無形之理寓焉聖人以是形是理而
離合別言之則道器之名豈不于是而可見哉
何則易之所有卦爻陰陽而已卦爻之竒偶陰
陽之動靜皆形也自是形而上言之竒實偶虛
必有所以實所以虛者以根柢是竒偶聲臭寂
然有非見聞之可及陽動陰靜必有所以動所
以靜者以樞紐是陰陽形迹泯然有非指陳之
可逮則謂之道焉自是形而下言之竒偶虛實
punctuated:
馬中錫
同考試官訓導賀批：道器不相離，作者往往析而二之。貫串成文，超出衆作，僅見此篇。
同考試官教諭朱批：道器之所以分，只在一形上下之間，有分別而不相離。此作得之，必精於《易》者，非初學可到。
考試官修撰劉批：分析道器名義，言簡而意明，盖有見之士也。
考試官左庶子黎批：道器非二物，此篇體認真切，深於《易》者也。
聖人即一形有無之別，而示人道器之名。夫有形之中，有無形之理寓焉。聖人以是形、是理而離合別言之，則道器之名，豈不于是而可見哉？何則？《易》之所有，卦爻陰陽而已。卦爻之竒偶，陰陽之動靜，皆形也。自是形而上言之：竒實偶虛，必有所以實、所以虛者以根柢是竒偶，聲臭寂然，有非見聞之可及；陽動陰靜，必有所以動、所以靜者以樞紐是陰陽，形迹泯然，有非指陳之可逮，則謂之道焉。自是形而下言之：竒偶虛實，
translation_en:
Ma Zhongxi 馬中錫

Comment by Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor He: The Way (dao 道) and concrete vessels (qi 器) are inseparable, yet writers often split them in two. Stringing them together into a coherent essay that surpasses the rest of the submissions—only this piece achieves it.

Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhu: That by which the Way and concrete vessels are distinguished lies solely between what is above and what is below a single form (xing 形): there is a distinction, yet they are not separate. This essay grasps it; the author must be well-versed in the Book of Changes (Yi 易)—this is not something a beginner could reach.

Comment by Examiner, Senior Compiler Liu: In analyzing the terms and meanings of the Way and concrete vessels, the language is concise and the meaning is clear. Truly, this is a scholar of insight.

Comment by Examiner, Left Mentor Li: The Way and concrete vessels are not two separate things. This essay's personal realization is genuine and keen; its author is profound in the Book of Changes.

Based on the distinction between the presence and absence of a single form, the Sage reveals to people the names of the Way and concrete vessels. Now, within that which has form, there resides formless principle (li 理). When the Sage speaks of this form and this principle in terms of their separation, union, and distinction, can the names of the Way and concrete vessels not thereby be seen? Why is this so? What the Book of Changes contains is nothing more than hexagrams, lines, yin, and yang. The odd and even of the hexagrams and lines, and the movement and stillness of yin and yang, are all forms. Speaking from what is above these forms: the odd is solid and the even is hollow, yet there must be that by which they are solid and that by which they are hollow to serve as the root and foundation of this odd and even—devoid of sound and odor, beyond the reach of sight and hearing; yang moves and yin is still, yet there must be that by which it moves and that by which it is still to serve as the pivot of this yin and yang—with all physical traces obliterated, beyond the reach of pointing out and setting forth; this is called the Way. Speaking from what is below these forms: the odd and even, the hollow and solid,…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
闔闢不已而諸卦剛柔之體以具聲臭皆可以
見聞矣陰陽動靜運行不息而萬物氣形之化
以成形迹皆可以指陳矣則謂之器焉吁道雖
無形也而實寓於有形之器器雖有形也而實
載乎無形之道是則道也器也可謂有分別而
不相離矣雖然大傳聖人於此既曰形而上者
謂之道而他章又曰一陰一陽之謂道陰陽氣
也而曰之謂道則似又涉乎有形矣噫此正道
之所以無形也蓋陰陽乃氣固有形矣道乃理
===
即其所以一陰而又一陽者也何嘗有形乎道
乗乎氣而神妙無方氣載乎道而變易無體此
古者聖人所以本之以作是易也歟
書
若金用汝作礪若濟巨川用汝作舟楫若
歲大旱用汝作霖雨
方晟
同考試官教諭陳批〔此題三節皆本納誨説場中作者間能知之而詞足以發其意者少此作意完文沛〕
punctuated:
闔闢不已，而諸卦剛柔之體以具，聲臭皆可以見聞矣；陰陽動靜，運行不息，而萬物氣形之化以成，形迹皆可以指陳矣，則謂之「器」焉。吁！道雖無形也，而實寓於有形之器；器雖有形也，而實載乎無形之道。是則道也、器也，可謂有分別而不相離矣。雖然，《大傳》聖人於此既曰「形而上者謂之道」，而他章又曰「一陰一陽之謂道」。陰陽，氣也，而曰「之謂道」，則似又涉乎有形矣。噫！此正道之所以無形也。蓋陰陽乃氣，固有形矣；道乃理，即其所以一陰而又一陽者也，何嘗有形乎？道乗乎氣而神妙無方，氣載乎道而變易無體，此古者聖人所以本之以作是《易》也歟！

《書》：
「若金，用汝作礪；若濟巨川，用汝作舟楫；若歲大旱，用汝作霖雨。」
方晟
同考試官教諭陳批：〔此題三節皆本納誨説，場中作者間能知之，而詞足以發其意者少。此作意完文沛，〕
translation_en:
… closing and opening without cease, so that the firm and yielding forms of the various hexagrams are thereby complete, and their sounds and scents can all be seen and heard; when yin and yang move and rest, revolving without pause, so that the transformations of vital force and physical form in the myriad things are thereby accomplished, and their forms and traces can all be pointed out and set forth—then this is called "vessel." Ah! Although the Way has no physical form, it truly resides within vessels that have form; although a vessel has physical form, it truly carries the formless Way. Thus, the Way and the vessel may be said to have a distinction and yet be inseparable from one another. Even so, in the Great Commentary (Dazhuan) the Sage says here, "What is above physical form is called the Way," yet in another chapter he also says, "One yin and one yang—this is called the Way." Yin and yang are vital force (qi); to say "this is called the Way" would seem once again to encroach upon what has physical form. Ah! This is precisely why the Way has no physical form. For yin and yang are vital force, and indeed have form; the Way is principle (li)—it is that very reason by which there is now yin and now yang. How could it ever have physical form? The Way rides upon vital force, mysterious and unbounded in direction; vital force carries the Way, changing and transforming without fixed body. Is this not what the sages of antiquity took as their foundation in making this Book of Changes?

Book of Documents (Shu):
"Suppose I am metal: I will use you as a whetstone. Suppose I am crossing a great river: I will use you as a boat and oars. Suppose it is a year of great drought: I will use you as aThree-day rain."
Fang Sheng 方晟
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Chen: [The three clauses of this topic are all rooted in the idea of "receiving instruction." Among the writers in the examination hall, some occasionally knew this, yet few had words sufficient to bring out its meaning. In this composition, the conception is complete and the style is fluent, …]

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
必熟於經者也
同考試官教諭章批此題作者多泥小註令人厭
觀是篇三節發明高宗託喻望說納誨之切瞭然可佳也
一薦何忝
考試官修撰劉批發明高宗責望傅說之意非
他卷所及
考試官左庶子黎批講約物甚精切
賢君望大臣納誨之心為愈切而取譬之意為
益深夫相業莫大於輔德輔德莫先於納誨也
===
高宗以此命傅說而託物喻之一節深於一節
焉其責望之心不亦愈切乎昔高宗得傅說立
為冢宰使兼師保上文既命之曰朝夕納誨以
輔台德於此乃託物喻之若曰金非礪石以磨
礲之則不能成器我之德有未脩豈不類於金
乎汝之納誨必也以剛濟柔而克去材質之偏
雜以可濟否而銷磨性氣之渣滓一如礪之磨
金不精其制度不止焉此望於說者切矣而猶
未也彼巨川非舟楫以通行之則不能濟險我
punctuated:
必熟於經者也。
同考試官教諭章批：此題作者多泥小註，令人厭觀。是篇三節發明高宗託喻望說納誨之切，瞭然可佳也，一薦何忝。
考試官修撰劉批：發明高宗責望傅說之意，非他卷所及。
考試官左庶子黎批：講約物甚精切。
賢君望大臣納誨之心為愈切，而取譬之意為益深。夫相業莫大於輔德，輔德莫先於納誨也。高宗以此命傅說，而託物喻之，一節深於一節焉，其責望之心不亦愈切乎？昔高宗得傅說，立為冢宰，使兼師保。上文既命之曰：「朝夕納誨，以輔台德。」於此乃託物喻之，若曰：金非礪石以磨礲之，則不能成器。我之德有未脩，豈不類於金乎？汝之納誨，必也以剛濟柔，而克去材質之偏雜；以可濟否，而銷磨性氣之渣滓，一如礪之磨金，不精其制度不止焉。此望於說者切矣，而猶未也。彼巨川非舟楫以通行之，則不能濟險。我
translation_en:
… must be one who is thoroughly versed in the Classic.
Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhang: Most candidates writing on this topic cling rigidly to the minor commentaries, making their essays tiresome to read. In its three sections, this essay elucidates how earnestly King Gaozong used metaphors to express his hope that Yue would offer instruction; it is clear and commendable. How could recommending it bring any shame?
Comment by Examiner, Senior Compiler Liu: It elucidates King Gaozong's intent in placing expectations upon Fu Yue in a way that other papers do not reach.
Comment by Examiner, Left Mentor Li: Its explanation of the metaphors [講納物/講約物?] is extremely precise and apt.
The worthy ruler's heart grew ever more earnest in hoping his great minister would offer instruction, and the meaning of the analogies he drew became ever deeper. Now, the work of a prime minister has nothing greater than assisting the ruler's virtue, and in assisting the ruler's virtue nothing comes before offering instruction. When King Gaozong charged Fu Yue with this and used physical things as metaphors for it, each section went deeper than the last—was not his heart of expectation ever more earnest? In ancient times, when King Gaozong obtained Fu Yue, he appointed him Prime Minister and had him concurrently serve as Grand Tutor and Grand Guardian. Having already charged him in the preceding text, saying, "Morning and evening offer instruction to assist my virtue," here he uses things as metaphors to illustrate it, as if to say: If metal does not have a whetstone to grind and polish it, it cannot be made into a vessel. Where my virtue is not yet cultivated, is it not like unworked metal? In offering instruction, you must temper softness with firmness so as to overcome and remove the biases and impurities of my natural disposition, and remedy what is unacceptable with what is acceptable so as to grind away the dregs of my temperament—just like a whetstone grinding metal, never stopping until its form and measure are perfected. What he hoped for from Yue here was earnest indeed, and yet that was not all. That great river, without boat and oars to traverse it, cannot be crossed through its perils. Where my…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之德有未達豈不類於巨川乎汝之納誨必也
順流開導以充擴聰明之廣遠勇往斷行以弘
濟事業之艱難一如舟楫之涉巨川不抵津涯
不已焉此望於說者加切矣而所及猶有限也
若歲大旱苟無三日之霖雨則萬物槁矣我之
德有未成心方渴教又豈不賴汝作大旱之霖
雨乎汝之納誨又必啓乃心而無隱沃我心而
厭飫忠言讜論大霈甘霖之膏澤用慰滿我之
顒望使怡然理順可也嘉謨嘉猷普施時雨之
===
利益用慰答我之深願使豁然心通可也此則
望於說者愈切而無以加矣古之君相其相資
以成德也有如是夫大抵惟高宗之心契於天
故良弼之徵先見於夢寐之間惟傅說之心契
於君故憲天之戒詳陳於求助之際高宗此以
舟楫霖雨為喻繼以麴糵鹽梅為喻終以股肱
惟人為喻所造益深所望益切矣異時君為令
王臣為賢佐果無負於今日之命也宜哉
志以道寧言以道接不作無益害有益功
punctuated:
