之德有未達，豈不類於巨川乎？汝之納誨，必也順流開導，以充擴聰明之廣遠；勇往斷行，以弘濟事業之艱難；一如舟楫之涉巨川，不抵津涯不已焉。此望於說者加切矣，而所及猶有限也。若歲大旱，苟無三日之霖雨，則萬物槁矣。我之德有未成，心方渴教，又豈不賴汝作大旱之霖雨乎？汝之納誨，又必啓乃心而無隱，沃我心而厭飫。忠言讜論，大霈甘霖之膏澤，用慰滿我之顒望，使怡然理順可也；嘉謨嘉猷，普施時雨之利益，用慰答我之深願，使豁然心通可也。此則望於說者愈切，而無以加矣。古之君相，其相資以成德也，有如是夫！
大抵惟高宗之心契於天，故良弼之徵先見於夢寐之間；惟傅說之心契於君，故憲天之戒詳陳於求助之際。高宗此以舟楫霖雨為喻，繼以麴糵鹽梅為喻，終以股肱惟人為喻，所造益深，所望益切矣。異時君為令王，臣為賢佐，果無負於今日之命也，宜哉！
志以道寧，言以道接。不作無益害有益，功…
translation_en:
…virtue is not yet fully extending, is this not like a great river? In offering your counsel, you must surely guide and open the way along the current so as to expand the breadth and reach of my intelligence and perception, and advance bravely and act decisively so as to broadly carry through the difficulties of our enterprises—just as a boat and oars crossing a great river do not stop until they reach the far shore. Here his expectation of Yue (Fu Yue 傅說) grew more earnest, yet what it reached was still limited. If in a year of great drought there is not a तीन-day soaking rain, then the myriad things will wither. Since my virtue is not yet perfected and my mind is just now thirsting for instruction, how could I not also rely on you to act as the soaking rain in a great drought? In offering your counsel, you must also open your mind without concealment and irrigate my mind until it is fully satisfied. With loyal words and upright discourses, lavishly pour forth the enriching grace of sweet rain to console and fulfill my earnest hopes, so that everything is harmoniously in accord with principle; with fine plans and admirable counsels, universally bestow the benefits of timely rain to console and answer my deep wishes, so that my mind is頓ly opened to understanding. Here his expectation of Yue was even more earnest, and nothing further could be added to it. How much the rulers and chief ministers of antiquity relied upon one another to perfect their virtue in just this way!

In general, it was only because the mind of Gaozong 高宗 was in accord with Heaven that the omen of a good assistant first appeared in his dreams; and it was only because the mind of Fu Yue was in accord with his ruler that the admonition to model oneself on Heaven was set forth in detail at the moment when his aid was sought. Here Gaozong used the metaphors of a boat and oars and of soaking rain, followed by the metaphors of yeast and malt and of salt and sour plums, and ended with the metaphor of the limbs making the man; the further he went, the deeper his attainment, and the more earnest his expectations. That in days to come the ruler became an exemplary king and the minister a worthy assistant, truly not failing the charge given on this day—how fitting indeed!

"When your will is reposed in the Way, and words are received according to the Way; when you do not do what is unprofitable to the injury of what is profitable, then your work…"

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
乃成不貴異物賤用物民乃足犬馬非其
土性不畜珍禽奇獸不育于國不寶遠物
則遠人格所寶惟賢則邇人安
方晟
同考試官教諭陳批此題頗長難於包括惟此
不泛不畧節節寫出召公戒武王之意可愛可愛
同考試官教諭章批作此題者往往自為臆說
不得指歸惟此卷主交脩内外以立本謹好尚以圖治得召公
告戒武王之深旨必孰於璧經者也宜錄之以冠本經
===
考試官修撰劉批能以正本圖治立說足見講貫
之學
考試官左庶子黎批凡作規諫文字要光明正大有
愛君之意此篇其庶幾乎
大臣之戒聖君惟欲交脩於内外以正其本而
致謹於好尚以圖其治夫全一道以兼制内外
則本正矣然不謹好尚是人欲猶得以害吾道
也治功何自而成哉此大臣所以詳為聖君言
歟昔者武王克商西旅貢獒召公以為非所當
punctuated:
乃成；不貴異物賤用物，民乃足。犬馬非其土性不畜，珍禽奇獸不育于國。不寶遠物，則遠人格；所寶惟賢，則邇人安。

方晟。

同考試官教諭陳批：此題頗長，難於包括。惟此不泛不畧，節節寫出召公戒武王之意，可愛可愛。
同考試官教諭章批：作此題者，往往自為臆說，不得指歸。惟此卷主交脩内外以立本、謹好尚以圖治，得召公告戒武王之深旨，必孰於《璧經》者也。宜錄之以冠本經。
考試官修撰劉批：能以正本圖治立說，足見講貫之學。
考試官左庶子黎批：凡作規諫文字，要光明正大，有愛君之意，此篇其庶幾乎。

大臣之戒聖君，惟欲交脩於内外以正其本，而致謹於好尚以圖其治。夫全一道以兼制内外，則本正矣；然不謹好尚，是人欲猶得以害吾道也，治功何自而成哉？此大臣所以詳為聖君言歟！昔者武王克商，西旅貢獒，召公以為非所當…
translation_en:
… then achievement will be accomplished; do not value exotic things and despise useful things, and then the people will have sufficiency. Dogs and horses that are not native to the land should not be raised; rare birds and strange beasts should not be bred in the state. If you do not treasure things from afar, then people from afar will come; if what you treasure is only the worthy, then people nearby will be at peace.”

Fang Sheng 方晟.

Associate Examiner Instructor Chen 陳 comments: This topic is rather long and difficult to encompass. Only this essay is neither rambling nor sketchy, bringing out point by point the meaning of the Duke of Shao’s admonition to King Wu. Truly admirable, truly admirable!
Associate Examiner Instructor Zhang 章 comments: Those who write on this topic often make up their own conjectures and fail to grasp the main purport. Only this paper takes as its central thesis cultivating both the inner and the outer to establish the foundation, and exercising caution in one’s preferences and tastes to seek good governance. It captures the profound import of the Duke of Shao’s admonition to King Wu; the author must be thoroughly versed in the Classic from the Wall [Book of Documents]. It ought to be selected to stand first in this Classic.
Examiner Senior Compiler Liu 劉 comments: Being able to construct the argument around rectifying the foundation and seeking good governance amply demonstrates a scholarship of thorough study and comprehension.
Examiner Left Mentor Li 黎 comments: Whenever one writes an essay on remonstrance, it must be upright, grand, and imbued with affection for the ruler. This piece comes very close to that ideal.

When a great minister admonishes a sage ruler, he desires only that the ruler cultivate both the inner and the outer so as to rectify the foundation, and exercise caution in his preferences and tastes so as to seek good governance. Now, when one preserves the single Way in its entirety so as to regulate both the inner and the outer, the foundation is rectified; yet if one is not cautious in preferences and tastes, then human desires can still harm our Way—how then could the work of governance ever be accomplished? Is this not why the great minister spoke at such length to the sage ruler? In antiquity, after King Wu conquered Shang, the Western Lü presented a mastiff as tribute. The Duke of Shao, considering that it was not something that ought to be…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
乃作書戒之若曰道者所當由之理也己之志
不以道而寧則妄發必也順適乎道心之正而
不陷於人欲之危使志與道一焉此存乎中以
應乎外也人之言不以道而接則妄受必也無
稽之言弗聽弗詢之謀勿庸使言與道俱焉此
制乎外以養其中也今王過受獒之志却獻獒
之言本斯正矣然不謹好尚以圖治又豈可哉
彼遊觀為無益而務農講武非有益乎惟不作
無益害有益則逸樂怠荒不妨乎政而功乃成
===
也奇巧為異物而服食器用非用物乎惟不貴
異物賤用物則橫征暴斂不加於民而民乃足
也南北之風土不同故犬馬非其土性者不畜
于我邦焉寒暑之稟性各異故禽獸賦質珍奇
者不育于我國焉然於犬馬之類不畜不育則
不以遠物為寶也人君賤貨如此殆見四夷之
人皆知吾君之正身脩德必奉贄貢琛而來享
矣其遠人格也為何如於俊傑之才是崇是長
則專以賢才為寶也人君貴德如此殆見中國
punctuated: 乃作書戒之。若曰：道者，所當由之理也。己之志不以道而寧，則妄發。必也順適乎道心之正，而不陷於人欲之危，使志與道一焉，此存乎中以應乎外也。人之言不以道而接，則妄受。必也無稽之言弗聽，弗詢之謀勿庸，使言與道俱焉，此制乎外以養其中也。今王過受獒之志，却獻獒之言，本斯正矣。然不謹好尚以圖治，又豈可哉？彼遊觀為無益，而務農講武非有益乎？惟不作無益害有益，則逸樂怠荒不妨乎政，而功乃成也。奇巧為異物，而服食器用非用物乎？惟不貴異物賤用物，則橫征暴斂不加於民，而民乃足也。南北之風土不同，故犬馬非其土性者不畜于我邦焉；寒暑之稟性各異，故禽獸賦質珍奇者不育于我國焉。然於犬馬之類不畜不育，則不以遠物為寶也。人君賤貨如此，殆見四夷之人皆知吾君之正身脩德，必奉贄貢琛而來享矣，其遠人格也為何如？於俊傑之才是崇是長，則專以賢才為寶也。人君貴德如此，殆見中國
translation_en:
… and thus wrote a treatise to admonish him, as if to say: The Way is the principle one ought to follow. If one's own will does not find repose through the Way, it will issue forth recklessly. One must conform to the correctness of the mind of the Way and not fall into the peril of human desires, making one's will and the Way become one; this is preserving what is within in order to respond to what is without. If the words of others are not received through the Way, they will be accepted recklessly. One must not listen to unfounded words nor employ unconsulted counsels, making words accord with the Way; this is regulating what is without in order to nourish what is within. Now, if the king checks [?] the will to accept the hound and rejects the words accompanying the presentation of the hound, the root will thereby be rectified. Yet how could it be permissible not to exercise caution in one's preferences and inclinations in order to plan for good governance?

Those excursions and sightseeing are unprofitable, whereas devoting oneself to agriculture and practicing martial arts—are these not profitable? Only when one does not do the unprofitable to the detriment of the profitable will indulgence in pleasure and negligent idleness not hinder governance, and thus achievements will be realized. The奇巧 (curious and ingenious) are strange things, whereas clothing, food, and implements—are these not useful things? Only when one does not prize strange things and belittle useful things will arbitrary levies and harsh exactions not be imposed upon the people, and thus the people will have sufficiency.

The climates and soils of north and south are not the same; therefore, dogs and horses not native to the land are not reared in our state. The natural endowments with respect to cold and heat each differ; therefore, birds and beasts of rare and curious nature are not bred in our country. Now, neither rearing nor breeding such things as dogs and horses means not treating things from afar as treasures. When a ruler disdains goods in this manner, we shall surely see the peoples of the four borderlands all recognize that our ruler rectifies his person and cultivates his virtue, and they will certainly present gifts and offer treasures in tribute; how great then will be the winning over of people from afar! When one honors and promotes men of outstanding talent, it means exclusively treating worthy talents as treasures. When a ruler esteems virtue in this manner, we shall surely see that in the Central States …

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之人皆被賢才之深仁厚澤必家給人足而永
寧矣其邇人安也又何如噫正其本則心法所
當全圖其治則治法所當備彼一獒烏足以累
盛德歟雖然以武王之聖宜若細行無不謹者
而召公猶拳拳戒之何也殊不知流金爍石而
一陰生寒於此始折膠墮指而一陽生暑於此
萌元老大臣愛君憂國常防危於其安為大於
其細耳厥後武王果能以敬勝怠垂八百年之
統良有以夫
===
詩
王命仲山甫式是百辟纘戎祖考王躬是
保出納王命王之喉舌賦政于外四方爰
發肅肅王命仲山甫將之
梁斆
同考試官訓導沈 批 題本平易作者忽畧多
不合㫖惟是篇詞氣和平宛然寫出當時吉甫贈行意
思一薦何忝
同考試官教諭徐 批 詩不下八百餘卷此題於
punctuated:
之人皆被賢才之深仁厚澤，必家給人足而永寧矣，其邇人安也又何如！噫！正其本則心法所當全，圖其治則治法所當備，彼一獒烏足以累盛德歟？雖然，以武王之聖，宜若細行無不謹者，而召公猶拳拳戒之，何也？殊不知流金爍石而一陰生，寒於此始；折膠墮指而一陽生，暑於此萌。元老大臣愛君憂國，常防危於其安，為大於其細耳。厥後武王果能以敬勝怠，垂八百年之統，良有以夫！

詩
王命仲山甫，式是百辟。纘戎祖考，王躬是保。出納王命，王之喉舌。賦政于外，四方爰發。肅肅王命，仲山甫將之。
梁斆
同考試官訓導沈批：題本平易，作者忽畧，多不合㫖。惟是篇詞氣和平，宛然寫出當時吉甫贈行意思，一薦何忝！
同考試官教諭徐批：詩不下八百餘卷，此題於
translation_en:
… people of the central states will all receive the deep benevolence and generous favor of worthy talents, and every household will surely be well-supplied, every person content, and the realm eternally peaceful—how great, too, will be the tranquility of those who are near! Alas! To rectify the root, the method of the mind must be made complete; to plan for good governance, the method of rule must be fully prepared. How could that single mastiff suffice to blemish his abundant virtue? Even so, given the sageliness of King Wu, it would seem that he was already careful in every minor action; why then did the Duke of Shao still so earnestly admonish him? Little do people realize that when heat melts metal and scorches stone, a single yin force is born, and cold begins right there; when frost snaps glue and makes fingers drop off, a single yang force is born, and summer heat sprouts right there. Elder statesmen and great ministers, loving their ruler and worrying for the state, always guard against danger in times of security and tackle the great while it is still small. Thereafter, King Wu was indeed able to overcome negligence through reverence and hand down a dynastic line of eight hundred years—truly there was a reason for it!

Classic of Poetry (Shijing)
"The King charged Zhong Shanfu: 'Be a model to all the lords; continue the work of your great ancestors, and protect the King's own person; issue and receive the King's commands, as the King's throat and tongue; spread government abroad, so that the four quarters respond in action.' Solemn is the King's charge, and Zhong Shanfu carries it out."
By Liang Xiao 梁斆
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Shen: The topic is inherently plain and accessible, yet writers treated it carelessly and most failed to match its purport. Only this essay is harmonious and calm in diction and spirit, vividly capturing Yin Jifu's 尹吉甫 thoughts when presenting a farewell poem at the time. What shame could there be in recommending it?
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Xu: There were no fewer than eight hundred scripts on the Classic of Poetry. On this topic, regarding …

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
宣王命山甫山甫奉王命處多得此失彼惟此作詞語舂
容事實不遺故用錄出
考試官脩撰劉批詞婉而意切詩人之意正如此
考試官左庶子黎批此言吉甫作頌曲盡大臣謀國之
忠朋友輔仁之益想其人必溫柔敦厚者
詩人之贈大臣也既述王者之命備舉眾職復
美大臣之賢克稱其職蓋人臣受命貴乎克稱
其職也今王者備舉眾職以命大臣而大臣能
奉承無忝焉非有德者能如是乎詩人美之於
===
贈行之時宜矣昔宣王命樊侯仲山甫築城于
齊而尹吉甫作詩送之此述王命山甫之意謂
夫外而諸侯冢宰所統也今則命爾為冢宰以
楷範藩垣為諸侯之法焉內而君德太保所輔
也今則命爾兼太保以繼繩祖考維王躬是保
焉于以出王命於區夏則承而布之也于以納
王命於朝廷則行而復之也出納王命以代王
言斯其為王之喉舌上下賴此總而達之矣于
以宣德意於萬國使民得其所也于以覃恩澤
punctuated:
宣王命山甫、山甫奉王命處，多得此失彼。惟此作詞語舂容，事實不遺，故用錄出。
考試官脩撰劉批：詞婉而意切，詩人之意正如此。
考試官左庶子黎批：此言吉甫作頌，曲盡大臣謀國之忠、朋友輔仁之益，想其人必溫柔敦厚者。
詩人之贈大臣也，既述王者之命備舉眾職，復美大臣之賢克稱其職。蓋人臣受命，貴乎克稱其職也。今王者備舉眾職以命大臣，而大臣能奉承無忝焉，非有德者能如是乎？詩人美之於贈行之時，宜矣。昔宣王命樊侯仲山甫築城于齊，而尹吉甫作詩送之。此述王命山甫之意，謂夫外而諸侯，冢宰所統也，今則命爾為冢宰，以楷範藩垣，為諸侯之法焉；內而君德，太保所輔也，今則命爾兼太保，以繼繩祖考，維王躬是保焉。于以出王命於區夏，則承而布之也；于以納王命於朝廷，則行而復之也。出納王命以代王言，斯其為王之喉舌，上下賴此總而達之矣。于以宣德意於萬國，使民得其所也；于以覃恩澤
translation_en:
… the points where King Xuan charges Shanfu and where Shanfu carries out the king's charge, most candidates grasp one aspect while losing sight of the other. Only this essay is composed in poised and measured language without omitting any of the substantive facts, and for that reason it has been selected for inclusion.

Examiner Liu, Senior Compiler, comments: The phrasing is gentle yet the meaning is incisive; the poet's intent was precisely this.

Examiner Li, Left Mentor of the Secretariat of the Heir Apparent, comments: Speaking of Jifu's composition of this ode, this essay thoroughly captures the loyalty of a great minister in planning for the state and the benefit of friends in aiding one another toward benevolence. One imagines the writer himself must be a person of gentle and generous disposition.

When the poet presented a farewell piece to the great minister, having recounted the sovereign's charge that comprehensively enumerated his manifold duties, he went on to praise the worthiness of the great minister in being fully equal to his offices. Indeed, when a minister receives a charge, what is prized is his ability to prove equal to his duties. Now, when a sovereign comprehensively enumerates manifold duties in charging a great minister, and the great minister is able to uphold and execute them without bringing disgrace upon them—could anyone who was not a man of virtue do such a thing? That the poet praised him at the time of his farewell was fitting indeed.

In antiquity, King Xuan commanded Zhong Shanfu, Marquis of Fan, to fortify a city in Qi, and Yin Jifu composed an ode to see him off. This stanza recounts the import of the king's charge to Shanfu, saying: Outside the court, the feudal lords are governed by the Minister of State; now I appoint you Minister of State to serve as a standard for the feudatory bulwarks and a model for the feudal lords. Inside the court, the ruler's virtue is assisted by the Grand Guardian; now I appoint you concurrently as Grand Guardian to continue the line of our ancestors and deceased father, and to protect the king's own person. In issuing the king's commands throughout the Chinese realm, you receive them and promulgate them; in reporting on the king's commands to the court, you carry them out and reply upon their execution. Issuing and reporting on the king's commands so as to speak on the king's behalf—this is to be the king's throat and tongue, upon whom both above and below rely to bring all matters together and communicate them. In proclaiming virtuous intentions to the myriad states so that the people may find their proper place, and in extending benevolent grace…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
於八荒使物遂其生也賦政于外以彰明命斯
其為國之藎臣四方於是發而應之矣王命仲
山甫者如此非山甫之賢曷能奉承哉故吉甫
復為之言曰今茲山甫之行外焉總領諸侯內
焉輔養君德王之命其嚴肅矣乎我嘗旁觀於
朝著之間求其悉乃心輸乃悃善體君心者盖
鮮焉若奉行此命而不失維山甫一人而已耳
入焉典司政本出焉經營四方王之命其嚴重
矣乎我嘗屈指於卿相之列求其披厥誠露厥
===
膽克諧帝旨者盖寡焉若對揚此命而無違亦
惟山甫一人而已耳大臣城齊之行而同列以
是贈之可謂相知之深而相與之切也歟考之
宣王復文武之境土振中興之大業未嘗不本
於良臣以為之佐耳故賛襄調燮者有山甫之
德行功業啓沃左右者有吉甫之學問文章此
所以恢復舊物而赫然中興也歟讀詩者尚當
知所本云
明明魯侯克明其德既作泮宮淮夷攸服
punctuated:
於八荒，使物遂其生也。賦政于外，以彰明命，斯其為國之藎臣，四方於是發而應之矣。王命仲山甫者如此，非山甫之賢，曷能奉承哉？故吉甫復為之言曰：今茲山甫之行，外焉總領諸侯，內焉輔養君德，王之命其嚴肅矣乎！我嘗旁觀於朝著之間，求其悉乃心、輸乃悃、善體君心者，盖鮮焉；若奉行此命而不失，維山甫一人而已耳。入焉典司政本，出焉經營四方，王之命其嚴重矣乎！我嘗屈指於卿相之列，求其披厥誠、露厥膽、克諧帝旨者，盖寡焉；若對揚此命而無違，亦惟山甫一人而已耳。大臣城齊之行，而同列以是贈之，可謂相知之深而相與之切也歟！考之宣王復文武之境土，振中興之大業，未嘗不本於良臣以為之佐耳。故賛襄調燮者，有山甫之德行功業；啓沃左右者，有吉甫之學問文章。此所以恢復舊物，而赫然中興也歟！讀詩者尚當知所本云。

「明明魯侯，克明其德。既作泮宮，淮夷攸服。
translation_en:
…unto the eight wildernesses, causing all living things to fulfill their lives. Spreading governance abroad so as to make manifest the bright mandate—thus he is a devoted minister of the state, and the four quarters thereupon stir and respond to him! What the King commanded of Zhong Shanfu 仲山甫 was such as this; without Shanfu's worthiness, how could he have received and upheld it? Therefore Jifu 吉甫 spoke further of him, saying: In Shanfu's present expedition, externally he exercises general leadership over the feudal lords, and internally he assists and nourishes the ruler's virtue—how solemn and august is the King's command! I have looked around among the ranks of the court, seeking those who exhaust their minds, pour out their sincere devotion, and skillfully embody the ruler's heart, and they are few indeed; as for carrying out this command without fail, there is only Shanfu alone. Entering court to take charge of the foundations of governance, going out to manage and order the four quarters—how grave and weighty is the King's command! I have counted on my fingers among the ranks of the grandees and chief ministers, seeking those who lay bare their sincerity, expose their courage, and are able to harmonize with the sovereign's intent, and they are rare indeed; as for responding to and extolling this command without transgression, there is likewise only Shanfu alone. On a great minister's journey to fortify Qi 齊, for a colleague to present him with such words as these—may it not be called a deep mutual understanding and an earnest mutual regard? When we examine how King Xuan 宣王 recovered the territory of Kings Wen 文 and Wu 武 and revived the great enterprise of dynastic restoration, it was never not rooted in having good ministers as his assistants. Thus, in assisting governance and harmonizing affairs, there were the virtuous conduct and meritorious achievements of Shanfu; in enlightening and guiding at his side, there were the learning and literary refinement of Jifu. Was it not by this means that he recovered the old patrimony and achieved a glorious restoration? Readers of the Odes (Shi 詩) ought indeed to recognize where its foundation lay.

"Bright, bright is the Marquis of Lu 魯, able to make bright his virtue. Having built the Pangong 泮宮 school, the Huai Yi 淮夷 tribes are thereby subdued. …

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
矯矯虎臣在泮獻馘淑問如臯陶在泮獻
囚濟濟多士克廣德心桓桓于征狄彼東
南烝烝皇皇不吳不揚不告于訩在泮獻
功
王敏
同考試官訓導沈批大題貴乎包括作者率皆
支離冗泛殊不愜意此篇文理簡明深體魯人祝君之心
冀北騏驥端在是矣
同考試官教諭徐批文教武功皆魯人願望其君
===
之詞作者以為實事殊戾本旨能以祝頌立說無踰此篇
考試官修撰劉批魯人頌禱其君之意宛然可見
善說詩者也
考試官左庶子黎批魯頌多願望之詞學者不可指
作實事惟講貫精到以已心想象當時自然成文矣此人善於
想象詩學必熟
魯人因其君飲于學也既願其興文教以懷遠
而得人以獻功復願羣臣振德威以伐遠而恊
心以獻功夫興文教以懷遠則文事舉振德威
punctuated:
矯矯虎臣，在泮獻馘；淑問如臯陶，在泮獻囚。濟濟多士，克廣德心，桓桓于征，狄彼東南。烝烝皇皇，不吳不揚，不告于訩，在泮獻功。
王敏
同考試官訓導沈批：大題貴乎包括，作者率皆支離冗泛，殊不愜意。此篇文理簡明，深體魯人祝君之心，冀北騏驥，端在是矣。
同考試官教諭徐批：文教武功，皆魯人願望其君之詞，作者以為實事，殊戾本旨。能以祝頌立說，無踰此篇。
考試官修撰劉批：魯人頌禱其君之意宛然可見，善說詩者也。
考試官左庶子黎批：魯頌多願望之詞，學者不可指作實事。惟講貫精到，以已心想象當時，自然成文矣。此人善於想象，詩學必熟。
魯人因其君飲于學也，既願其興文教以懷遠，而得人以獻功；復願羣臣振德威以伐遠，而恊心以獻功。夫興文教以懷遠，則文事舉；振德威…
translation_en:
…"Martial are the tiger-like ministers, who at the Pan Palace present the severed left ears of the slain; skilled in interrogation like Gao Yao, at the Pan Palace they present the captives. Numerous are the many officers, able to broaden their virtuous hearts; martial as they go on the campaign, they keep at bay those tribes of the southeast. Vigorous and grand, neither clamorous nor boastful, bringing no disputes for judgment, at the Pan Palace they present their achievements."

Wang Min 王敏

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Shen 沈 comments: A long topic calls for comprehensive coverage, yet writers are generally fragmented, verbose, and unfocused, which is most unsatisfactory. The reasoning and style of this essay are concise and clear, deeply grasping the people of Lu's 魯 desire to offer blessings to their ruler. Truly, here is a fine steed from north of Ji 冀!

Associate Examiner and Instructor Xu 徐 comments: Both the civil teachings and the military achievements are words expressing what the people of Lu hoped for in their ruler; writers who treat them as accomplished facts go quite against the original purport. In constructing an argument grounded in celebratory prayer, no essay surpasses this one.

Examiner and Senior Compiler Liu 劉 comments: The intent of the people of Lu in praising and praying for their ruler is vividly apparent. Here is one skilled in explaining the Odes (Shijing)!

Examiner and Left Mentor of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent Li 黎 comments: The "Praise-Odes of Lu" (Lu song 魯頌) consist largely of expressions of hope and aspiration, which scholars must not treat as accomplished facts. Only when one's comprehension is thorough and exact, using one's own mind to imagine the circumstances of that time, will a fine composition naturally take shape. This candidate excels at such imaginative empathy; his mastery of the Odes must be thorough indeed.

On the occasion of their ruler's feasting at the state school, the people of Lu first wished that he might promote civil teachings so as to win over the distant, and obtain worthy men to present their achievements; and they further wished that all his ministers might rouse their virtuous majesty to campaign against the distant, and unite their hearts to present their achievements. Now, when civil teachings are promoted to win over the distant, civil affairs are upheld; when virtuous majesty is roused…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
以伐遠則武備脩魯人以此祝其君臣且願羣
臣各獻功於學焉其忠愛之誠一何至哉此飲
于泮宫而頌禱之詞想夫魯人之意若曰我明
明之魯侯戾止于斯誠願其遏欲存理克明厥
德而無昧焉美茲泮宫崇化於我魯也久矣今
其脩之使遵先王之教以采其芹藻也蠢彼淮
夷為害於我魯也深矣行且服之使被泮宫之
化以屈此羣醜也然淮夷有梗化不服者焉安
得矯矯之武臣勇猛如虓虎臨陳殄戮取所格
===
者之左耳獻于泮宫乎有執訊而服罪者焉安
得明慎之士師善問如皐陶錄拘囚者之罪狀
獻于泮宫乎盖古者建學飲酒在此受成在此
所謂興文教以懷遠而得人以獻功者非歟然
魯人之意不但已也又言曰願我濟濟之多士
懲忿窒欲克推善意而不隘焉彼東南淮夷今
既獻馘不可遺患又當奮桓桓之武攘而遏之
也今既獻囚不可縱惡尚當驅烈烈之兵征而
□□也夫人惟無勇也則功不立安得多士出
punctuated: 以伐遠則武備脩。魯人以此祝其君臣，且願羣臣各獻功於學焉，其忠愛之誠一何至哉！此飲于泮宫而頌禱之詞。想夫魯人之意，若曰：「我明明之魯侯戾止于斯，誠願其遏欲存理，克明厥德而無昧焉。美茲泮宫，崇化於我魯也久矣，今其脩之，使遵先王之教，以采其芹藻也；蠢彼淮夷，為害於我魯也深矣，行且服之，使被泮宫之化，以屈此羣醜也。然淮夷有梗化不服者焉，安得矯矯之武臣，勇猛如虓虎，臨陳殄戮，取所格者之左耳獻于泮宫乎？有執訊而服罪者焉，安得明慎之士師，善問如皐陶，錄拘囚者之罪狀獻于泮宫乎？盖古者建學，飲酒在此，受成在此，所謂興文教以懷遠，而得人以獻功者非歟？」然魯人之意不但已也，又言曰：「願我濟濟之多士，懲忿窒欲，克推善意而不隘焉。彼東南淮夷，今既獻馘，不可遺患，又當奮桓桓之武，攘而遏之也；今既獻囚，不可縱惡，尚當驅烈烈之兵，征而□□也。夫人惟無勇也，則功不立，安得多士出
translation_en: …to chastise the distant, military preparedness is cultivated. That the people of Lu offered such wishes for their ruler and ministers, and furthermore wished for the assembled ministers each to present their achievements at the school—how supreme was the sincerity of their loyalty and affection! These are the words of praise and prayer offered while feasting at the Pan Palace (Pangong). Let us imagine the intent of the people of Lu, as if they were saying: "Our illustrious Marquis of Lu has arrived here; we truly wish that he curb human desires and preserve heavenly principle, being able to make bright his virtue without obscuration. Admirable is this Pan Palace, which has long exalted moral transformation in our state of Lu; now let him cultivate it, causing people to follow the teachings of the former kings and gather its cress and pondweed. Unruly are those Huai Yi tribes, who have deeply harmed our state of Lu; soon he will subjugate them, causing them to receive the transformative influence of the Pan Palace and bringing this multitude of miscreants to submission. Yet among the Huai Yi there are those who obstruct transformation and refuse to submit—how might we obtain martial ministers of valor, fierce as roaring tigers, to exterminate them in battle and take the severed left ears of those slain in combat to present at the Pan Palace? And as for those who are captured for interrogation and confess their crimes—how might we obtain a discerning and cautious Chief Justice (shishi), skilled in questioning like Gao Yao, to record the offenses of the prisoners and present them at the Pan Palace? For in antiquity, when schools were established, feasting took place here and the reporting of completed military campaigns took place here. Is this not what is meant by promoting civil teachings to cherish the distant, and obtaining capable men to present their achievements?" Yet the intent of the people of Lu did not stop there. They further said: "We wish that our dignified multitude of officers restrain their anger and repress their desires, able to extend their good intentions broadly without narrowness. As for those Huai Yi of the southeast, now that severed ears have been presented, no lingering threat must be left behind, so they should again rouse their martial might to repel and check them; now that prisoners have been presented, evil must not be indulged, so they should still drive forth their formidable troops to campaign and [?] them. Indeed, only when men lack courage can merit not be established; how might we have our multitude of officers go forth…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
□有烝烝皇皇之衆盛有不吴不揚之整肅一
舉而收萬全之功乎人惟不和也則事不成安
得多士凱還不以争功之事告于治獄之官惟
和敬以在泮獻功乎盖古者建學養才在此獻
功在此所謂振德威以伐遠而恊心以獻功者
又非歟甚矣魯人之愛君也祝頌之辭不一而
足孝祖獲福魯侯欲也從而願之飲酒得壽魯
侯欲也從而願之順長道化淮夷魯侯欲也從
而願之魯人無一念不願其君如此詞雖夸而
===
心則忠非深愛其君者不能君子謂魯有先王
之遺風信夫
春秋
戊辰諸侯盟于葵丘
萬盛
同考試官教諭顏批葵丘之盟專美齊桓伯
業之盛作者多以盛衰對說殊戾厥旨獨此篇一本胡傳
詞豐筆勁如長江疊浪然非老學不能辭經魁擢舎子其誰
考試官修撰劉批義本胡傳以葵丘為齊桓伯業
punctuated:
□，有烝烝皇皇之衆盛，有不吴不揚之整肅，一舉而收萬全之功乎？人惟不和也，則事不成；安得多士凱還，不以争功之事告于治獄之官，惟和敬以在泮獻功乎？盖古者建學，養才在此，獻功在此，所謂振德威以伐遠，而恊心以獻功者，又非歟？甚矣，魯人之愛君也！祝頌之辭，不一而足。孝祖獲福，魯侯欲也，從而願之；飲酒得壽，魯侯欲也，從而願之；順長道、化淮夷，魯侯欲也，從而願之。魯人無一念不願其君如此，詞雖夸而心則忠，非深愛其君者不能。君子謂魯有先王之遺風，信夫！

春秋

戊辰，諸侯盟于葵丘。

萬盛
同考試官教諭顏批：葵丘之盟，專美齊桓伯業之盛。作者多以盛衰對說，殊戾厥旨。獨此篇一本胡傳，詞豐筆勁，如長江疊浪然，非老學不能辭。經魁擢，舎子其誰？
考試官修撰劉批：義本胡傳，以葵丘為齊桓伯業
translation_en:
… march [?], possessing the thriving multitude of vigorous and majestic troops, and the solemn discipline free of clamor or arrogance, so as to achieve complete success at a single stroke? It is only when men lack harmony that enterprises fail; how could we obtain this host of officers returning in triumph, bringing no disputes over merit before the judicial officials, but instead presenting their achievements at the Pan palace in harmony and reverence? For in antiquity, when schools were established, nurturing talent took place here, and presenting achievements took place here. Is this not also what is meant by rousing moral prestige to chastise distant lands, and uniting hearts to present achievements? Profound indeed was the people of Lu's love for their ruler! Their words of blessing and praise were manifold. To be filial to the ancestors and receive blessings was what the Marquis of Lu desired, and accordingly they wished it for him; to drink wine and attain longevity was what the Marquis of Lu desired, and accordingly they wished it for him; to follow the enduring Way and transform the Huai Yi tribes was what the Marquis of Lu desired, and accordingly they wished it for him. Not a single thought of the people of Lu failed to wish the best for their ruler in this manner. Though their words were grand, their hearts were loyal—none who did not deeply love their ruler could be capable of this. When the gentleman says that Lu preserved the lingering customs of the former kings, how true it is!

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

"On the day wuchen, the feudal lords made a covenant at Kuiqiu."

Wan Sheng 萬盛
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Yan 顏: The covenant at Kuiqiu exclusively praises the flourishing of Duke Huan of Qi's hegemonic enterprise. Most writers contrast its flourishing with its decline, which goes utterly against the true purport. Only this essay is grounded wholly in the Commentary of Hu An-guo (Hu zhuan), with rich diction and vigorous brushwork like the surging waves of the Yangtze River—expressions of which none but a seasoned scholar is capable. For selection as top graduate in this Classic (jingkui), if not you, then who?
Comment by Examiner Senior Compiler Liu 劉: Its meaning is grounded in the Commentary of Hu An-guo, taking Kuiqiu as the … of Duke Huan of Qi's hegemonic enterprise …

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之盛得筆削之旨
考試官左庶子黎批葵丘五禁孟子與之朱子曰葵丘
之會自是好本末自是别胡傳以為美之大者其言伯業之衰
乃後人推出耳今讀春秋必欲外胡傳以盛衰對講惑矣此篇
專主胡傳備言美之大者後乃結出衰處學春秋者當法此
伯主講信以明天王之大禁春秋特筆以示人
臣之大美此見五伯莫盛於桓公而桓公之業
又莫盛於葵丘春秋備日以書之其美之大者
尚何以加於此哉嘅自姬轍不西乾綱失馭天
===
下之不知有周久矣幸而齊桓者出力收渙散
之人心營成九合之功業兩鄄有會伯圖定矣
而王室則未尊兩幽有盟王室尊矣而王禁則
未明是以葵丘之會方同於夏葵丘之盟復講
於秋斯時也冢宰既歸諸侯咸在大而鄭衛昔
嘗違水木本源之義各國其國也今則傾心協
從而駿奔走于壇坫之間小而曹許昔嘗昧江
漢朝宗之心各民其民也今則拱手聽令而恪
供事於威靈之下與夫魯公宋子又皆膏車秣
punctuated:
之盛，得筆削之旨。

考試官左庶子黎批：葵丘五禁，孟子與之。朱子曰：「葵丘之會自是好，本末自是别。」胡傳以為美之大者，其言伯業之衰，乃後人推出耳。今讀春秋，必欲外胡傳，以盛衰對講，惑矣。此篇專主胡傳，備言美之大者，後乃結出衰處。學春秋者當法此。

伯主講信，以明天王之大禁；春秋特筆，以示人臣之大美。此見五伯莫盛於桓公，而桓公之業又莫盛於葵丘。春秋備日以書之，其美之大者，尚何以加於此哉！嘅自姬轍不西，乾綱失馭，天下之不知有周久矣。幸而齊桓者出，力收渙散之人心，營成九合之功業。兩鄄有會，伯圖定矣，而王室則未尊；兩幽有盟，王室尊矣，而王禁則未明。是以葵丘之會方同於夏，葵丘之盟復講於秋。斯時也，冢宰既歸，諸侯咸在。大而鄭衛，昔嘗違水木本源之義，各國其國也，今則傾心協從，而駿奔走于壇坫之間；小而曹許，昔嘗昧江漢朝宗之心，各民其民也，今則拱手聽令，而恪供事於威靈之下。與夫魯公宋子，又皆膏車秣
translation_en:
…the flourishing of his hegemony, grasping the intent behind the text’s inclusions and omissions.

Comment by Examiner Li, Left Junior Supervisor of Instruction: Mencius approved the five prohibitions proclaimed at Kuiqiu. Master Zhu said: “The meeting at Kuiqiu was certainly good; its beginning and end are separate matters.” Hu’s Commentary regards this as an instance of the highest excellence. The claim that it speaks of the decline of the hegemony is merely an inference drawn by later readers. Those who now read the Spring and Autumn Annals and insist on setting aside Hu’s Commentary to discuss flourishing and decline as a contrasting pair are mistaken. This essay takes Hu’s Commentary alone as its guide, fully expounding that supreme excellence, and only afterward brings out the point of decline in its conclusion. Students of the Spring and Autumn Annals should take this as their model.

The hegemon reaffirmed good faith to make clear the great prohibitions of the Heavenly King; the Spring and Autumn Annals employed exceptional wording to display the supreme excellence of a ruler’s servant. This shows that, among the Five Hegemons, none flourished more than Duke Huan, and that Duke Huan’s achievements reached their height at Kuiqiu. The Spring and Autumn Annals records the event with its precise date: how could the greatness of this praise possibly be surpassed? Alas, ever since the carriage tracks of the house of Ji ceased to lead westward and the sovereign’s authority lost its command, the world had long ceased to acknowledge Zhou. Fortunately, Duke Huan of Qi emerged, striving to rally the scattered loyalties of the people and accomplishing the great work of assembling the lords nine times. With the two meetings at Juan, his plan for hegemony was secured, but the royal house had yet to be honored. With the two covenants at You, the royal house was honored, but the royal prohibitions had yet to be made clear. Thus, after the gathering at Kuiqiu had brought them together in summer, the covenant at Kuiqiu was reaffirmed in autumn.

At this time, the Grand Steward had already returned, while the regional lords were all still present. Among the larger states, Zheng and Wei had formerly violated the principle that water has a source and trees have roots, each treating its own state as wholly its own. Now they gave their wholehearted allegiance and hastened about the covenant altar and ceremonial stands. Among the smaller states, Cao and Xu had formerly lacked the disposition to pay homage, as the Jiang and Han rivers flow toward the sea, each treating its own people as wholly its own. Now they stood with hands clasped, awaiting commands, and respectfully rendered service beneath his awe-inspiring authority. The Duke of Lu and the lord of Song likewise all greased their carriages and readied fodder…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
馬聿來同好矣此雖人事當然亦天有意於周
室而扶持之也曾謂會盟非畏天乎桓公於是
束牲載書申明五禁有如正綱常用賢才國君
所以隆家國也則初命再命舉之序長幼重刑
賞國君所以明政治也則三命四命申之與夫
睦鄰封爵又皆丁寧告戒五命詳陳矣此雖天
典所在亦人有心於倫理而表正之也曾謂法
禁不可律人乎五命之嚴如風動物一王之法
如日中天臣子之大節以盡天下之號令一新
===
桓公翼戴襄王之功於是乎盛矣春秋為見天
子之禁故備日以紀其實為表尊王之義故備
地以著其美而仲尼稱其一匡孟子與其為盛
良有以夫於戲美則美矣謂之盡善則未也况
使桓公終始此心安知不底於王道耶柰何初
心一移成功頓異城杞之勤不若城邢救徐之
師怠於救許伐黃不恤謀鄫無成三十年之功
一旦掃地矣先儒於此以為美其盛而憂其衰
豈無意歟孟子曰以力假仁者伯吾觀於桓益
punctuated: 馬，聿來同好矣。此雖人事當然，亦天有意於周室而扶持之也。曾謂會盟非畏天乎？桓公於是束牲載書，申明五禁：有如正綱常、用賢才，國君所以隆家國也，則初命、再命舉之；序長幼、重刑賞，國君所以明政治也，則三命、四命申之；與夫睦鄰、封爵，又皆丁寧告戒，五命詳陳矣。此雖天典所在，亦人有心於倫理而表正之也。曾謂法禁不可律人乎？五命之嚴，如風動物；一王之法，如日中天。臣子之大節以盡，天下之號令一新，桓公翼戴襄王之功，於是乎盛矣。《春秋》為見天子之禁，故備日以紀其實；為表尊王之義，故備地以著其美。而仲尼稱其「一匡」，孟子與其為盛，良有以夫！於戲！美則美矣，謂之盡善則未也。况使桓公終始此心，安知不底於王道耶？柰何初心一移，成功頓異：城杞之勤不若城邢，救徐之師怠於救許，伐黃不恤，謀鄫無成，三十年之功一旦掃地矣。先儒於此，以為美其盛而憂其衰，豈無意歟？孟子曰：「以力假仁者伯。」吾觀於桓益…
translation_en:
… [greased their] carriages and fed their horses, coming forth to join in shared amity! Although this was naturally the course of human affairs, it was also because Heaven had intentions for the House of Zhou and sustained it. Could it ever be said that holding assemblies and covenants was not out of reverence for Heaven?

Duke Huan (Huan Gong 桓公) thereupon bound the sacrificial victim without slaughtering it and placed the covenant text upon it, reiterating the five prohibitions: as for rectifying the fundamental bonds and constant virtues and employing worthy talents—the means by which the ruler of a state exalts his family and state—these were raised in the first and second injunctions; ordering precedence between elder and younger and giving weight to punishments and rewards—the means by which the ruler of a state clarifies governance—these were reiterated in the third and fourth injunctions; and as for maintaining harmony with neighboring states and the conferring of noble ranks, these too were repeatedly and earnestly admonished, set forth in detail in the fifth injunction. Although this was where the canons of Heaven resided, it was also because men had their hearts set upon moral principles and sought to manifest and rectify them. Could it ever be said that laws and prohibitions cannot regulate men? The strictness of the five injunctions moved things like the wind; the law of the one true king was like the sun at mid-sky. The great duty of ministers and sons was thereby fulfilled, the commands and orders of the realm were entirely renewed, and Duke Huan's achievement in supporting and upholding King Xiang (Xiang Wang 襄王) thus reached its height!

Because the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋) sought to display the prohibitions of the Son of Heaven, it recorded the exact day in full to chronicle the reality; because it sought to manifest the principle of honoring the king, it recorded the place in full to make illustrious its beauty. That Confucius (Zhongni 仲尼) praised his "uniting and rectifying all under Heaven" and Mencius (Mengzi 孟子) commended this assembly as the most magnificent—truly there was good reason for it!

Alas! Admirable it was indeed, yet to call it perfectly good is not yet warranted. Moreover, had Duke Huan maintained this mind from beginning to end, how do we know he would not have attained the Kingly Way? Why was it that once his original commitment shifted, his accomplishments suddenly changed: his diligence in walling Qi 杞 did not match his walling of Xing 邢; his army to rescue Xu 徐 was more remiss than in rescuing Xu 許; when Huang 黃 was attacked he showed no concern, and his deliberations on Zeng 鄫 came to naught, so that the achievements of thirty years were swept away in a single morning! When former Confucians took the entry here as praising his flourishing while lamenting his decline, how could that be without meaning? Mencius said: "He who uses force while borrowing the name of benevolence is a hegemon." When I observe Duke Huan, I all the more…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
信
晉人及姜戎敗秦于殽晉人敗狄于箕
晉人陳人鄭人伐許〔並僖公三十三年〕及晉處父
盟〔文公二年〕秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕晉侯伐秦〔文公四年〕
李之尚
同考試官教諭顏批場中作此題者率多臆度
分截不明有專責晉者有予晉退三強者又有責晉
辱魯而善秦改誓者殊失春秋畧晉責秦之㫖惟此篇
一據胡傳斷制詳切宜表而出之
===
考試官修撰劉批聖人以常情待晉襄王事責秦
穆此作按據以定二伯之得失可謂有見矣
考試官左庶子黎批春秋據傳命題易識認難為文
字若主司以巳意命題難揣摩可以泛說雖然傳者大匠之規矩
也舍此無依據矣此題有胡傳惟此作得之詞氣亦佳其深於
經者乎
春秋於晉秦也原其所行之事異其所責之詞
此所以於晉則書爵而於秦則書人也春秋書
法何其嚴歟且晉襄秦穆勢均力敵所行之事
punctuated:
信。

「晉人及姜戎敗秦于殽」、「晉人敗狄于箕」、「晉人、陳人、鄭人伐許」〔並僖公三十三年〕、「及晉處父盟」〔文公二年〕、「秦人伐晉」〔文公三年〕、「晉侯伐秦」〔文公四年〕。

李之尚。

同考試官教諭顏批：場中作此題者，率多臆度，分截不明。有專責晉者，有予晉退三強者，又有責晉辱魯而善秦改誓者，殊失《春秋》畧晉責秦之㫖。惟此篇一據《胡傳》，斷制詳切，宜表而出之。

考試官修撰劉批：聖人以常情待晉襄，王事責秦穆。此作按據以定二伯之得失，可謂有見矣。

考試官左庶子黎批：《春秋》據《傳》命題，易識認，難為文字；若主司以巳意命題，難揣摩，可以泛說。雖然，《傳》者，大匠之規矩也，舍此無依據矣。此題有《胡傳》，惟此作得之，詞氣亦佳，其深於經者乎！

《春秋》於晉、秦也，原其所行之事，異其所責之詞，此所以於晉則書爵，而於秦則書人也。《春秋》書法，何其嚴歟！且晉襄、秦穆，勢均力敵，所行之事，
translation_en:
…convinced of this.

"The men of Jin and the Jiang Rong defeated Qin at Yao"; "The men of Jin defeated the Di at Ji"; "The men of Jin, the men of Chen, and the men of Zheng attacked Xu" [all thirty-third year of Duke Xi]; "[The Duke] made a covenant with Chufu of Jin" [second year of Duke Wen]; "The men of Qin attacked Jin" [third year of Duke Wen]; "The Marquis of Jin attacked Qin" [fourth year of Duke Wen].

By Li Zhishang 李之尚.

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Yan 顏: Those in the examination hall who wrote on this topic generally indulged in much conjecture, and their division of the passages was unclear. Some exclusively blamed Jin, some praised Jin for repelling three strong powers, and others blamed Jin for humiliating Lu while commending Qin for reforming through its oath—all of which completely missed the Spring and Autumn Annals' (Chunqiu) purport of passing lightly over Jin while holding Qin to account. Only this essay relies entirely on Hu Anguo's Commentary (Huzhuan); its judgments are detailed and incisive, and it ought to be singled out for publication.

Comment by Examiner and Senior Compiler Liu 劉: The Sage judged Duke Xiang of Jin by ordinary human standards, while holding Duke Mu of Qin accountable to the standards of kingly affairs. This essay examines the textual basis to determine the merits and faults of the two hegemons; it can truly be said to show insight.

Comment by Examiner and Left Mentor of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent Li 黎: When a Spring and Autumn Annals topic is set directly from the Commentary, it is easy to recognize the theme, yet difficult to compose the essay; whereas if the examiners set a topic by combining passages according to their own ideas, it is difficult to fathom their intent, yet one can write in broad generalities. Even so, the Commentary is the master artisan's compass and square; if one sets it aside, there is nothing to rely upon. This topic is directly addressed in Hu's Commentary, and this essay alone has grasped it. Its diction and spirit are also fine—surely the author is one deeply versed in the Classic!

In its treatment of Jin and Qin, the Spring and Autumn Annals examines the deeds they performed and differentiates the wording with which it reproves them; this is why, in the case of Jin, it records the ruler's title of nobility, whereas in the case of Qin, it merely records "men." How strict indeed is the historiographical method of the Spring and Autumn Annals! Moreover, Duke Xiang of Jin and Duke Mu of Qin were evenly matched in power and strength, and the deeds they performed…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
□相等也春秋果何以異其所責之詞耶盖晋
襄自嗣伯以来首焉忘親背惠以敗秦于殽繼
焉墨衰即戎以敗狄于箕問許黨楚既偕陳鄭
以肆伐責魯不朝又縱處父以抗盟晋襄之所
行專事威力矣秦穆自敗殽之後悔過自誓深
懲既往之失增脩德政冀新將来之善勇夫媚
嫉絶之而弗貴良士彦聖親之而弗遠秦穆之
於過庶幾能改矣夫以秦穆之悔過脩德吾方
以王事責之使能堅矢其心慎終如始不亦賢
===
乎柰何耻敗之念猶存伐晋之兵遽起始則濟
河而焚舟終取王官以及郊借曰晋讐在所必
報然懲忿之心蔑矣其如前日之誓何春秋於
秦伐晋貶而稱人者非嚴也責其所可責耳傳
曰春秋以王事責秦穆其是之謂歟以晋襄之
逞威尚力吾固以常情待之使或櫜弓戢矢休
兵息民不亦善乎胡乃亟戰而不知戢毒衆而
不暇顧遂自將以臨秦竟窮兵而圍邑雖曰秦
怨在所當報然黷武之心甚矣其如民力之困
punctuated: □相等也，春秋果何以異其所責之詞耶？盖晋襄自嗣伯以来，首焉忘親背惠，以敗秦于殽；繼焉墨衰即戎，以敗狄于箕。問許黨楚，既偕陳、鄭以肆伐；責魯不朝，又縱處父以抗盟。晋襄之所行，專事威力矣。秦穆自敗殽之後，悔過自誓，深懲既往之失，增脩德政，冀新將来之善。勇夫媚嫉，絶之而弗貴；良士彦聖，親之而弗遠。秦穆之於過，庶幾能改矣。夫以秦穆之悔過脩德，吾方以王事責之，使能堅矢其心，慎終如始，不亦賢乎？柰何耻敗之念猶存，伐晋之兵遽起。始則濟河而焚舟，終取王官以及郊。借曰晋讐在所必報，然懲忿之心蔑矣，其如前日之誓何？春秋於秦伐晋貶而稱人者，非嚴也，責其所可責耳。傳曰：「春秋以王事責秦穆。」其是之謂歟！以晋襄之逞威尚力，吾固以常情待之，使或櫜弓戢矢，休兵息民，不亦善乎？胡乃亟戰而不知戢，毒衆而不暇顧，遂自將以臨秦，竟窮兵而圍邑。雖曰秦怨在所當報，然黷武之心甚矣，其如民力之困
translation_en:
… [?] are equal; why indeed did the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) differentiate the wording of its censure?

This is because Duke Xiang of Jin (Jin Xiang), ever since inheriting the hegemony, first forgot his father's mourning and betrayed past kindness by defeating Qin at Xiao; next he dyed his mourning garments black to go to war, defeating the Di at Ji. Calling Xu to account for siding with Chu, he joined Chen and Zheng in launching an unbridled campaign; reproaching Lu for failing to pay court, he further allowed Chufu to stand as an equal in a covenant. What Duke Xiang of Jin practiced was exclusively the pursuit of coercive force.

Duke Mu of Qin (Qin Mu), after the defeat at Xiao, repented of his faults and made a solemn oath to himself, deeply chastened by his past mistakes, and increasingly cultivated virtuous governance in hopes of renewing good conduct in the future. Brave men and jealous flatterers [reading 媚嫉 for 娼嫉], he cut off and did not prize; worthy gentlemen and accomplished sages, he drew close and did not keep at a distance. With respect to his faults, Duke Mu of Qin was nearly able to reform.

Now, given that Duke Mu of Qin repented of his faults and cultivated virtue, one would just then hold him to the standard of kingly affairs. Had he been able to firmly swear his heart to it and be as careful at the end as at the beginning, would he not have been worthy? Why then did the thought of shame over his defeat still linger, so that troops to attack Jin were suddenly raised? At first he crossed the Yellow River and burned his boats; in the end he took Wangguan and reached Jiao. Even if one says that the feud with Jin had to be avenged, his resolve to restrain his anger had vanished—what then became of his oath of the former day? That the Spring and Autumn Annals downgraded Qin in its attack on Jin and referred to him merely as "men [of Qin]" (ren) was not out of harshness; it was simply holding to account one who was worthy of being held to account. The commentary says: "The Spring and Autumn Annals held Duke Mu of Qin to the standard of kingly affairs." Is this not what is meant?

Given that Duke Xiang of Jin indulged in coercion and prized force, one naturally treated him according to ordinary human standards. Had he perhaps cased his bows and gathered in his arrows, resting his troops and giving respite to the people, would it not have been good? Why then did he rush into battle without knowing how to desist, bringing misery upon the multitudes without sparing a thought for them, thereupon leading his army in person to march against Qin and ultimately exhausting his military might to besiege its towns? Even though it might be said that the grievance against Qin ought to be repaid, his bellicose heart was extreme—what then of the exhaustion of the people's strength…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
何春秋於晉襄伐秦直書其爵者非恕也以其
不足責耳傳曰春秋以常情待晉襄其斯之謂
歟抑晉襄之徇私逞忿負勇好戰不必言矣彼
秦穆之貳過雖為可責然自是見伐不報始能
踐自誓之言其善又可知矣噫此夫子取之以
繼四代之書曾子傳大學引之以釋平天下章
也歟
禮記
凡三王教世子必以禮樂樂所以脩內也
===
禮所以脩外也禮樂交錯於中發形於外
是故其成也懌恭敬而温文立太傅少傅
以養之欲其知父子君臣之道也
吳裕
同考試官訓導宋批題雖二節意實相貫他
卷槩泛說獨此作體認真切筆三王教世子之心宛然在目
考試官修撰劉批詞理簡明亦素有講貫者
考試官左庶子黎批禮樂教之之道苟非教之之人
則道不虛行此篇與題意合
punctuated:
何？《春秋》於晉襄伐秦，直書其爵者，非恕也，以其不足責耳。《傳》曰：「《春秋》以常情待晉襄。」其斯之謂歟！抑晉襄之徇私逞忿、負勇好戰，不必言矣；彼秦穆之貳過，雖為可責，然自是見伐不報，始能踐自誓之言，其善又可知矣。噫！此夫子取之以繼四代之書，曾子傳《大學》，引之以釋平天下章也歟！

《禮記》
凡三王教世子，必以禮樂。樂所以脩內也，禮所以脩外也。禮樂交錯於中，發形於外，是故其成也懌，恭敬而温文。立太傅、少傅以養之，欲其知父子、君臣之道也。
吳裕
同考試官訓導宋批：題雖二節，意實相貫。他卷槩泛說，獨此作體認真切，筆三王教世子之心，宛然在目。
考試官修撰劉批：詞理簡明，亦素有講貫者。
考試官左庶子黎批：禮樂，教之之道；苟非教之之人，則道不虛行。此篇與題意合。
translation_en:
… [what of] the exhaustion of the people's strength? When the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) directly records Duke Xiang of Jin's (晉襄) title in his invasion of Qin, it is not out of leniency, but simply because he is not worth reproaching. The Commentary (Zhuan) says: "The Spring and Autumn Annals treats Xiang of Jin according to ordinary human passions." Is this not what it means? Now, there is no need to speak of Xiang of Jin indulging his private desires, giving vent to his anger, relying on bravery, and loving warfare. As for Duke Mu of Qin (秦穆) repeating his transgression, although he deserves reproach, yet from this point on, when attacked he did not retaliate, finally fulfilling the words of his own oath; thus his goodness can also be known. Alas! Is this not why the Master selected it to append to the documents of the Four Dynasties, and why Master Zeng (Zengzi 曾子), in transmitting the Great Learning (Daxue), cited it to explain the chapter on bringing peace to the world?

Record of Rites (Liji)
"In all cases, when the Three Kings taught their heirs apparent, it was必ず by means of ritual and music. Music is that by which the interior is cultivated; ritual is that by which the exterior is cultivated. Ritual and music interpenetrate within and manifest in form without; therefore, when his character is achieved, he is harmonious and joyful, respectful, reverent, gentle, and refined. They established the Grand Mentor and Junior Mentor to nurture him, wishing him to know the way of father and son, ruler and minister."
Wu Yu 吳裕
Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Assistant Instructor: Although the topic consists of two passages, their meaning actually runs through as one. Other papers generally spoke vaguely; this composition alone grasps the meaning earnestly and closely, and in writing out the mind of the Three Kings in teaching the heir apparent, makes it vividly present before the eyes.
Comment by Examiner Liu, Senior Compiler: The diction and reasoning are concise and clear; this is someone who has long been thoroughly versed in the subject.
Comment by Examiner Li, Left Mentor of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent: Ritual and music are the Way of teaching him; yet without the men to teach him, the Way does not operate in a vacuum. This essay accords with the meaning of the topic.

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
先王之於世子也不惟設教以成其德性尤必
立官以教之倫理夫德性成而後倫理可明也
先王之於世子既設禮樂之教而復立輔導之
官豈無其意也歟文王世子記此謂夫世子居
儲貳之位將繼世而有天下者也三王教之果
何道哉曰禮樂而已教之以樂使習夫絃誦之
音羽籥之舞以消融其邪慝之蘊脩於內也教
之以禮使習夫祭祀之儀養老之容以陶成其
恭肅之儀脩於外也然禮固脩外矣而亦達於
===
中樂固脩內矣而亦達於外禮樂二者醺醲涵
暢相與無間由是懌然懽忻愉悅之意動于中
藹然恭敬溫文之氣形于外而德性成矣德性
既成而倫理不可以不明故又立太傅少傅之
官以養之焉太傅在前從容啓迪養其本然之
善少傅在後優游審喻詳其固有之理彼其曰
慈曰孝為人父為人子之道也而開悟之使無
不明曰仁曰敬為人君為人臣之道也而薰陶
之使無不知則倫理明矣德性既成倫理既明
punctuated: 先王之於世子也，不惟設教以成其德性，尤必立官以教之倫理。夫德性成，而後倫理可明也。先王之於世子，既設禮樂之教，而復立輔導之官，豈無其意也歟？《文王世子》記此，謂夫世子居儲貳之位，將繼世而有天下者也。三王教之，果何道哉？曰：禮樂而已。教之以樂，使習夫絃誦之音、羽籥之舞，以消融其邪慝之蘊，脩於內也；教之以禮，使習夫祭祀之儀、養老之容，以陶成其恭肅之儀，脩於外也。然禮固脩外矣，而亦達於中；樂固脩內矣，而亦達於外。禮樂二者，醺醲涵暢，相與無間。由是懌然懽忻愉悅之意動于中，藹然恭敬溫文之氣形于外，而德性成矣。德性既成，而倫理不可以不明，故又立太傅、少傅之官以養之焉。太傅在前，從容啓迪，養其本然之善；少傅在後，優游審喻，詳其固有之理。彼其曰慈、曰孝，為人父、為人子之道也，而開悟之使無不明；曰仁、曰敬，為人君、為人臣之道也，而薰陶之使無不知，則倫理明矣。德性既成，倫理既明，
translation_en:
In dealing with the heir apparent, the former kings not only established instruction to perfect his moral nature, but also unfailingly appointed officials to teach him the moral principles of human relations. For only after his moral nature is perfected can the principles of human relations be made clear. Since the former kings, with respect to the heir apparent, both established instruction in rites and music and further appointed officials to guide and assist him, how could this have been without purpose?

The chapter "King Wen as Heir Apparent" (Wen Wang shizi) records this, meaning that the heir apparent occupies the position of designated successor and is one who in a succeeding generation will possess All under Heaven. By what Way, indeed, did the Three Kings instruct him? One may say: by rites and music alone. They instructed him in music, causing him to practice the sounds of stringed instruments and recitation and the dances with feathers and flutes, so as to melt away any hidden evil or perversity—this was cultivation within. They instructed him in rites, causing him to practice the ceremonies of sacrifice and the deportment of caring for the aged, so as to mold his respectful and solemn bearing—this was cultivation without. Yet while rites assuredly cultivate the exterior, they also penetrate within; while music assuredly cultivates the interior, it also reaches without. The two—rites and music—steep and saturate him like rich wine, working together without interruption. Thereby, a joyful, happy, and pleased disposition stirs within, while an affable, respectful, reverent, gentle, and refined aura takes form without, and his moral nature is perfected.

Once his moral nature is perfected, the principles of human relations cannot remain unclear; therefore, they also established the offices of Grand Mentor (taifu) and Junior Mentor (shaofu) to nurture him. The Grand Mentor goes before him, unhurriedly enlightening and guiding him so as to nurture his inherent goodness; the Junior Mentor follows behind him, leisurely and carefully explaining things so as to make clear in detail the principles native to him. As for what are called kindness and filiality—the Way of being a father and of being a son—they awaken him to these so that nothing remains unclear; as for what are called benevolence and reverence—the Way of being a ruler and of being a minister—they steep and mold him in these so that nothing remains unknown. Thus the principles of human relations are made clear. Once his moral nature is perfected and the principles of human relations are made clear,…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
君天下之道且基于此而况為世子者哉抑此
篇為教世子而作上文自春夏學以下皆言教
世子之道也此自立太傅少傅以下皆言教世
子之人也盖道非人無以行人非道無以教三
王之教世子能兼舉而不偏廢是宜後之子孫
宜君宜王而享國祚於無窮也歟
是故天時有生也地理有宜也人官有能
也物曲有利也
張達
===
同考試官訓導朱批本房百十餘卷以制禮作
者過半偶得此篇原記者本意攟摭成章非出入二戴者
不能也
考試官修撰劉批以禮順天地人物之宜立說不戾
經肯
考試官左庶子黎批四者在觀會通行典禮之後是
作能知之而詞亦簡明
造化人物各有所宜非通於禮者不能順也盖
禮貴順於天地人物而已矣苟非其生養材利
punctuated:
君天下之道且基于此，而况為世子者哉？抑此篇為教世子而作，上文自「春夏學」以下，皆言教世子之道也；此自「立太傅、少傅」以下，皆言教世子之人也。盖道非人無以行，人非道無以教。三王之教世子，能兼舉而不偏廢，是宜後之子孫宜君宜王，而享國祚於無窮也歟！

「是故天時有生也，地理有宜也，人官有能也，物曲有利也。」

張達

同考試官訓導朱批：本房百十餘卷，以制禮作者過半，偶得此篇，原記者本意，攟摭成章，非出入二戴者不能也。
考試官修撰劉批：以禮順天地人物之宜立說，不戾經肯。
考試官左庶子黎批：四者在觀會通行典禮之後，是作能知之，而詞亦簡明。

造化、人物各有所宜，非通於禮者不能順也。盖禮貴順於天地、人物而已矣，苟非其生養、材利
translation_en:
… the Way of ruling All under Heaven as sovereign is grounded in this—how much more so for one who is the Heir Apparent! Moreover, this chapter was composed on the subject of educating the Heir Apparent. The preceding passage from "studying in spring and summer" onward all speaks of the Way of educating the Heir Apparent; this passage from "establishing the Grand Mentor and Junior Mentor" onward all speaks of the personnel who educate the Heir Apparent. Indeed, without the right people, the Way cannot be put into practice; without the Way, those people have nothing whereby to teach. Because the Three Kings, in educating their Heirs Apparent, were able to attend to both together without neglecting either, was it not fitting that their descendants in later generations were worthy to be sovereigns and kings, enjoying the blessings of the realm without end!

"Therefore, the seasons of Heaven have their generative cycles, the configurations of Earth have their suitabilities, human offices have their capabilities, and the varied forms of things have their utilities." [Record of Rites, "Liqi"]

Zhang Da 張達

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhu 朱: Among the more than one hundred and ten papers in this examination ward, over half treated the topic in terms of instituting the rites. Happening upon this essay, I found that it traces the original intent of the compiler of the Record, gathering materials into a coherent composition—something only one thoroughly versed in the Elder and Younger Dai's ritual texts (Er Dai 二戴) could achieve.
Comment by Examiner and Senior Compiler Liu 劉: Establishing its thesis on how the rites accord with what is suitable to Heaven, Earth, human beings, and things, it does not contravene the purport of the Classic [reading 肯 as 旨].
Comment by Examiner and Left Mentor of the Secretariat of the Heir Apparent Li 黎: These four matters follow after observing the convergence and continuity of principles and putting the canons of ritual into practice; this composition understands that, and its diction is also concise and clear.

Nature's creative processes, human beings, and things each have what is suitable to them; none who is not thoroughly versed in the rites can accord with them. Indeed, the rites value nothing more than according with Heaven, Earth, human beings, and things. If it does not accord with what is suitable to their generation and nourishment, their capacities and utilities…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之所宜夫豈可以為禮哉何則禮非財物不可
行也而其財物非天時地理豈能生養之乎盖
天時謂春夏秋冬陰陽寒暖之不齊而其所生
之品彙亦隨時而異如韭麥生於春夏黍稻生
於秋冬取之當合其時而順天之所宜焉地理
謂山林川澤高下燥濕之不一而其所產之財
利亦隨地而殊如麋豕產於山林魚鼈產於川
澤取之當因其理而順地之所宜焉夫天時地
理既順之如此而人官物曲又可不順乎盖人
===
官有能謂助祭執事之官各有所能當因任其
能而不廢如宗祝能知禮則任以宣祝嘏樂師
能知樂則任以辨聲詩而順人之所宜矣物曲
有利謂物之材質委曲各有所利也當曲成其
利而不遺如麴櫱利為酒醴則用之以成味桐
竹利為琴笙則用之以成音而有以順物之所
宜矣夫順天地人物之所宜以為禮非禮之會
通孰能與於此哉抑此推言上文禮也者合於
天時至理萬物之義然上言順於鬼神合於人
punctuated: 之所宜，夫豈可以為禮哉？何則？禮非財物不可行也，而其財物非天時地理，豈能生養之乎？盖天時謂春夏秋冬、陰陽寒暖之不齊，而其所生之品彙亦隨時而異。如韭麥生於春夏，黍稻生於秋冬，取之當合其時，而順天之所宜焉。地理謂山林川澤、高下燥濕之不一，而其所產之財利亦隨地而殊。如麋豕產於山林，魚鼈產於川澤，取之當因其理，而順地之所宜焉。夫天時地理既順之如此，而人官物曲又可不順乎？盖人官有能，謂助祭執事之官各有所能，當因任其能而不廢。如宗祝能知禮，則任以宣祝嘏；樂師能知樂，則任以辨聲詩，而順人之所宜矣。物曲有利，謂物之材質委曲各有所利也，當曲成其利而不遺。如麴櫱利為酒醴，則用之以成味；桐竹利為琴笙，則用之以成音，而有以順物之所宜矣。夫順天地人物之所宜以為禮，非禮之會通，孰能與於此哉？抑此推言上文「禮也者，合於天時」至「理萬物」之義。然上言「順於鬼神，合於人
translation_en:
…what is appropriate to them, how could it be taken as ritual? Why is this? Ritual cannot be practiced without resources and goods, and how could those resources and goods be produced and nourished without the seasons of heaven and the principles of the earth? Now, "the seasons of heaven" refers to the variations of spring, summer, autumn, and winter, and of yin and yang, cold and warmth; the categories of things they bring forth likewise differ according to the season. For instance, leeks and wheat grow in spring and summer, while millet and rice grow in autumn and winter; in gathering them, one must match their proper season, thereby conforming to what is appropriate to heaven. "The principles of the earth" refers to the differences among mountains, forests, streams, and marshes, and between high and low, dry and wet; the resources and utilities they yield likewise vary according to the terrain. For instance, elk and swine are produced in mountains and forests, while fish and soft-shelled turtles are produced in streams and marshes; in taking them, one must follow their terrestrial principles, thereby conforming to what is appropriate to the earth.

Since the seasons of heaven and the principles of the earth are conformed to in this manner, how could one fail to conform as well to human offices and the particularities of things? Now, "human offices have their capabilities" means that the officers who assist in sacrifices and manage affairs each possess their own capabilities, and one ought to assign them duties according to those capabilities without letting them go unused. For instance, if the liturgists and invocators understand ritual, they are entrusted with proclaiming the prayers and blessings; if the music masters understand music, they are entrusted with distinguishing the musical airs and odes—thus conforming to what is appropriate to human beings. "The particularities of things have their utilities" means that the material qualities of things, in all their intricate particularities, each have their own utility, and one ought to bring those utilities to nuanced completion without overlooking any. For instance, since leaven and sprouted grain are suited for making fermented and sweet wines, they are used to perfect flavors; since paulownia wood and bamboo are suited for making zithers and mouth-organs, they are used to perfect musical sounds—thus having the means to conform to what is appropriate to things.

Indeed, to practice ritual by conforming to what is appropriate to heaven, earth, human beings, and things—who could participate in this without a comprehensive mastery of ritual? Furthermore, this extends and elaborates the meaning of the preceding passage, from "Ritual is that which accords with the seasons of heaven" down to "orders the myriad things." Yet whereas the preceding text speaks of "conforming to ghosts and spirits, and according with human…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
心而止曰人官有能則是特言人之為成材而
不及於鬼神者何也人者鬼神之所依言人則
見鬼神矣况欲鬼神之饗而不順天地人物之
所宜豈可得乎此又行禮君子所當知
論
大哉堯之為君
馬中錫
同考試官訓導賀批立論高見理卓繪後聖
贊前聖之大於觚翰中光焰燁然令人退避三舍
===
同考試官教諭宋批筆力蒼古文勢雄偉有
感慨有抑揚發揮仲尼賛堯之意殆無餘蘊矣
考試官修撰劉批意新筆老夐出衆作場屋中
有此文字亦自可喜况初場已高秋闈首選將屬之子矣
考試官左庶子黎批文章以變為工愈變而愈工
文之至也此論變而不失其正盖文之傑者矧初試已雄於人
可備魁選
論曰舉不可形容之名而歸諸無以有加
之聖人是必立言者有微意矣夫論帝而
punctuated:
心，而止曰「人官有能」，則是特言人之為成材，而不及於鬼神者，何也？人者，鬼神之所依，言人則見鬼神矣。况欲鬼神之饗，而不順天地人物之所宜，豈可得乎？此又行禮君子所當知。

論
大哉堯之為君
馬中錫
同考試官訓導賀批：立論高，見理卓，繪後聖贊前聖之大於觚翰中，光焰燁然，令人退避三舍。
同考試官教諭宋批：筆力蒼古，文勢雄偉，有感慨，有抑揚，發揮仲尼賛堯之意，殆無餘蘊矣。
考試官修撰劉批：意新筆老，夐出衆作。場屋中有此文字，亦自可喜。况初場已高，秋闈首選將屬之子矣。
考試官左庶子黎批：文章以變為工，愈變而愈工，文之至也。此論變而不失其正，盖文之傑者。矧初試已雄於人，可備魁選。

論曰：舉不可形容之名，而歸諸無以有加之聖人，是必立言者有微意矣。夫論帝而
translation_en:
…human heart, yet here it only says that "human offices have their capacities"—speaking specifically of humans as accomplished talents without mentioning spirits and gods—why is this? Humans are those upon whom spirits and gods depend; when one speaks of humans, spirits and gods are thereby manifest. Moreover, if one wishes for the spirits and gods to accept offerings without conforming to what is appropriate for Heaven, Earth, humans, and things, how could that be attained? This too is what the noble man who practices ritual ought to know.

Discourse
"Great indeed was Yao as a sovereign!"
Ma Zhongxi 馬中錫
Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor He 賀: The thesis is lofty and the grasp of principle is outstanding. Depicting the later sage's praise of the former sage's greatness within writing tablets and brush, its brilliance shines forth resplendently, making others retreat three stages in deference.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Song 宋: The brushwork is vigorous and archaic, the momentum of the prose grand and majestic. With deep feeling and rhythmic cadence, it elaborates the meaning of Zhongni's [Confucius's] praise of Yao until virtually nothing is left unexpressed.
Comment by Examiner Senior Compiler Liu 劉: The conception is fresh and the brush seasoned, standing far above the crowd of compositions. To find such writing in the examination compound is in itself a delight. Moreover, since his first-session papers were already superior, first place in the autumn examination hall shall belong to this gentleman!
Comment by Examiner Left Mentor Li 黎: In literature, skill lies in transformation; the more it transforms, the more skillful it becomes—this is the pinnacle of prose. This discourse transforms without losing its orthodoxy; it is truly an outstanding piece of writing. All the more since his first-session examination already surpassed others, he is worthy of being placed at the head of the list.

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
至於堯則人不可以有加為君而至於堯
則道不可以有加於不可有加之上而強
加之以名以極其形容稱賛焉吾固為聖
人喜亦竊為聖人憂是何也高厚不可繪
而細微易以描溟渤不可探而沼沚易以
測不可形容也而務極其形容不可有加
也而復加以稱賛竊恐大之一言有以繪
帝堯之高厚而探帝堯之溟渤也眾人信
之達者疑焉抑孰知大之名一立則小即
===
隨之而無大則亦無小也小大相形世變
之升降繫焉識者不為帝堯憂寧不為世
道憂乎孔子曰大哉堯之為君是以不可
形容之大而賛吾不可有加之神堯也請
發其意前乎堯而有皇斯時也穴居野處
摶生咀華不知所以為大也不知所以為
大安知所以為小乎故庖羲神農黃帝之
世如春而大之名未立後乎堯而有王斯
時也太朴既散元氣已支蓋有所以為大
punctuated: 至於堯，則人不可以有加；為君而至於堯，則道不可以有加。於不可有加之上，而強加之以名，以極其形容稱賛焉，吾固為聖人喜，亦竊為聖人憂。是何也？高厚不可繪，而細微易以描；溟渤不可探，而沼沚易以測。不可形容也，而務極其形容；不可有加也，而復加以稱賛，竊恐「大」之一言，有以繪帝堯之高厚，而探帝堯之溟渤也。眾人信之，達者疑焉。抑孰知大之名一立，則小即隨之，而無大則亦無小也。小大相形，世變之升降繫焉。識者不為帝堯憂，寧不為世道憂乎？孔子曰：「大哉，堯之為君！」是以不可形容之大，而賛吾不可有加之神堯也。請發其意。前乎堯而有皇，斯時也，穴居野處，摶生咀華，不知所以為大也。不知所以為大，安知所以為小乎？故庖羲、神農、黃帝之世如春，而大之名未立。後乎堯而有王，斯時也，太朴既散，元氣已支，蓋有所以為大
translation_en: … reaches Yao, no human being can surpass him; when ruling as a sovereign reaches Yao, the Way cannot be surpassed. To forcibly attach a name onto that which cannot be surpassed, so as to carry its description and praise to the utmost—while I certainly rejoice for the sage, I also privately worry for the sage. Why is this? What is lofty and thick cannot be painted, whereas the minute and subtle are easy to depict; the vast ocean cannot be fathomed, whereas a small pond or islet is easy to measure. When something cannot be described, yet one strives to carry its description to the utmost; when nothing can be added to it, yet one further adds praise to it—I privately fear that this single word "great" might serve to paint the loftiness and thickness of Emperor Yao and fathom the vast ocean of Emperor Yao! The multitude believe it, yet men of penetrating understanding doubt it. Moreover, who knows that once the name of "great" is established, "small" immediately follows it, whereas without "great" there is also no "small"? When small and great are contrasted with one another, the rise and fall of worldly transformations are bound up with them. Even if men of insight do not worry for Emperor Yao, how could they not worry for the Way of the world? Confucius said, "Great indeed was Yao as a sovereign!" By this, he used an indescribable greatness to praise our unsurpassable,神-like (divine) Yao. Allow me to elucidate the meaning of this. Prior to Yao there were the August Ones (Huang). At that time, people dwelt in caves and lived in the wilds, grasping raw things and chewing the fruits and blossoms of plants, not knowing what constituted "great." Not knowing what constituted "great," how could they know what constituted "small"? Therefore, the ages of Paoxi (Fuxi), Shennong, and the Yellow Emperor (Huangdi) were like spring, and the name of "great" was not yet established. Subsequent to Yao there were the Kings (Wang). At that time, the Great Uncarved Block had already dispersed and the primordial vitality had already fragmented, so there was indeed that which constituted "great"…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
矣既有所以為大安知不有所以為小乎
故神禹成湯文武之世如秋而大之名漸
弊有如堯焉以大稱之吾意其仰焉三皇
已不能追其忘言之大化俯焉三王將有
以似其可形之大名矣故以當時為君之
道觀之欽明文思允恭克讓其德大矣然
回視渾渾爾者其何如如天如神如日如
雲其道大矣然仰思噩噩爾者其奚若舟
楫牛馬之制興弧矢門柝之制創所以為
===
民興利除害者大矣然孰若利害之兩忘
井臼宫室之法起上衣下裳之法更所以
為民移風易俗者大矣然孰若風俗之未
變書契之用大矣而結繩之治不可追禮
樂之用大矣而土鼓之風不可復功業雖
大如無功之為愈文章雖大如不文之為
全璞已雕矣而非復在山之時玉已斲矣
而無復在石之日不獨有識者為世道憂
也雖帝堯之心盖亦自將為世道不釋然
punctuated: 矣。既有所以為大，安知不有所以為小乎？故神禹、成湯、文、武之世如秋，而大之名漸弊。有如堯焉，以大稱之，吾意其仰焉三皇，已不能追其忘言之大化；俯焉三王，將有以似其可形之大名矣。故以當時為君之道觀之：欽明文思，允恭克讓，其德大矣，然回視渾渾爾者其何如？如天如神，如日如雲，其道大矣，然仰思噩噩爾者其奚若？舟楫、牛馬之制興，弧矢、門柝之制創，所以為民興利除害者大矣，然孰若利害之兩忘？井臼、宫室之法起，上衣、下裳之法更，所以為民移風易俗者大矣，然孰若風俗之未變？書契之用大矣，而結繩之治不可追；禮樂之用大矣，而土鼓之風不可復。功業雖大，如無功之為愈；文章雖大，如不文之為全。璞已雕矣，而非復在山之時；玉已斲矣，而無復在石之日。不獨有識者為世道憂也，雖帝堯之心，盖亦自將為世道不釋然
translation_en:
… And once there was that by which things were deemed great, how could there not also be that by which things were deemed small? Therefore, the ages of the divine Yu (神禹), Tang the Successful (成湯), and Kings Wen (文) and Wu (武) were like autumn, and the name of "great" gradually deteriorated. When it comes to someone like Yao, who was praised as "great," I think that looking up to the Three Sovereigns, he could no longer recapture their great transformation that needed no words; looking down to the Three Kings, he was about to resemble their describable great renown.

Therefore, if we observe the way of being a ruler in his time: reverent, intelligent, accomplished, and thoughtful, sincerely courteous and capable of yielding—his virtue was great indeed; yet looking back upon that which was simple and undifferentiated, how does it compare? Like heaven and like spirit, like the sun and like the clouds—his Way was great indeed; yet looking up and pondering that which was austere and unadorned, how does it measure up? The institutions of boats and oars, oxen and horses arose, and the institutions of bows and arrows, gates and night-watch clappers were created; that by which benefits were promoted and harms removed for the people was great indeed, yet how could that compare to forgetting both benefit and harm? The methods of wells, mortars, and dwellings arose, and the fashion of upper garments and lower skirts was altered; that by which customs and habits were transformed for the people was great indeed, yet how could that compare to when customs and habits had not yet changed? The use of written contracts was great indeed, yet the governance of knotted cords could no longer be overtaken; the use of rites and music was great indeed, yet the customs of earthen drums could not be restored. Although his achievements were great, it would have been better to have no achievements; although his cultural refinement was great, it would have been more complete to be unrefined. The uncarved gem had already been chiseled, and it was no longer as when it was in the mountain; the jade had already been carved, and the days when it was inside the stone would never return. Not only did men of discernment worry for the Way of the world, even in the mind of Emperor Yao himself, he too must have felt uneasy for the Way of the world…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
也不獨帝堯為世道憂也雖夫子之心盖
亦將為世道不懌然也或者乃曰易不云
乎大哉乾元是夫子嘗以大哉贊乾天矣
今以之而贊堯是不以堯視堯而以天視
堯也奚有於不宜殊不知大易之所贊者
託於有言之天也以有言之天視堯孰愈
於以忘言之天視堯乎斯義也夫子豈為
不知直以世道既降不能不以有言之天
歸諸堯也不歸諸堯何以陋後世之小乎
===
或者又曰大哉孔子是夫子嘗見稱大哉
於達巷矣今以之而贊堯是不以堯視堯
而以已視堯也何有於不可殊不知達巷
之所贊者春秋之仲尼耳以春秋之仲尼
視堯孰愈於以無言之仲尼視堯乎斯義
也夫子豈為不知直以世道既下不能不
以時人之見贊諸堯也不贊諸堯何以鄙
後世之小乎觀夫分裂於春秋縱橫於戰
國為君者非無也不過春秋戰國之君耳
punctuated:
也；不獨帝堯為世道憂也，雖夫子之心，盖亦將為世道不懌然也。
或者乃曰：「《易》不云乎？『大哉乾元！』是夫子嘗以『大哉』贊乾天矣。今以之而贊堯，是不以堯視堯，而以天視堯也，奚有於不宜？」殊不知大《易》之所贊者，託於有言之天也。以有言之天視堯，孰愈於以忘言之天視堯乎？斯義也，夫子豈為不知？直以世道既降，不能不以有言之天歸諸堯也；不歸諸堯，何以陋後世之小乎？
或者又曰：「『大哉孔子！』是夫子嘗見稱『大哉』於達巷矣。今以之而贊堯，是不以堯視堯，而以已視堯也，何有於不可？」殊不知達巷之所贊者，春秋之仲尼耳。以春秋之仲尼視堯，孰愈於以無言之仲尼視堯乎？斯義也，夫子豈為不知？直以世道既下，不能不以時人之見贊諸堯也；不贊諸堯，何以鄙後世之小乎？
觀夫分裂於春秋，縱橫於戰國，為君者非無也，不過春秋、戰國之君耳，
translation_en:
… And it was not only Emperor Yao who worried for the Way of the world; even the heart of the Master [Confucius] must also have felt ill at ease for the Way of the world.
Someone might say: "Does the Book of Changes (Yi) not say, 'Great indeed is the originating power of Qian [Heaven]!'? Thus the Master once praised Heaven with the words 'Great indeed!' Now, to use these same words to praise Yao is to view Yao not merely as Yao, but as Heaven—how could that be inappropriate?" Yet they fail to realize that what the great Book of Changes praises is entrusted to a Heaven that speaks through words. How could viewing Yao as a Heaven of words be better than viewing Yao as a Heaven that forgets words? Could the Master have been unaware of this principle? It was simply because the Way of the world had already declined that he could not help attributing the Heaven of words to Yao; for if he did not attribute it to Yao, how could he expose the pettiness of later ages?
Someone else might say: "'Great indeed is Confucius!' Thus the Master himself was once praised as 'Great indeed!' by the villager of Daxiang. Now, to use these words to praise Yao is to view Yao not merely as Yao, but as he himself was viewed—how could that be impermissible?" Yet they fail to realize that what the villager of Daxiang praised was merely the Zhongni [Confucius] of the Spring and Autumn period. How could viewing Yao through the Zhongni of the Spring and Autumn period be better than viewing Yao through the wordless Zhongni? Could the Master have been unaware of this principle? It was simply because the Way of the world had already fallen that he could not help praising Yao according to the perspective of the people of his time; for if he did not praise Yao thus, how could he disdain the pettiness of later ages?
Observe how, amidst the fragmentation of the Spring and Autumn period and the shifting alliances of the Warring States period, it was not that there were no rulers, yet they were nothing more than rulers of the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, …

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
如堯之大者誰耶混一於漢唐平定於晉
宋為君者非無也不過漢唐晉宋之君耳
如堯之大者誰耶夫春秋之時不足道也
而如漢如唐特帝王之卷石耳以卷石而
見山嶽之大則其大可知以漢唐而較帝
堯之大堯之大豈應如是乎戰國之時不
足數也而若晉若宋特帝王之培塿耳以
培塿而見丘陵之大則其大可想以晉宋
而較帝堯之大堯之大豈應若此乎然則
===
夫子以大哉贊帝堯者豈其本意哉盖不
得已而贊之也亦不得已而不贊之也夫
子之微意豈不端在是乎雖然以堯視大
固為未足以眾人視之則弗勝其大也故
當時百姓昭明明此大也黎民於變變此
大也康衢之謠謠此大也擊壤之歌歌此
大也舜禹皐陶保此大之家相也殳斨伯
與分此大之百職也上承三皇以此大而
承也下啓三王以此大而啓也巢由囿於
punctuated: 如堯之大者誰耶？混一於漢、唐，平定於晉、宋，為君者非無也，不過漢、唐、晉、宋之君耳，如堯之大者誰耶？夫春秋之時，不足道也；而如漢、如唐，特帝王之卷石耳。以卷石而見山嶽之大，則其大可知；以漢、唐而較帝堯之大，堯之大豈應如是乎？戰國之時，不足數也；而若晉、若宋，特帝王之培塿耳。以培塿而見丘陵之大，則其大可想；以晉、宋而較帝堯之大，堯之大豈應若此乎？然則夫子以「大哉」贊帝堯者，豈其本意哉？盖不得已而贊之也，亦不得已而不贊之也。夫子之微意，豈不端在是乎？雖然，以堯視大，固為未足；以眾人視之，則弗勝其大也。故當時百姓昭明，明此大也；黎民於變，變此大也；康衢之謠，謠此大也；擊壤之歌，歌此大也；舜、禹、皐陶，保此大之家相也；殳斨、伯與，分此大之百職也。上承三皇，以此大而承也；下啓三王，以此大而啓也。巢、由囿於
translation_en: …who had the greatness of Yao? Among those who unified the realm in the Han and Tang, or pacified it in the Jin and Song, it is not that there were no rulers, yet they were merely rulers of the Han, Tang, Jin, and Song—who among them had the greatness of Yao? Now, the Spring and Autumn period is not worth mentioning, and even dynasties like the Han and Tang were merely a fist-sized stone among emperors and kings. If one views the greatness of sacred peaks from the perspective of a fist-sized stone, their greatness can be known; yet if one measures the greatness of Emperor Yao against the Han and Tang, how could Yao's greatness merely be like that? The Warring States period is not worth counting, and even dynasties like the Jin and Song were merely a small mound among emperors and kings. If one views the greatness of hills and highlands from the perspective of a small mound, their greatness can be imagined; yet if one measures the greatness of Emperor Yao against the Jin and Song, how could Yao's greatness merely be like this? If so, then when the Master praised Emperor Yao with the words "Great indeed!", how could that have been his original intent? For he praised him only because he had no choice, just as he also had no choice but to refrain from praising him further. Does the Master's subtle intent not lie precisely in this? Even so, if one views "greatness" from the perspective of Yao himself, the word is certainly inadequate; yet if one views him from the perspective of the multitude, his greatness is more than they can fathom. Thus, in that era, when the hundred surnames became brightly distinguished, it was this greatness that they made bright; when the black-haired people were transformed, it was by this greatness that they were transformed; the ballad of the highroad sang of this greatness; the song of striking the clods chanted of this greatness. Shun, Yu, and Gao Yao were the chief ministers who preserved this greatness; Shu Qiang and Bo Yu were the various officials who shared the duties of this greatness. Above, he succeeded the Three August Ones, and it was with this greatness that he succeeded them; below, he opened the way for the Three Kings, and it was with this greatness that he opened the way for them. Chao Fu and Xu You were encompassed within…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
此大而自外之工鯀安於此大而自逆之
而帝堯為君之大自如也故孔子以聖契
聖曰大哉堯之為君若
今日之
聖天子則蕩蕩乎民無能名焉愚何足以知其
大謹論
同前
邢旭
同考試官教諭陳批此篇議論英發詞氣
婉曲深得論體宜録出以範後學
同考試官教諭章批議論層疊孔子賛堯之
意宛然可見非稚筆所能
考試官修撰劉批此論頗平實故併録之
考試官左庶子黎批是規矩文字
論曰於難形容者而形容之此聖人能知
聖人也盖易於形容者不若難於形容者
之為盛也易於形容者有迹之可名德之
小者也難於形容者無迹之可名德之大
punctuated:
此大而自外之，工鯀安於此大而自逆之，而帝堯為君之大自如也。故孔子以聖契聖曰：「大哉堯之為君！」若今日之聖天子，則蕩蕩乎民無能名焉，愚何足以知其大！謹論。

同前
邢旭
同考試官教諭陳批：此篇議論英發，詞氣婉曲，深得論體，宜録出以範後學。
同考試官教諭章批：議論層疊，孔子賛堯之意宛然可見，非稚筆所能。
考試官修撰劉批：此論頗平實，故併録之。
考試官左庶子黎批：是規矩文字。

論曰：於難形容者而形容之，此聖人能知聖人也。盖易於形容者，不若難於形容者之為盛也。易於形容者，有迹之可名，德之小者也；難於形容者，無迹之可名，德之大
translation_en:
… [Chao Fu and Xu You were encompassed within] this greatness and yet kept themselves aloof from it; Gonggong and Gun rested in this greatness and yet set themselves against it. Nevertheless, the greatness of Emperor Yao as a ruler remained completely unchanged. Therefore Confucius, as one sage corresponding in spirit with another sage, said: "Great indeed was Yao as a ruler!" As for the Sacred Son of Heaven of today, how vast is his virtue, so that the people can find no name for it! How could someone as foolish as I suffice to know his greatness? I respectfully submit this discourse.

Same topic as the preceding
Xing Xu 邢旭
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Chen 陳: The argumentation in this piece is spirited and vigorous, and its tone is nuanced and supple. It deeply grasps the style of the discourse (lun) genre and ought to be copied out as a model for later students.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Zhang 章: The arguments unfold layer upon layer, making Confucius's intention in praising Yao vividly apparent. This is not something an immature brush could achieve.
Comment by Examiner Senior Compiler (xiuzhuan) Liu 劉: This discourse is quite plain and solid; therefore it is recorded alongside the previous one.
Comment by Examiner Left Mentor of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent (zuo shuzi) Li 黎: This is a composition that adheres well to standard rules.

The discourse reads: To give description to that which is difficult to describe—this is how a sage is able to truly know a sage. For that which is easy to describe is not as grand as that which is difficult to describe. What is easy to describe has visible traces that can be named, and is a lesser virtue; what is difficult to describe has no visible traces that can be named, and is a great [virtue]…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
者也惟其為德之大所以民沾其澤人囿
於化渾渾乎噩噩乎非言語之可陳非繪
畫之可狀如天之大物蒙其生成而不知
其所以生成者誰之功物賴其長養而不
識其所以長養者誰之力此其所以為難
形容者歟孔子曰大哉堯之為君其善於
形容者矣愚請申之三皇以道而化民乾
坤之於屯蒙也民皆知其道矣謂之太古
則可謂之大哉則未焉三王以功而勸民
===
大旱之於雲霓也民皆知其功矣謂之盡
美則可謂之大哉亦未焉至於五伯以力
而率民桔橰之於夏畦也民皆知其力矣
謂之小補則可謂之大哉又豈可乎然則
大哉之稱舍堯之為君其誰當之堯之德
本不可名矣強而名之曰大哉亦名其所
不可名者也是故欽明文思安安德之得
於天者大也允恭克讓德之見於行者大
也莫大於四表被于四表者此德之大莫
punctuated: 者也。惟其為德之大，所以民沾其澤，人囿於化，渾渾乎、噩噩乎，非言語之可陳，非繪畫之可狀。如天之大，物蒙其生成而不知其所以生成者誰之功，物賴其長養而不識其所以長養者誰之力，此其所以為難形容者歟？孔子曰：「大哉堯之為君！」其善於形容者矣。愚請申之。三皇以道而化民，乾坤之於屯蒙也，民皆知其道矣，謂之太古則可，謂之大哉則未焉。三王以功而勸民，大旱之於雲霓也，民皆知其功矣，謂之盡美則可，謂之大哉亦未焉。至於五伯以力而率民，桔橰之於夏畦也，民皆知其力矣，謂之小補則可，謂之大哉又豈可乎？然則大哉之稱，舍堯之為君，其誰當之？堯之德本不可名矣，強而名之曰「大哉」，亦名其所不可名者也。是故欽明文思安安，德之得於天者大也；允恭克讓，德之見於行者大也。莫大於四表，被于四表者，此德之大；莫
translation_en:
…[a virtue that is] great. Precisely because his virtue is great, the people are steeped in his beneficence and humanity is encompassed within his transforming influence—boundless and unadorned, beyond what words can set forth or paintings can depict. It is like the greatness of Heaven: all things receive its generation and completion without knowing whose merit brings them about, and all things rely on its nurturing and growth without recognizing whose power sustains them. Is this not why it is so difficult to describe? Confucius said, "Great indeed was Yao as a sovereign!" He was truly adept at describing it. Allow me in my humble capacity to elaborate upon this.

The Three Sovereigns transformed the people through the Way, like the hexagrams Qian (The Creative) and Kun (The Receptive) acting upon Tun (Difficulty at the Beginning) and Meng (Youthful Folly); the people all knew their Way. To call this "primordial antiquity" is permissible, but to call it "great indeed" is not yet fitting. The Three Kings encouraged the people through merit, like clouds and rainbows in a great drought; the people all knew their merit. To call this "perfectly beautiful" is permissible, but to call it "great indeed" is likewise not yet fitting. As for the Five Hegemons, who led the people through force, like a well-sweep watering summer garden plots; the people all knew their force. To call this a "minor help" is permissible, but how could one possibly call it "great indeed"?

Such being the case, apart from Yao as a sovereign, who else could be worthy of the acclaim "great indeed"? Yao's virtue was fundamentally beyond naming; to force a name upon it and call it "great indeed" is simply to name that which cannot be named. Therefore, "reverent, intelligent, accomplished, and thoughtful, naturally and without effort"—the virtue he received from Heaven was great; "sincerely courteous and capable of yielding"—the virtue manifested in his conduct was great. Nothing is greater than the four extremities of the world, yet it was the greatness of this virtue that reached unto the four extremities; nothing…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
大於上下格于上下者此德之大乃聖乃
神其德全體之大也乃武乃文其德妙用
之大也當時日出而作日入而息者不知
誰之所為如萬物形色乎天之造化而不
自知也耕田而食鑿井而飲者不知誰之
所使如萬物性命乎天之賦予而不自覺
也但見其百姓昭明黎民於變成功巍然
若雲行雨施品物流形之可仰也而不知
其所以成功者何所由由乎德之大發見
===
耳但見其曆象之頒大章之奏文章煥然
若日照月臨萬象森羅之可覩也而不知
其所以文章者何所本本乎德之大呈露
耳神全而化不形民由其化而無可擬其
化體厚而用不顯民利其用而不能談其
用故觀之萬民萬民以為堯何有於我乃
見堯之大極至於無形觀之萬物萬物以
為天何有於我乃見天之大神妙於無迹
萬民忘乎堯萬物忘乎天此大哉帝堯之
punctuated: 大於上下，格于上下者，此德之大；乃聖乃神，其德全體之大也；乃武乃文，其德妙用之大也。當時日出而作、日入而息者，不知誰之所為，如萬物形色乎天之造化而不自知也；耕田而食、鑿井而飲者，不知誰之所使，如萬物性命乎天之賦予而不自覺也。但見其百姓昭明、黎民於變，成功巍然，若雲行雨施、品物流形之可仰也，而不知其所以成功者何所由，由乎德之大發見耳；但見其曆象之頒、大章之奏，文章煥然，若日照月臨、萬象森羅之可覩也，而不知其所以文章者何所本，本乎德之大呈露耳。神全而化不形，民由其化而無可擬其化；體厚而用不顯，民利其用而不能談其用。故觀之萬民，萬民以為「堯何有於我」，乃見堯之大極至於無形；觀之萬物，萬物以為「天何有於我」，乃見天之大神妙於無迹。萬民忘乎堯，萬物忘乎天，此「大哉帝堯之
translation_en: …greater than what lies above and below, and what reaches above and below is the greatness of this virtue. Being sagely and spirit-like is the greatness of the complete substance of his virtue; being martial and civil is the greatness of the wondrous functioning of his virtue. At that time, those who went to work at sunrise and rested at sunset did not know whose doing it was, just as the myriad things take their forms and colors from Heaven's creative transformation without knowing it themselves; those who plowed the fields to eat and dug wells to drink did not know who caused it to be so, just as the myriad things receive their natures and destinies from Heaven's endowment without being aware of it themselves. One only saw that the hundred clans were illustrious and the black-haired people were transformed, his achievements towering on high, admirable like the passing of clouds and the falling of rain whereby the various things flow into form; yet no one knew whence those achievements arose—they arose simply from the manifestation of the greatness of his virtue. One only saw the promulgation of the calendar and astronomical instruments and the performance of the Dazhang music, his cultural accomplishments shining brightly, visible like the shining of the sun and the approach of the moon whereby all phenomena are arrayed in order; yet no one knew upon what those cultural accomplishments were founded—they were founded simply upon the revelation of the greatness of his virtue. When spirit is complete, transformation leaves no form; the people follow his transformation yet have nothing by which to liken his transformation. When substance is deep, function is not overt; the people benefit from his functioning yet are unable to speak of his functioning. Therefore, looking at the myriad people, the myriad people think, "What is Yao to us?"—and therein is seen the greatness of Yao reaching the ultimate point of formlessness; looking at the myriad things, the myriad things think, "What is Heaven to us?"—and therein is seen the greatness of Heaven in its wondrousness without a trace. The myriad people forget Yao, and the myriad things forget Heaven. Is this not how "Great indeed was Yao as…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
為君所以與天準則而民無能名者乎惟
其民無能名乃見其與天準則惟其與天
準則乃見其所以為大也三皇尚不能同
其大三王巳不可擬其大五霸焉能彷彿
其萬一哉夫子贊之言約而意盡矣粤昔
史臣贊堯有曰其仁如天其智如神望之
如日就之如雲夫日與雲皆天之一耳未
足以盡其妙惟如天一語與夫子之言合
也坤承乾而不得以並乾故於乾曰大哉
===
===
而於坤則曰至哉舜承堯而不得以並堯
故於堯曰大哉而於舜則曰君哉求其黜
五霸超三王等三皇並美帝堯而為大哉
之君者今幸有
聖天子在上謹論
詔
擬漢遣將軍周亞夫等屯兵備邊詔
彭斅
同考試官教諭顏批措詞典實深得詔體
punctuated:
為君，所以與天準則而民無能名者乎！惟其民無能名，乃見其與天準則；惟其與天準則，乃見其所以為大也。三皇尚不能同其大，三王巳不可擬其大，五霸焉能彷彿其萬一哉！夫子贊之，言約而意盡矣。粤昔史臣贊堯有曰：「其仁如天，其智如神，望之如日，就之如雲。」夫日與雲皆天之一耳，未足以盡其妙，惟「如天」一語與夫子之言合也。坤承乾而不得以並乾，故於乾曰「大哉」，而於坤則曰「至哉」；舜承堯而不得以並堯，故於堯曰「大哉」，而於舜則曰「君哉」。求其黜五霸、超三王、等三皇，並美帝堯而為「大哉」之君者，今幸有聖天子在上。謹論。

詔
擬漢遣將軍周亞夫等屯兵備邊詔
彭斅
同考試官教諭顏批：措詞典實，深得詔體。
translation_en:
… rulership is why he modeled himself on Heaven and the people could find no name for his virtue! Only because the people could find no name for it do we see that he modeled himself on Heaven; only because he modeled himself on Heaven do we see wherein his greatness lay. Even the Three Sovereigns could not equal his greatness, and the Three Kings already could not be compared to his greatness—how then could the Five Hegemons resemble even one ten-thousandth of it? When the Master praised him, his words were brief yet his meaning was exhaustive. In antiquity, the historian praised Yao, saying: "His benevolence was like Heaven, his wisdom like a spirit; seen from afar he was like the sun, approached he was like the clouds." Now, the sun and the clouds are each merely one aspect of Heaven and are insufficient to exhaust his wonder; only the single phrase "like Heaven" accords with the Master's words. Kun (Earth) receives from Qian (Heaven) and cannot be placed on a par with Qian; therefore of Qian it is said "Great indeed!" while of Kun it is said "Utmost indeed!"
