Shun succeeded Yao and could not be placed on a par with Yao; therefore of Yao it is said "Great indeed!" while of Shun it is said "A ruler indeed!" If we seek one who rejects the Five Hegemons, surpasses the Three Kings, equals the Three Sovereigns, and matches the excellence of Emperor Yao to be a ruler of whom it is said "Great indeed!", today we are fortunate to have our sagely Son of Heaven reigning above. I respectfully present this discourse.

Imperial Edict (Zhao)
An Imitation of the Han Edict Dispatching General Zhou Yafu 周亞夫 and Others to Garrison Troops and Prepare the Frontier
By Peng Xiao 彭斅
Comment by the Associate Examiner, Instructor Yan 顏: The wording is classical and substantive, deeply capturing the style of an imperial edict.

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
考試官修撰劉批得漢詔體
考試官左庶子黎批曾見漢詔是如此作
朕惟先王之於夷狄服則懷之以恩叛則
懾之以威故周宣中興命南仲城朔方方
叔伐玁狁厥功懋焉茲者匈奴不道擾我
北邊上郡雲中咸罹荼毒救民保境良切
朕心特命爾將軍周亞夫次細柳劉禮次
霸上徐厲次棘門以備之朕將躬行勞軍
作其銳氣於戲宣威敵愾冀蚤獻其成功
===
掃穴犁庭尚徐圖其後舉故茲詔示咸使
聞知
誥
擬唐破突厥擒頡利可汗加李靖左光祿
大夫誥
王忻
同考試官訓導朱批文追古作整然可觀
考試官修撰劉批用唐語可取
考試官左庶子黎批誥有事實
punctuated:
考試官修撰劉批：得漢詔體。
考試官左庶子黎批：曾見漢詔是如此作。

朕惟先王之於夷狄，服則懷之以恩，叛則懾之以威。故周宣中興，命南仲城朔方，方叔伐玁狁，厥功懋焉。茲者匈奴不道，擾我北邊，上郡、雲中，咸罹荼毒。救民保境，良切朕心。特命爾將軍周亞夫次細柳，劉禮次霸上，徐厲次棘門，以備之。朕將躬行勞軍，作其銳氣。於戲！宣威敵愾，冀蚤獻其成功；掃穴犁庭，尚徐圖其後舉。故茲詔示，咸使聞知。

誥
擬唐破突厥擒頡利可汗加李靖左光祿大夫誥
王忻
同考試官訓導朱批：文追古作，整然可觀。
考試官修撰劉批：用唐語，可取。
考試官左庶子黎批：誥有事實。
translation_en:
Examiner and Senior Compiler Liu comments: It captures the style of a Han proclamation.
Examiner and Left Mentor of the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent Li comments: I have seen that Han proclamations were written in just this way.

We reflect that in their treatment of the border tribes, the Former Kings cherished them with grace when they submitted, and awed them with might when they rebelled. Thus, during the restoration of King Xuan of Zhou, he commanded Nanzhong to fortify Shuofang and Fangshu to attack the Xianyun, and their achievements were great indeed. Now the Xiongnu act without principle and harass Our northern frontiers; Shang Commandery (Shangjun) and Yunzhong have both suffered their cruel ravages. Rescuing the people and protecting the borders weigh heavily upon Our heart. We specially command you, General Zhou Yafu, to encamp at Xiliu; Liu Li to encamp at Bashang; and Xu Li to encamp at Jimen, in order to guard against them. We shall go in person to reward and comfort the troops and rouse their keen spirit. Alas! Display Our majesty and vent anger against the enemy, in the hope that you will soon present the accomplishment of your success; as for sweeping out their dens and plowing up their courts, let Us deliberate unhurriedly on subsequent campaigns. Therefore We issue this proclamation of instruction so that all may be made to hear and know of it.

Mandate (gao)
An Imitation of a Tang Mandate Advancing Li Jing to Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon upon Defeating the Turks (Tujue) and Capturing the Illig Qaghan (Xieli Kehan)
Wang Xin 
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhu comments: The prose rivals ancient works, orderly and well worth reading.
Examiner and Senior Compiler Liu comments: It uses Tang-dynasty phrasing, which is commendable.
Examiner and Left Mentor of the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent Li comments: The mandate is grounded in historical fact.

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
蓋聞執訊獲醜詩詠元老凱還之勳崇德
報功書載哲王惇宗之典故大臣能成蓋
世之偉績國家必有不次之榮遷在古道
以當然於朕心乎何有咨爾具官李靖兼
資文武植德忠良入登相府佐乾御以龍
飛出握將拳振兵師而虎奮演八陳舊規
於六花法內留百戰大名於七德舞中平
梁廟筭昔着巴陵破虜奇功今收突厥風
驅電掃襲惡陽而瓦解定襄鶚擊鵬摶破
===
陰山而霜清大漠遂擒頡利上獻朝廷雪
耻酬百王
太上皇春生喜色除兇報千古四方民雷動懽
聲厥績偉哉是宜褒擢今特加爾左光祿
大夫用答爾勞爾尚益篤忠貞爰圖報稱
予欲仁義宣布爾敷陳周召之言予欲禮
樂興行爾匹休夷夔之美往哉汝諧勿替
朕命
表
punctuated:
蓋聞執訊獲醜，《詩》詠元老凱還之勳；崇德報功，《書》載哲王惇宗之典。故大臣能成蓋世之偉績，國家必有不次之榮遷。在古道以當然，於朕心乎何有？咨爾具官李靖，兼資文武，植德忠良。入登相府，佐乾御以龍飛；出握將拳，振兵師而虎奮。演八陳舊規於六花法內，留百戰大名於《七德舞》中。平梁廟筭，昔着巴陵；破虜奇功，今收突厥。風驅電掃，襲惡陽而瓦解定襄；鶚擊鵬摶，破陰山而霜清大漠。遂擒頡利，上獻朝廷。雪耻酬百王，太上皇春生喜色；除兇報千古，四方民雷動懽聲。厥績偉哉，是宜褒擢。今特加爾左光祿大夫，用答爾勞。爾尚益篤忠貞，爰圖報稱。予欲仁義宣布，爾敷陳周、召之言；予欲禮樂興行，爾匹休夷、夔之美。往哉汝諧，勿替朕命。

表
translation_en:
We have heard that taking prisoners for interrogation and capturing enemy crowds is what the Classic of Poetry (Shi) sings of as the meritorious achievement of the senior minister returning in triumph; exalting virtue and rewarding merit is what the Classic of Documents (Shu) records as the canon of wise kings generously honoring the worthy. Therefore, when a great minister can accomplish an extraordinary achievement that surpasses the age, the state must bestow an exceptional promotion in honor. According to the ancient Way this is only natural; in Our own heart, how could there be any hesitation?

Oh, you, Li Jing 李靖, holding your full official titles: you are endowed with both civil and military talents, and have established your virtue in loyalty and goodness. Entering court to ascend to the Counsellor's office, you assisted the sovereign's rule as the dragon took flight; going out on campaign holding the general's authority [? 拳, for 權], you roused the armies as a tiger springs into action. You adapted the ancient regulations of the Eight Formations within the Six-Petaled Method, and left your great renown from a hundred battles in the Dance of the Seven Virtues (Qide wu). Your court strategies for pacifying Liang were formerly demonstrated at Baling 巴陵; your marvelous功 merit in smashing the caitiffs has now brought about the submission of the Turks (Tujue 突厥). Driving like the wind and sweeping like lightning, you launched a surprise attack on Eyang 惡陽 and caused Dingxiang 定襄 to collapse like tiles; striking like an osprey and soaring like a roc, you smashed them at the Yin Mountains 陰山 and cleared the Great Desert like frost. Thus you captured Jieli 頡利 [Illig Qaghan] and presented him up to the court. Wiping away shame to requite a hundred kings, the Retired Emperor's face brightened with spring-like joy; eliminating the wicked to avenge a thousand ages, the people of the four quarters raised thunderous cheers of delight. Magnificent indeed is your achievement! It is fitting that you be praised and promoted.

Now We specially confer upon you the prestige title of Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon (Zuo guanglu dafu), in order to reward your toil. May you ever more deeply dedicate yourself to loyalty and integrity, and strive to repay your office. When I wish benevolence and righteousness to be proclaimed abroad, you shall set forth words like those of the Dukes of Zhou 周 and Shao 召; when I wish rites and music to flourish and be practiced, you shall match the excellence of Boyi 伯夷 and Kui 夔. Go forth and be harmonious in your duties; do not neglect Our command!

Memorials (Biao 表)

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
擬宋司馬光進資治通鑑表
王敏
同考試官訓導沉批表得駢儷體詞且典
雅可佳
同考試官教諭徐批表語忠懇宛然温公
詞氣
考試官修撰劉批典麗可佳
考試官左庶子黎批似宋朝文字
具官臣光言臣於治平中奉
===
敕編集歷代君臣事迹續奉
聖旨賜名資治通鑑今已完畢謹用進
呈者伏以天庭垂柱下史之星璣衡允協
帝闕分左右史之職言動必書故古者列國封
建記時事掌於世家而累朝百度舉行公
是非付之直筆既惟年代之遷革遂令簡
冊之浩繁匪遇
聖朝曷成定制臣誠惶誠懼頓首頓首竊念臣
性識庸魯學問荒疎讀古書有愚者之一
punctuated:
擬宋司馬光進《資治通鑑》表
王敏
同考試官訓導沉批：表得駢儷體，詞且典雅，可佳。
同考試官教諭徐批：表語忠懇，宛然温公詞氣。
考試官修撰劉批：典麗可佳。
考試官左庶子黎批：似宋朝文字。
具官臣光言：臣於治平中，奉敕編集歷代君臣事迹，續奉聖旨，賜名《資治通鑑》。今已完畢，謹用進呈者。伏以天庭垂柱下史之星，璣衡允協；帝闕分左右史之職，言動必書。故古者列國封建，記時事掌於世家；而累朝百度舉行，公是非付之直筆。既惟年代之遷革，遂令簡冊之浩繁。匪遇聖朝，曷成定制？臣誠惶誠懼，頓首頓首。竊念臣性識庸魯，學問荒疎。讀古書有愚者之一…
translation_en:
An Imitation of the Song Dynasty Memorial by Sima Guang 司馬光 Presenting the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government (Zizhi tongjian 資治通鑑)
Wang Min 王敏

Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Shen 沉 comments: The memorial captures the parallel-prose style, and its diction is moreover classical and refined; commendable.
Associate Examiner, Instructor Xu 徐 comments: The language of the memorial is loyal and earnest, quite in the tone and spirit of the Duke of Wen 温公 (Sima Guang).
Examiner, Senior Compiler Liu 劉 comments: Classical, elegant, and commendable.
Examiner, Left Mentor Li 黎 comments: It resembles a composition of the Song dynasty.

Your servant Guang, holding full official title, states: During the Zhiping 治平 reign (1064–1067), your servant received an imperial command to compile and edit the deeds of rulers and ministers through the successive dynasties, and subsequently received an imperial decree bestowing upon it the title Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government (Zizhi tongjian). Now that it has been completed, I respectfully present it to the throne.

I humbly reflect that in the heavenly court there hangs the star of the Archivist Below the Pillars, with which the armillary sphere is truly in harmony; at the imperial palace are divided the offices of the Scribes of the Left and the Right, by whom words and deeds are unfailingly recorded. Thus in antiquity, when the various states were enfeoffed, the recording of contemporary affairs was the charge of hereditary houses; and as the myriad institutions were carried out through successive dynasties, impartial judgments of right and wrong were entrusted to the forthright brush. Yet because of the passage and succession of eras, the bamboo slips and books have grown vast and voluminous. Had we not encountered this Sacred Dynasty, how could a definitive standard be established?

Your servant is truly in awe and trepidation, bowing his head to the ground, bowing his head to the ground. I privately reflect that your servant is mediocre and dull in nature and perception, and rusty and superficial in learning. In reading ancient books, I have had the single [insight] of a foolish man…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
得毎願獻於仰
宸扆勞一日之萬幾似難博物恒不自揆輙
取遷固以下諸史可供
御覽者刪冗長而撮機要易紀傳以為編年
俾先後有倫精麤不雜然私家寡力弘道
待人伏遇
英皇睿智天成文明日麗毎懷歴覽古道用以
恢張大猷爰
詔下臣俾之編集仍許自辟官屬選集賢翰
===
苑庶府之英復令借貸秘書發龍圖天章
三館之積居
朝則給
内帑以供費在外則設書局以自隨臣自幸
夙昔所願一朝獲伸然尚懼考究惟艱曠
時未就欽惟
〇〇〇嗣登
大寶茂纘
洪圖自誠明謂之性紹三皇五帝之傳惟精
punctuated: 得，毎願獻於仰宸扆。勞一日之萬幾，似難博物；恒不自揆，輙取遷、固以下諸史可供御覽者，刪冗長而撮機要，易紀傳以為編年，俾先後有倫，精麤不雜。然私家寡力，弘道待人。伏遇英皇睿智天成，文明日麗，毎懷歴覽古道，用以恢張大猷，爰詔下臣，俾之編集。仍許自辟官屬，選集賢、翰苑、庶府之英；復令借貸秘書，發龍圖、天章、三館之積。居朝則給内帑以供費，在外則設書局以自隨。臣自幸夙昔所願，一朝獲伸；然尚懼考究惟艱，曠時未就。欽惟〇〇〇嗣登大寶，茂纘洪圖。自誠明謂之性，紹三皇五帝之傳；惟精
translation_en:
…gain, which I have ever wished to offer up; looking up at the imperial screen, toiling over a myriad affairs in a single day, it seems difficult to encompass extensive learning. Constantly failing to measure my own abilities, I forthwith took the various histories from Sima Qian and Ban Gu onward that could be offered for Imperial Perusal, pruned away redundancies to extract the essential points, and changed the annals-and-biographies format into a chronological one, so that earlier and later events would follow in proper order and the refined and the coarse would not be muddled together. Yet a private household has meager resources, and broadening the Way awaits the right person.

Humbly encountering Emperor Yingzong, whose sagely wisdom was heaven-endowed and whose cultural brilliance shone like the sun, and who ever cherished reviewing the ancient ways wherewith to expand the Great Plan—he thereupon issued an edict to this lowly subject, commanding me to compile and edit the work. He further permitted me to personally recruit subordinate officials, selecting the finest talents from the Academy of Scholarly Worthies (Jixian yuan), the Hanlin Academy, and the various offices; and he also ordered the loan of secret books, opening up the stores of the Longtu and Tianzhang Pavilions and the Three Institutes. While at court, funds were supplied from the Inner Treasury to cover expenses; when serving in the provinces, a compilation bureau was established to accompany me. I counted myself fortunate that what I had long wished for could in a single morning be realized; yet I still feared that historical investigation was arduous and that after a long lapse of time it was not yet completed.

Reverently reflecting that Your Majesty [〇〇〇] has succeeded to the Great Treasure and richly carried on the Grand Enterprise: "from sincerity to enlightenment is called nature," continuing the transmission of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors; "being pure…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
一執厥中繼
一祖四宗之志錫嘉名以渙汗其大號敷
睿藻而序冠其首編常令進讀於
經筵遂俾盛傳於當代臣誠荷
離明之繼照敢忘坤道之代終爰因分司提
舉職務之閑稽合表志紀傳簡編之富聚
眾長而設例採輿論以立言嘆春秋既絕
筆於獲麟嗟後學敢續經於先聖造端咸
烈寓感姬周沿戰國下移兩漢則臣攽之
===
說是從降三國俯歷孤隋則臣恕之言是
證暨彼五代之分裂又臣祖禹之折衷崇德
廣業大焉而禮樂制度有徵纂要鈞玄細
焉而稗官野史無忽務窮夜以繼日亦守
約而御煩蓋上從三晉之初封下訖季周
之末造凡閱
二聖朝一十有七年之久完此千三百六十有
二年之書然後事之關國家盛衰繫民生
休戚與夫善可為法惡可為戒者一覽可
punctuated: 一、執厥中，繼一祖四宗之志。錫嘉名以渙汗其大號，敷睿藻而序冠其首編。常令進讀於經筵，遂俾盛傳於當代。臣誠荷離明之繼照，敢忘坤道之代終？爰因分司提舉職務之閑，稽合表、志、紀、傳簡編之富，聚眾長而設例，採輿論以立言。嘆《春秋》既絕筆於獲麟，嗟後學敢續經於先聖？造端威烈，寓感姬周。沿戰國下移兩漢，則臣攽之說是從；降三國俯歷孤隋，則臣恕之言是證；暨彼五代之分裂，又臣祖禹之折衷。崇德廣業大焉，而禮樂制度有徵；纂要鈞玄細焉，而稗官野史無忽。務窮夜以繼日，亦守約而御煩。蓋上從三晉之初封，下訖季周之末造，凡閱二聖朝一十有七年之久，完此千三百六十有二年之書。然後事之關國家盛衰、繫民生休戚，與夫善可為法、惡可為戒者，一覽可
translation_en:
… [Being refined and] single-minded, holding fast to the Mean, Your Majesty continues the aspirations of the Founding Ancestor and the Four Imperial Ancestors. You bestowed an auspicious title upon the work, proclaiming it through a grand edict, and unfurled Your imperial literary brilliance to place a preface at the head of its first volume. By regularly ordering it to be presented and read at the Classics Colloquium, You have caused it to circulate widely in the present age.

Truly indebted to the successive illumination of Your radiant wisdom, how could your servant dare forget the ministerial duty of bringing tasks to completion? Therefore, taking advantage of the leisure afforded by my duties in the branch office and as Intendant of a shrine, I examined and synthesized the abundant records of chronological tables, treatises, basic annals, and biographies, gathering the strengths of many to establish editorial principles and drawing upon general opinion to formulate judgments. Lamenting that the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) ended its brush with the capture of the unicorn, how would a later scholar dare to presume to continue the Classic of the Former Sage? Thus, I began the work with King Weilie [rendered 咸烈 in text], embedding my reflections on the decline of the Ji-surname Zhou dynasty. Moving along from the Warring States down to the Two Han dynasties, the explanations of your servant [Liu] Ban (劉攽) were followed; coming down from the Three Kingdoms and passing through to the solitary Sui dynasty, the words of your servant [Liu] Shu (劉恕) were used for verification; and reaching the division of the Five Dynasties, the balanced judgments of your servant [Fan] Zuyu (范祖禹) were relied upon. In exalting virtue and broadening the enterprise on a grand scale, rites, music, and institutional systems are thoroughly attested; in compiling the essentials and probing the abstruse in fine detail, even minor accounts and unofficial histories were not neglected. Striving to prolong the day into the night, I held to conciseness in order to master complexity.

Tracing from the initial enfeoffment of the Three Jin at the top, down to the final years of the Later Zhou at the bottom, it took a total of seventeen years across two sacred reigns to complete this chronicle spanning one thousand three hundred and sixty-two years. Only then could matters concerning the rise and fall of states, tied to the weal and woe of the people's livelihood, as well as the good deeds that can serve as models and the evil deeds that can serve as warnings, all at a single glance be…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
豈有他道乎聖人有身教有言教觀諸五
經如易之家人書之五典詩之皇矣春秋
之謹名分皆言孝弟而禮記則備述之也
觀諸
聖製如大誥之申明五常陰隲之魏顆從治孝
順之大孝達孝皆言孝弟而五倫書則備
載之也至於孝弟兼備之人豈非禹湯文
武哉欽惟
皇上嗣登
===
大寶十年以來至尊
親上隆懽於
慈極即所謂教民親愛莫善於孝其與堯舜之
孝同一心彝倫惇叙下疏愛於
天潢即所謂教民禮順莫善於弟其與堯舜
之弟同一致是以身脩於家化形於國而
效達於天下引今天下之民納諸唐虞之
世人人親其親長其長而天下平矣然執
事又舉時務下詢承學愚以為則天之經
punctuated: 豈有他道乎？聖人有身教，有言教。觀諸《五經》，如《易》之《家人》、《書》之五典、《詩》之《皇矣》、《春秋》之謹名分，皆言孝弟，而《禮記》則備述之也。觀諸聖製，如《大誥》之申明五常、《陰隲》之魏顆從治、《孝順》之大孝達孝，皆言孝弟，而《五倫書》則備載之也。至於孝弟兼備之人，豈非禹、湯、文、武哉！欽惟皇上嗣登大寶十年以來，至尊親，上隆懽於慈極，即所謂「教民親愛莫善於孝」，其與堯、舜之孝同一心；彝倫惇叙，下疏愛於天潢，即所謂「教民禮順莫善於弟」，其與堯、舜之弟同一致。是以身脩於家，化形於國，而效達於天下。引今天下之民，納諸唐、虞之世，人人親其親、長其長，而天下平矣。然執事又舉時務，下詢承學，愚以為「則天之經，
translation_en:
…is there any other Way than this? The sages taught both by personal example and by words. Looking at the Five Classics—such as the "Family" (Jiaren) hexagram in the Book of Changes, the Five Canons in the Book of Documents, the ode "August" (Huang yi) in the Book of Odes, and the strict observance of names and statuses in the Spring and Autumn Annals—all speak of filial piety and fraternal submission, while the Record of Rites gives a comprehensive account of them. Looking at the imperial compositions—such as the clarification of the Five Constant Virtues in the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao), the account of Wei Ke following the rational charge in the Hidden Retribution (Yinzhi), and the discussions of great and far-reaching filial piety in the Facts of Filial Piety and Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi)—all speak of filial piety and fraternal submission, while the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu) records them in full. As for those who possessed both filial piety and fraternal submission in full measure, were they not Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu?

Reverently I reflect that since His Majesty succeeded to the Great Treasure ten years ago, in honoring the utmost affection, above he has lavished joy upon the Empress Dowager—which is precisely what is meant by "for teaching the people affection and love, nothing is better than filial piety," sharing the same heart as the filial piety of Yao and Shun. In richly ordering the invariable human relationships, below he has extended love across the imperial clan—which is precisely what is meant by "for teaching the people ritual propriety and compliance, nothing is better than fraternal submission," achieving the same result as the fraternal submission of Yao and Shun. Therefore, his person is cultivated in the family, his transforming influence is manifested in the state, and its efficacy reaches throughout the realm. Leading the people of the world today and placing them into an age like that of Tang and Yu (Yao and Shun), everyone treats their parents as parents and their elders as elders, and the world is at peace. Yet Your Honor has further raised current affairs to inquire of this junior scholar; in my humble opinion, "patterning oneself on the regularities of Heaven…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
考試官修撰劉批敷陳治本孝弟之意詳
整可觀
考試官左庶子黎批策善答結分孝弟大小尤
見學識
道行於往古垂百王之楷範惟本於孝弟
道著於
来今開萬世之泰平亦惟本於孝弟于以見
先聖
後聖其揆一也今承明問請詳陳之夫大哉帝
堯聖莫有及之者也君哉帝舜聖莫有踰
之者也然孟子論其道乃曰孝弟而已矣
盖堯光帝嚳之統羞兄摯之愆九族既睦
萬邦為之協和舜化瞽瞍之頑若弟象之
傲五典克從四方為之風動堯舜之為君
外孝弟豈有餘道乎堯舜人倫之至後之
聖人皆取法焉若禹之敘彝倫湯之釐耿
命文王之事王季而厚同姓武王之事文
王而相周公禹湯文武之為君外孝弟又
punctuated:
考試官修撰劉批：敷陳治本孝弟之意，詳整可觀。
考試官左庶子黎批：策善答結，分孝弟大小，尤見學識。

道行於往古，垂百王之楷範，惟本於孝弟；道著於来今，開萬世之泰平，亦惟本於孝弟。于以見先聖後聖，其揆一也。今承明問，請詳陳之。夫大哉帝堯，聖莫有及之者也；君哉帝舜，聖莫有踰之者也。然孟子論其道，乃曰：「孝弟而已矣。」盖堯光帝嚳之統，羞兄摯之愆，九族既睦，萬邦為之協和；舜化瞽瞍之頑，若弟象之傲，五典克從，四方為之風動。堯、舜之為君，外孝弟豈有餘道乎？堯、舜，人倫之至，後之聖人皆取法焉。若禹之敘彝倫，湯之釐耿命，文王之事王季而厚同姓，武王之事文王而相周公，禹、湯、文、武之為君，外孝弟又
translation_en:
Examiner Senior Compiler Liu comments: The exposition of the idea that governance is rooted in filial piety and fraternal respect is detailed, well-structured, and worthy of appreciation.
Examiner Left Mentor Li comments: The policy essay answers and concludes well; its distinction between the greater and lesser aspects of filial piety and fraternal respect especially shows erudition and insight.

When the Way was practiced in antiquity, handing down a model for a hundred kings, it was rooted solely in filial piety and fraternal respect; when the Way is made manifest in the present and future, opening up great peace for ten thousand generations, it is likewise rooted solely in filial piety and fraternal respect. From this we can see that the former sages and the later sages share the same principles. Now, having received your enlightened question, I beg leave to set this forth in detail.

Great indeed was Emperor Yao—in sageliness none could equal him! A true sovereign indeed was Emperor Shun—in sageliness none could surpass him! Yet when Mencius discussed their Way, he said, "It is simply filial piety and fraternal respect, and nothing more." For Yao glorified the lineage of Emperor Ku and felt shame at the failings of his elder brother Zhi; once the nine branches of his kin were brought into harmony, the myriad states were thereby united in concord. Shun transformed the obstinacy of Gusou and accommodated the arrogance of his younger brother Xiang; the Five Cardinal Duties were capably observed, and the four quarters were thereby moved as by the wind. In being sovereigns, what other Way did Yao and Shun have apart from filial piety and fraternal respect? Yao and Shun were the culmination of human moral relations, and the sages of later times all took them as their model. Such were Yu's ordering of the invariable human relationships, Tang's rectification of the mandate at Geng [?], King Wen's serving of King Ji and generous treatment of those of the same surname, and King Wu's serving of King Wen and reliance on the Duke of Zhou as prime minister. In being sovereigns, apart from filial piety and fraternal respect, how could Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu furthermore…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
盡矣臣平生精力悉在此編然中間抵捂
難逃重譴伏望矜願忠之誠曲加容納於
燕閒之地時賜省觀監于古考于今急親賢
之為務聴其言觀其行動典學之是圖俾
聖心洞達而
天德崇壽配乾坤之久遠
皇極尊安而民福厚
恩同海嶽之高深臣無任瞻
天仰
===
聖激切屏營之至謹以通鑑若干卷目錄并考
異若干卷隨表上
進以
聞臣光誠惶誠懼頓首頓首謹言
策
第一問
萬盛
同考試官教諭顏 批脩答治道一本孝弟
策塲中之巨擘也况前二塲尤稱宜取以冠本房
punctuated:
盡矣。臣平生精力，悉在此編，然中間抵捂，難逃重譴。伏望矜願忠之誠，曲加容納，於燕閒之地，時賜省觀。監于古，考于今，急親賢之為務；聴其言，觀其行，動典學之是圖。俾聖心洞達而天德崇，壽配乾坤之久遠；皇極尊安而民福厚，恩同海嶽之高深。臣無任瞻天仰聖，激切屏營之至。謹以《通鑑》若干卷、《目錄》并《考異》若干卷，隨表上進以聞。臣光誠惶誠懼，頓首頓首，謹言。

策
第一問
萬盛
同考試官教諭顏批：脩答治道，一本孝弟，策塲中之巨擘也。况前二塲尤稱，宜取以冠本房。
translation_en:
… has been exhausted. The energy of your servant's entire life is completely contained in this compilation; yet for the contradictions and errors within it, it is hard to escape heavy censure. I humbly hope that You will take pity on my sincerity in wishing to be loyal and graciously grant Your acceptance, bestowing Your inspection upon it from time to time in moments of leisure. Taking warning from antiquity and examining the present, make closeness to the worthy Your urgent task; listening to their words and observing their deeds, make every move a plan for constant study. Thus may Your Sacred Mind be thoroughly enlightened and Your Heavenly Virtue exalted, with longevity matching the endurance of Heaven and Earth; may the Imperial Ultimate be revered and tranquil and the people's blessings abundant, with grace equal to the height of the mountains and the depth of the seas. Your servant is overcome with the utmost emotion and trepidation in looking up to Heaven and revering the Sage. I respectfully present a certain number of chapters of the Comprehensive Mirror (Tongjian), together with a certain number of chapters of the Catalog (Mulu) and Examination of Differences (Kaoyi), accompanying this memorial for Your Majesty's hearing. Your servant Guang, in utmost fear and trepidation, bows his head to the ground again and again and respectfully speaks.

Policy Essays
First Question
Wan Sheng 萬盛
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Yan 顏: His thorough response on the Way of governance is rooted entirely in filial piety and fraternal submission—a masterwork of the policy-essay session! Moreover, as his first two sessions are especially fitting, he should be selected to head this examination ward.

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
因地之利以順天下是以其教不肅而成
其政不嚴而治則致中和以極于天地位
萬物育固本於孝弟也孝弟之至通于神
明光于四海無所不通則隆禮于
上帝以至於鳳凰降龜龍假風雨節寒暑時亦
本於孝弟也愛敬盡於事親而德教加于
百姓刑于四海則正心正朝廷以底于中
國尊安四夷順服又非本於孝弟乎夫
天子之孝弟視膳問安徐行後長皆其小者而
===
有至德要道以順天下天典民彝以化四
方乃其大者惟不忽其小者而備舉其大
者焉斯治道全矣管見如斯未知是否惟
進而教之
第二問
馬中錫
同考試官訓導賀 批 理學一策聖賢傳授
之言異世相符殊塗同歸融會而一之者蓋不多見
此作得之況氣完詞湧可當獨步
punctuated:
因地之利，以順天下。是以其教不肅而成，其政不嚴而治。」則致中和以極于「天地位，萬物育」，固本於孝弟也。「孝弟之至，通于神明，光于四海，無所不通。」則隆禮于上帝，以至於鳳凰降、龜龍假、風雨節、寒暑時，亦本於孝弟也。「愛敬盡於事親，而德教加于百姓，刑于四海。」則正心、正朝廷，以底于中國尊安、四夷順服，又非本於孝弟乎？夫天子之孝弟，視膳、問安、徐行後長，皆其小者；而有至德要道以順天下，天典民彝以化四方，乃其大者。惟不忽其小者，而備舉其大者焉，斯治道全矣。管見如斯，未知是否，惟進而教之。

第二問
馬中錫
同考試官訓導賀批：理學一策，聖賢傳授之言，異世相符，殊塗同歸。融會而一之者，蓋不多見，此作得之。況氣完詞湧，可當獨步。
translation_en:
… and taking advantage of the benefits of the earth in order to bring harmony to All under Heaven. Therefore, his teaching succeeds without being severe, and his governance brings order without being strict." Thus, achieving equilibrium and harmony to the ultimate point where "Heaven and Earth are in their proper places and the myriad things are nourished" is truly rooted in filial piety and fraternal submission. "Filial piety and fraternal submission at their utmost reach the spirits, shine throughout the Four Seas, and penetrate everywhere." Thus, exalting rites to the Lord on High, even to the point where phoenixes descend, tortoises and dragons arrive, wind and rain are regulated, and cold and heat come in their proper seasons, is also rooted in filial piety and fraternal submission. "When love and reverence are exhausted in serving one's parents, moral teaching extends to the common people and serves as a model throughout the Four Seas." Thus, rectifying the mind and rectifying the court so as to bring about the revered security of the Central States and the obedient submission of the Four Barbarians—is this not also rooted in filial piety and fraternal submission? Now, in the filial piety and fraternal submission of the Son of Heaven, inspecting the meals, inquiring after health, and walking slowly behind elders are all the lesser matters; whereas possessing supreme virtue and the essential Way to bring harmony to All under Heaven, and the heavenly norms and constant human virtues to transform the four quarters, are the greater matters. Only by not neglecting the lesser matters while fully carrying out the greater ones will the Way of governance be complete. Such is my humble view; I do not know whether it is correct, and I pray you will advance me and instruct me.

Second Question
Ma Zhongxi 馬中錫
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor He 賀: In this policy essay on the Learning of Principle (lixue 理學), the words transmitted by the sages and worthies tally across different ages and arrive at the same destination by different paths. Those who can synthesize and unify them are rarely seen, yet this composition achieves it. Moreover, its vital breath is complete and its words surge forth; it deserves to stand without peer.

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭朱批能會聖賢諸儒之言
於一又知所以用功次第必究心於理學者
考試官修撰劉批知行工夫本於居敬斯有門
戶可入此策發明詳盡可謂知所用心矣
考試官左庶子黎批此策理學詳明似嘗體諸身者
聖賢之學以身心為本身心之功以知行
為要蓋致知則有以會此理于心力行則
有以體此理于身知行並進身心交脩此
聖賢之學所以為至也歟請因明問而陳
===
之天地之所以樞紐陰陽化生人物者此
理也聖人之所以參贊天地綱紀人物者
亦此理也理之原于天而具于人萬古一
致如此豈可得而易哉是故以聖賢之已
言者論之堯舜禹之授受曰允執厥中湯
武之授受曰建中建極中與極此理之無
過不及也春秋之時聖王不作孔子窮而
在下但以此理授其門人曾子子貢皆以
一貫此理之一本而萬殊也至顏子又以
punctuated:
同考試官教諭朱批：能會聖賢諸儒之言於一，又知所以用功次第，必究心於理學者。
考試官修撰劉批：知行工夫本於居敬，斯有門戶可入。此策發明詳盡，可謂知所用心矣。
考試官左庶子黎批：此策理學詳明，似嘗體諸身者。

聖賢之學，以身心為本；身心之功，以知行為要。蓋致知則有以會此理于心，力行則有以體此理于身。知行並進，身心交脩，此聖賢之學所以為至也歟！請因明問而陳之。天地之所以樞紐陰陽、化生人物者，此理也；聖人之所以參贊天地、綱紀人物者，亦此理也。理之原于天而具于人，萬古一致如此，豈可得而易哉！是故以聖賢之已言者論之：堯、舜、禹之授受曰「允執厥中」，湯、武之授受曰「建中」、「建極」。「中」與「極」，此理之無過不及也。春秋之時，聖王不作，孔子窮而在下，但以此理授其門人。曾子、子貢皆以「一貫」，此理之一本而萬殊也；至顏子又以
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhu 朱 comments: He is able to synthesize the words of the sages, worthies, and various Confucian scholars into one, and moreover understands the proper sequence of effort in self-cultivation; he must be someone who has devoted his mind to the learning of Principle (lixue).
Examiner and Senior Compiler Liu 劉 comments: When the effort of knowledge and action is rooted in abiding in reverence, there is a gateway through which to enter. This policy essay elucidates the matter thoroughly and exhaustively; he may truly be said to know where to direct his mind.
Examiner and Left Mentor of the Secretariat of the Heir Apparent Li 黎 comments: This policy essay explains the learning of Principle clearly and in detail; it seems to be the work of one who has personally embodied it.

The learning of the sages and worthies takes the body and the mind as its foundation, and the cultivation of the body and the mind takes knowledge and action as its essentials. For by extending knowledge, one has the means to comprehend this Principle in the mind, and by practicing earnestly, one has the means to embody this Principle in the person. When knowledge and action advance together and body and mind are mutually cultivated, is this not why the learning of the sages and worthies reaches the ultimate! Please allow me to set this forth in response to your enlightened question. That by which Heaven and Earth serve as the pivot of yin and yang and transform and generate human beings and all things is this Principle; that by which the sages assist in the transforming and nourishing powers of Heaven and Earth and bring order to human beings and all things is also this Principle. That Principle originates in Heaven and is endowed in human beings, remaining uniform across ten thousand ages like this—how could it ever be altered! Therefore, if we discuss it in terms of what the sages and worthies have already said: in the transmission between Yao 堯, Shun 舜, and Yu 禹, it was called "sincerely holding fast the Mean"; in the transmission between Tang 湯 and Wu 武, it was called "establishing the Mean" and "establishing the Ultimate." The "Mean" and the "Ultimate" refer to this Principle having neither excess nor deficiency. In the Spring and Autumn period, sage-kings no longer arose, and Confucius 孔子, in adversity and occupying a lowly station, merely transmitted this Principle to his disciples. With Both Zengzi 曾子 and Zigong 子貢, he spoke of "one thread binding all," which refers to this Principle having one root and ten thousand manifestations; as for Yanzi 顏子, he further spoke of…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
仁雖不及一貫盖學而至於仁則私欲淨
盡天理流行一貫之理在是矣曰中曰極
曰仁與一貫名不同而同此理焉曾子一
傳而子思中庸以誠為要誠即此理之真
實無妄也再傳而孟子七篇以性善養氣
為至性善即此理之本然養氣求無慊于
此理而已其與仁與一貫之旨何戾乎周
子繼孔孟之學於百世之下太極一圖推
原陰陽造化之根圖之說曰無極而太極
===
此理無形而極至也中正仁義而主靜聖
人全此理之動靜而主乎靜也其與孔孟
之言何殊乎程子親及周子之門而受是
圖及其教人不以圖而以敬盖圖之理微
未有能受之者敬則使人有所持循以入
果能于是而有得焉則圖之理亦不外矣
夫學之為道有知焉有行焉辨析聖賢之
言而會其理于心知也知之既真惟其所
得身體而力行之以求無愧于聖賢□□
punctuated: 仁，雖不及一貫，盖學而至於仁，則私欲淨盡，天理流行，一貫之理在是矣。曰中、曰極、曰仁與一貫，名不同而同此理焉。曾子一傳而子思《中庸》以誠為要，誠即此理之真實無妄也。再傳而《孟子》七篇以性善養氣為至，性善即此理之本然，養氣求無慊于此理而已，其與仁與一貫之旨何戾乎？周子繼孔、孟之學於百世之下，《太極》一圖推原陰陽造化之根。圖之說曰「無極而太極」，此理無形而極至也；「中正仁義而主靜」，聖人全此理之動靜而主乎靜也，其與孔、孟之言何殊乎？程子親及周子之門而受是圖，及其教人，不以圖而以敬。盖圖之理微，未有能受之者；敬則使人有所持循以入，果能于是而有得焉，則圖之理亦不外矣。夫學之為道，有知焉，有行焉。辨析聖賢之言，而會其理于心，知也；知之既真，惟其所得，身體而力行之，以求無愧于聖賢，□□
translation_en:
… humaneness (ren); although he did not mention the "one thread running through all," when one studies and attains humaneness, selfish desires are completely cleansed away and Heavenly Principle flows freely—the principle of the "one thread" is right within this. Whether called the "Mean," the "Ultimate," "humaneness," or the "one thread," the names differ, yet they share this same principle.

Passed down one generation from Master Zeng, Zisi's Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) took sincerity (cheng) as its essential point; sincerity is simply the true reality and freedom from falsehood of this principle. Passed down again, the seven books of Mencius (Mengzi) took the goodness of human nature and the nourishing of vital energy (qi) as the highest aim; the goodness of human nature is the original state of this principle, and nourishing vital energy is merely seeking to have no deficiency in this principle. How does this conflict at all with the purport of humaneness and the "one thread"?

Master Zhou [Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤] succeeded to the learning of Confucius and Mencius a hundred generations later, and his single Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taijitu) traced the roots of yin and yang and the creative transformations of nature. The Explanation of the Diagram (Tushuo) states, "The Non-Ultimate and yet the Supreme Ultimate"—meaning that this principle is formless and yet represents the highest ultimate. It states, "Centrality, correctness, humaneness, and righteousness, while taking tranquility as fundamental"—meaning that the sage embodies this principle completely in both activity and tranquility, while taking tranquility as fundamental. How does this differ at all from the words of Confucius and Mencius?

The Masters Cheng [Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤] personally attended Master Zhou's gate and received this diagram, yet when they taught others, they did not use the diagram, but rather taught reverent seriousness (jing). For the principle of the diagram is subtle, and none were yet able to receive it; reverent seriousness, however, gives people something to hold on to and follow in order to enter the Way. If one is truly able to gain understanding through this, then the principle of the diagram is likewise nothing outside of it.

Now, the Way of learning involves both knowledge and practice. To analyze and discern the words of the sages and worthies and to grasp their principle in one's mind—this is knowledge. Once one's knowledge is genuine, to personally embody and strenuously practice what one has attained, seeking not to feel ashamed before the sages and worthies, [and so?] …

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
與之齊乃行之事而學之至也愚生晩進
末學義理之閫奥未能窺其髣髴何敢思
齊聖賢但於知行二者用力之始亦竊有
志焉而未得其要也聞之程子甞曰涵養
須用敬進學則在致知蓋敬者一心之主
宰萬事之根本學者無志聖賢之學則已
如有志焉非先之以敬以涵養其本原則
心境不純何以為致知之地乎致知且無
地何從而力行乎子朱子答東萊吕氏書
===
稱此兩言雖約入德之門無以踰之者豈
欺我哉雖然敬之一字豈特始學者知行
之初所當從事雖至於成德之地亦不可
缺焉故曰敬者聖學之所以成始而成終
者也管中之見真妄未必敢以質之明執
事
第三問
方晟
同考試官教諭陳批時務一策以虞周君
punctuated:
與之齊，乃行之事而學之至也。愚生晩進末學，義理之閫奥未能窺其髣髴，何敢思齊聖賢？但於知行二者用力之始，亦竊有志焉，而未得其要也。聞之程子甞曰：「涵養須用敬，進學則在致知。」蓋敬者，一心之主宰，萬事之根本。學者無志聖賢之學則已，如有志焉，非先之以敬以涵養其本原，則心境不純，何以為致知之地乎？致知且無地，何從而力行乎？子朱子答東萊吕氏書，稱此兩言雖約，入德之門無以踰之者，豈欺我哉！雖然，敬之一字，豈特始學者知行之初所當從事，雖至於成德之地，亦不可缺焉。故曰：「敬者，聖學之所以成始而成終者也。」管中之見，真妄未必，敢以質之明執事。
第三問
方晟
同考試官教諭陳批：時務一策，以虞、周君
translation_en:
… [and seeking] to equal them: this is the business of practice and the culmination of learning. As an ignorant student of late advancement and superficial learning, I have not even caught a faint glimpse of the inner depths of moral principle—how would I dare aspire to equal the sages and worthies? Yet at the outset of applying my effort to both knowledge and action, I privately harbor this ambition, though I have not yet grasped the essential point. I have heard that Master Cheng (Cheng Yi 程頤) once said: "For nurturing the mind one must employ reverence; advancing in learning lies in the extension of knowledge." For reverence is the master of the one mind and the root of the myriad affairs. If a scholar has no ambition for the learning of the sages and worthies, then so be it; if he does have such ambition, unless he puts reverence first so as to nurture the fundamental source, the state of his mind will not be pure—and on what ground will he then extend his knowledge? If there is not even ground for extending knowledge, how can he proceed to strenuous practice? When Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹), in his reply to Mr. Lü of Donglai (Lü Zuqian 呂祖謙), praised these two maxims, saying that concise though they are, as a gateway to entering virtue nothing can surpass them, how could he have been deceiving us! Even so, is this single word "reverence" merely something to which beginning scholars should devote themselves at the outset of knowledge and action? Even when one reaches the stage of accomplished virtue, it cannot be dispensed with. Therefore it is said: "Reverence is that whereby the learning of the sages brings both beginning and end to completion." Whether this narrow view of mine is true or false I cannot be sure, and I venture to submit it to the judgment of the enlightened examiners.

Third Question
Fang Sheng 方晟
Associate Examiner Instructor Chen comments: On the policy question concerning current affairs, he takes the ruler… [of Shun's Yu and the Zhou]

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
臣治泰保泰立說酌古準今鑿鑿可行宛然規戒之意
形於言表非卓然有見者不能
同考試官教諭章批場中答者多昧大易治
泰之旨惟此卷隨問隨答能以仁義禮智之德而周八事
之用足見窮經致用之學
考試官修撰劉批據理以斷時務卓然有識
之士也
考試官左庶子黎批此策難答風簷寸晷方戰慄於
監試威嚴之下而能操觚染翰條答無遺可見京師多學者
===
聖人釋易道之泰其設戒也深人君保世
道之泰其慮患也遠此天理之所以常存
而人心之所以不泯也昔者百姓昭明黎
民於變非有虞之泰乎然慎乃有位敬脩
可願帝舜之心方且凛凛於南面之時而
為之臣者又詳陳儆戒之謨四海永清萬
姓悅服非成周之泰乎然敬勝怠吉義勝
欲從武王之心方且慄慄於垂拱之日而
為之臣者亦懇言慎德之戒所以然者無
punctuated:
臣治泰、保泰立說，酌古準今，鑿鑿可行，宛然規戒之意形於言表，非卓然有見者不能。
同考試官教諭章批：場中答者多昧《大易》治泰之旨，惟此卷隨問隨答，能以仁義禮智之德而周八事之用，足見窮經致用之學。
考試官修撰劉批：據理以斷時務，卓然有識之士也。
考試官左庶子黎批：此策難答，風簷寸晷，方戰慄於監試威嚴之下，而能操觚染翰，條答無遺，可見京師多學者。
聖人釋《易》道之泰，其設戒也深；人君保世道之泰，其慮患也遠。此天理之所以常存，而人心之所以不泯也。昔者「百姓昭明，黎民於變」，非有虞之泰乎？然「慎乃有位，敬脩可願」，帝舜之心，方且凛凛於南面之時，而為之臣者，又詳陳儆戒之謨。「四海永清，萬姓悅服」，非成周之泰乎？然「敬勝怠吉，義勝欲從」，武王之心，方且慄慄於垂拱之日，而為之臣者，亦懇言慎德之戒。所以然者無
translation_en:
… and ministers governing in times of Great Peace (Tai) and preserving Great Peace, weighing antiquity and measuring the present with solid, practicable proposals. A spirit of remonstrance and admonition is vividly manifest beyond the words themselves; none without outstanding insight could achieve this.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor (jiaoyu): Most respondents in the examination hall were blind to the purport of governing in times of Great Peace in the Great Change (Book of Changes). Only this paper answers each point as it is asked, able to encompass the application of the eight affairs through the virtues of benevolence, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom—amply demonstrating learning that exhausts the Classics for practical application.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Senior Compiler (xiuzhuan): Judging current affairs on the basis of principle, he is a scholar of outstanding discernment.

Comment by Examiner Li, Left Mentor of the Secretariat of the Heir Apparent (zuo shuzi): This policy question is difficult to answer. Under the windswept eaves with only an inch of shadow on the sundial, while trembling beneath the stern majesty of the surveillance officials, that he was able to take up his writing tablet, dip his brush, and answer item by item without omission shows how many learned scholars there are in the capital.

When the sages explained Great Peace (Tai) in the Way of the Changes, the warnings they established were profound; when a ruler preserves Great Peace in the way of the world, his foresight regarding calamities is far-reaching. This is why Heavenly principle endures forever and the human mind is never extinguished. In antiquity, "the hundred surnames became illustrious, and the black-haired people were transformed"—was this not the Great Peace of Yu (Shun)? Yet "being cautious in his position, and reverently cultivating what is desirable," the mind of Emperor Shun was still filled with awe even as he faced south as sovereign, while those who served as his ministers further set forth in detail counsels of vigilance and admonition. "The four seas were forever cleared, and the myriad姓 gladly submitted"—was this not the Great Peace of Completed Zhou? Yet knowing that "when reverence prevails over indolence it is auspicious, and when righteousness prevails over desire one follows the right," the mind of King Wu was still trembling with dread on the very days he ruled withrobes hanging down and hands folded, while those who served as his ministers likewise earnestly spoke warnings on being cautious in virtue. The reason for this was none…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
他聖君賢相制治於未亂不待已亂而始
為制治之方保邦於未危不待已危而方
脩保邦之具盖深體易道而行之世雖已
泰恒存艱苦貞固之心冀永享其泰之福
也今夫泰之為卦歴師比畜履而後成其
所由来遠矣至是則君推誠以任下臣盡
誠以事君上下之志通朝廷之泰也君子
来處於內小人往處於外善惡之分明天
下之泰也宜若可以久安長治矣然聖人
===
釋之既謂無常安平而不險陂又慮三陰
在上皆失其實是即舜武不自滿足之心
預圖保之耳能存舜武之心雖至於豐可
免憂雖入於否可無咎又何将来之足恤
哉若夫九二一爻乃人臣之正位上應六
五之賢君聖人於此立法以包荒用馮河
不遐遺朋亡四者為治泰之道盡之矣彼
其以含容之量而施剛果之用以經遠之
識而為馭衆之公聖賢所為也四者豈不
punctuated: 他，聖君賢相，制治於未亂，不待已亂而始為制治之方；保邦於未危，不待已危而方脩保邦之具。盖深體《易》道而行之，世雖已泰，恒存艱苦貞固之心，冀永享其泰之福也。今夫《泰》之為卦，歴《師》、《比》、《畜》、《履》而後成，其所由来遠矣。至是，則君推誠以任下，臣盡誠以事君，上下之志通，朝廷之泰也；君子来處於內，小人往處於外，善惡之分明，天下之泰也。宜若可以久安長治矣。然聖人釋之，既謂「無常安平而不險陂」，又慮「三陰在上，皆失其實」，是即舜、武不自滿足之心，預圖保之耳。能存舜、武之心，雖至於《豐》，可免憂；雖入於《否》，可無咎，又何将来之足恤哉！若夫九二一爻，乃人臣之正位，上應六五之賢君。聖人於此立法，以「包荒」、「用馮河」、「不遐遺」、「朋亡」四者為治泰之道，盡之矣。彼其以含容之量而施剛果之用，以經遠之識而為馭衆之公，聖賢所為也，四者豈不
translation_en: … other reason than that sage rulers and worthy chief ministers establish order before disorder arises, not waiting until disorder has already broken out to devise methods for establishing order; and they preserve the state before peril arrives, not waiting until peril has already struck to prepare the means for preserving the state. Indeed, they deeply embody the Way of the Book of Changes (Yi) and put it into practice: even when the world is already in a state of Peace (Tai), they constantly maintain a mind of arduousness and firm rectitude, hoping thereby to forever enjoy the blessings of that peace. Now, the hexagram Tai (Peace) is formed only after passing through the hexagrams Shi (The Army), Bi (Holding Together), Xu (The Taming Power of the Small), and Lü (Treading); its origins reach far back. When this stage is reached, the ruler extends sincerity in employing his subordinates, and the ministers exhaust their sincerity in serving their ruler; the intentions of superior and inferior communicate freely, which is the peace of the royal court. Gentlemen come to occupy the inner realm, while petty men go to occupy the outer realm; the distinction between good and evil is clear, which is the peace of the empire. It would seem that enduring tranquility and lasting order could thus be assured. Yet when the Sage explained this, he not only said that "there is no permanent peace and levelness that does not turn into danger and obliquity," [cf. Commentary on the Third Nine of Tai] but also worried that "the three yin lines above have all lost their substance" [cf. Commentary on the Fourth Six of Tai]. This is precisely the mind of Emperors Shun and Wu, who never grew self-satisfied, taking precautions in advance to preserve their rule. If one can preserve the mind of Shun and Wu, then even when reaching the hexagram Feng (Abundance), one can be free of sorrow; even when entering the hexagram Pi (Standstill), one can be free of blame—what need would there be to worry about the future! As for the Second Nine line, it is the proper position of a minister, corresponding above to the worthy ruler at the Fifth Six line. Here the Sage established the model, taking the four principles of "bearing with the uncultured," "crossing the river without a boat," "not neglecting the distant," and "putting away factionalism" as exhausting the Way of governing in a time of Peace. Combining a capacity for tolerant forbearance with the exercise of resolute decisiveness, and uniting far-reaching vision with impartiality in governing the multitude—this is the conduct of sages and worthies. How could these four principles not…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
相為用乎方
今正泰寧之世也執事發策即此爻為問愚
請竭其所見焉夫以包荒言之世道久安
則法度弛而習成誕慢欺蔽矣驟然改之
近患先起當包以大量可也然如賞功勳
賑災傷之類似包之難盡焉誠使崇德報
功之必審量入為出之有節而又法舜之
御眾以寬於一視同仁之中施之有等則
所包者皆當尚何愈濫愈乏之足憂乎以
===
馮河言之人情久逸則紀綱縱而下趨委
靡陵替矣恬然安之將來愈甚當革以猛
力可也然如禦外侮去貪殘之類似革之
示勇焉誠使選將練兵之有道司銓斷獄
之得人而又法武王之一怒安民於綱紀
四方之事斷行無疑則所革者皆當又何
暴師貽累之足患乎以不遐遺言之眾志
久寧則變故少而無復深謀矣遠而慮之
必周庶事不可遺遐遠也然如恤兵民用
punctuated: 相為用乎？方今正泰寧之世也，執事發策，即此爻為問，愚請竭其所見焉。夫以「包荒」言之：世道久安，則法度弛而習成誕慢欺蔽矣；驟然改之，近患先起，當包以大量可也。然如賞功勳、賑災傷之類，似包之難盡焉。誠使崇德報功之必審，量入為出之有節，而又法舜之御眾以寬，於一視同仁之中，施之有等，則所包者皆當，尚何愈濫愈乏之足憂乎？以「馮河」言之：人情久逸，則紀綱縱而下趨委靡陵替矣；恬然安之，將來愈甚，當革以猛力可也。然如禦外侮、去貪殘之類，似革之示勇焉。誠使選將練兵之有道，司銓斷獄之得人，而又法武王之一怒安民，於綱紀四方之事，斷行無疑，則所革者皆當，又何暴師貽累之足患乎？以「不遐遺」言之：眾志久寧，則變故少而無復深謀矣；遠而慮之，必周庶事，不可遺遐遠也。然如恤兵民、用
translation_en:
… mutually serve one another? The present is precisely an age of great peace and tranquility. Since Your Excellency, in posing this policy question, has inquired specifically into this hexagram line, I, in my simplicity, beg leave to exhaust my humble views on the matter.

To speak first of "embracing the uncultivated" (baohuang): when the world has long been at peace, laws and regulations slacken, and customs settle into arrogance, negligence, deceit, and concealment. If one reforms them abruptly, immediate troubles will arise first; thus it is fitting to embrace them with great magnanimity. Yet in matters such as rewarding meritorious service and relieving disaster-stricken areas, it seems difficult for such magnanimity to cover everything completely. Truly, if we ensure that honoring virtue and recompensing merit are carefully scrutinized, and that regulating expenditures according to revenues is governed by moderation—while also modeling ourselves on Shun's governing the multitude with宽容 (lenience), applying graded distinctions within universal benevolence—then all that is embraced will be appropriate. Why then would there still be any need to worry about rewards growing ever more excessive or resources ever more depleted?

To speak next of "crossing a river without a boat" (pinghe, i.e., resolute boldness): when human nature has long been accustomed to ease, discipline and order loosen, and those below sink into listlessness, apathy, and decline. If one complacently rests in this state, it will only grow worse in the future; thus it is fitting to reform it with vigorous force. Yet in matters such as repelling foreign aggression and removing greedy and cruel officials, such reform seems merely a display of bravery. Truly, if there is a proper method for selecting generals and training troops, and if the right men are found to take charge of personnel evaluation and the adjudication of legal cases—while also modeling ourselves on King Wu, who by a single burst of righteous anger brought peace to the people, executing measures to bring order to the four quarters with decisive resolve and without hesitation—then all that is reformed will be appropriate. Why then would there be any need to fear exhausting the army or leaving behind lingering burdens?

To speak of "not neglecting the distant" (bu xiayi): when the minds of the multitude have long been at peace, unforeseen emergencies are few, and there is no longer any deep or far-reaching planning. To take long-term precautions, one must be comprehensive in all affairs and must not neglect what is distant and remote. Yet in matters such as showing compassion to soldiers and civilians and employing…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
賢才之類猶若未周焉誠使仁先小民而
不虐無告賢揚側陋而不廢困窮而又法
舜之好問好察於明目達聰之美克全則
下情上達尚何遐逺之見遺乎以不私朋
比言之時勢乆順則人情肆而至於私昵
惡德矣約而正之必絶黨與不可私朋比
也然如禁奢侈限田產之類猶若相昵焉
誠使周公恭儉近戚先行晏嬰節約貴家
首務而又法武王之建其有極於淫朋比
===
德之討必嚴則公道大彰又何朋比之相
昵乎夫易之四事足以盡保泰之常法而
主司所言之八事猶未盡今日之急務引
而伸之觸類而長之然後治道全也欽惟
皇上法天立道措世泰寧觀其寛裕溫柔足以
有容而仁之量以弘發彊剛毅足以有執
而義之勇以决則包荒用馮河之事官使
得其人文理密察足以有别而智之明以
廣齊莊中正足以有敬而禮之節以詳則
punctuated:
賢才之類，猶若未周焉。誠使仁先小民而不虐無告，賢揚側陋而不廢困窮；而又法舜之好問好察，於明目達聰之美克全，則下情上達，尚何遐逺之見遺乎？以不私朋比言之，時勢乆順，則人情肆而至於私昵惡德矣；約而正之，必絶黨與，不可私朋比也。然如禁奢侈、限田產之類，猶若相昵焉。誠使周公恭儉，近戚先行；晏嬰節約，貴家首務；而又法武王之建其有極，於淫朋比德之討必嚴，則公道大彰，又何朋比之相昵乎？

夫《易》之四事，足以盡保泰之常法；而主司所言之八事，猶未盡今日之急務。引而伸之，觸類而長之，然後治道全也。欽惟皇上法天立道，措世泰寧。觀其寛裕溫柔足以有容，而仁之量以弘；發彊剛毅足以有執，而義之勇以决，則包荒、用馮河之事，官使得其人；文理密察足以有别，而智之明以廣；齊莊中正足以有敬，而禮之節以詳，則
translation_en:
… employing men of virtue and talent, this still seems not yet fully comprehensive. Truly, if benevolence is extended first to the common people so that the helpless are not oppressed, and men of worth are raised up from humble obscurity so that the destitute are not neglected; and if one further models oneself on Shun's fondness for questioning and examining, fully realizing the beauty of seeing and hearing clearly in all directions, then the conditions of those below will reach those above—how then could anything distant be overlooked? As for not showing partiality to factions: when the times and circumstances have long been favorable, human inclinations grow unrestrained to the point of private intimacy and evil conduct; to restrain and rectify them, one must cut off factional partisans and not show partiality to cliques. Yet measures such as prohibiting extravagance and limiting landholdings still seem as if tainted by mutual partiality. Truly, if the reverence and frugality of the Duke of Zhou are practiced first by close imperial relatives, and the economy of Yan Ying (晏嬰) is made the foremost duty of noble families; and if one further models oneself on King Wu's establishment of the Supreme Standard, strictly punishing licentious factions and collusive virtue, then the public way will be greatly manifest—what mutual intimacy of factions could there still be?

Now, the four principles of the Book of Changes (Yi) are sufficient to exhaust the constant method of preserving Great Peace (Tai), whereas the eight matters spoken of by the Examiner still do not exhaust the urgent tasks of today. Only by extending and expanding them, reasoning by analogy to develop them further, can the way of governance be made complete. I reverently reflect that Your Majesty models Yourself on Heaven to establish the Way, placing the world in peaceful tranquility. Observing how Your generosity, magnanimity, gentleness, and mildness suffice to be all-embracing, so that the capacity of Your benevolence is broadened; and how Your vigor, strength, firmness, and resolution suffice to hold fast, so that the courage of Your righteousness is decisive—then in the matters of "embracing the uncultivated" and "crossing the river without a boat," offices and commissions obtain the right men. Observing how Your refined pattern and close examination suffice to make distinctions, so that the clarity of Your wisdom is widened; and how Your solemnity, gravity, impartiality, and uprightness suffice to command respect, so that the regulations of Your ritual propriety are made thorough—then …

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
不遺遐朋亡之事付託稱其任是以一氣
默運太虛無為天下皆知吾
君主泰之為聖而不知所以聖手扶日月足履
星辰天下皆知吾相輔泰之為賢而不知
所以賢愚生竊願恭拜今日之
舜禹而續賡歌陳雅頌以備言泰道之未備者
執事以為何如
第四問
郭維藩
===
同考試官訓導沈 批 性理之學最為微奧塲
中能會一眾說分析詳明者寡此篇詞理俱到參之前
塲如出一手春闈高捷此其兆矣
同考試官教諭徐 批 敷對詳明必於性理之
學深有所造詣者與前二塲稱宜冠本經
考試官修撰劉 批 答性理策而能以意貫之
詞氣流動畧無窘滯似非臆說矣
考試官左庶子黎 批 辨析性理詳盡詩經他卷皆
不及此
punctuated:
不遺遐、朋亡之事，付託稱其任。是以一氣默運，太虛無為，天下皆知吾君主泰之為聖，而不知所以聖；手扶日月，足履星辰，天下皆知吾相輔泰之為賢，而不知所以賢。愚生竊願恭拜今日之舜、禹，而續賡歌、陳《雅》《頌》，以備言泰道之未備者。執事以為何如？

第四問
郭維藩
同考試官訓導沈批：性理之學最為微奧，塲中能會一眾說、分析詳明者寡。此篇詞理俱到，參之前塲，如出一手。春闈高捷，此其兆矣。
同考試官教諭徐批：敷對詳明，必於性理之學深有所造詣者。與前二塲稱，宜冠本經。
考試官修撰劉批：答性理策而能以意貫之，詞氣流動，畧無窘滯，似非臆說矣。
考試官左庶子黎批：辨析性理詳盡，《詩經》他卷皆不及此。
translation_en:
… the tasks of "not neglecting the distant" and "dispelling factionalism" are entrusted to men who match their responsibilities. Thus, as the single vital force silently revolves and the Great Void remains in non-action, all under Heaven know that our Sovereign who presides over peace and prosperity (tai) is sage, without knowing whereby he is sage; with hands supporting the sun and moon and feet treading among the stars and constellations, all under Heaven know that our ministers who assist in peace and prosperity are worthy, without knowing whereby they are worthy. This foolish student humbly wishes to bow in reverence before the Shun and Yu of today, to continue the exchanged songs of praise and set forth the Odes and Hymns, so as to state fully what remains unstated concerning the Way of peace and prosperity. What do the examiners think of this?

Question Four
Guo Weifan 郭維藩
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Shen 沈 comments: The learning of human nature and principle (xingli) is most subtle and profound; in the examination hall, few are able to synthesize the various doctrines and analyze them with clarity and thoroughness. In this essay, both diction and reasoning hit the mark, and when compared with his earlier sessions' papers, they clearly come from the same hand. A high placement in the spring Metropolitan Examination is presaged here!
Associate Examiner, Instructor Xu 徐 comments: His exposition and reply are detailed and clear; he must be one who has attained deep mastery in the learning of human nature and principle. It matches the quality of his first two sessions and deserves to be placed first in his classic.
Examiner, Senior Compiler Liu 劉 comments: In answering the policy question on human nature and principle, he is able to thread it together with a coherent conception; his diction and vital breath flow smoothly without the slightest stiffness or obstruction—it is clearly no mere conjecture.
Examiner, Left Mentor Li 黎 comments: His discrimination and analysis of human nature and principle are exhaustive; none of the other papers in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing) equal this one.

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
言性一也有指其天命之本然者有指其
氣質之雜然者以天命之本然者言之性
即理也理善則性無不善矣以氣質之雜
然者言之清濁美惡參差不齊性亦隨之
而異此所以廑執事之問也請申言之人
之生也得天地之理以為性得天地之氣
以為形是性本諸理而形本諸氣也然理
之與氣雖有異名實非二物故以理而言
性則無不善以氣而言性此理旣墮於氣
===
質之中不能不隨之而有清濁美惡之異
矣孔子之性相近兼其墮於氣質者言故
曰相近孟子之性善專以理言故直曰善
孔孟之言非不同也各有攸當耳且孔子
傳易嘗曰繼之者善成之者性矣孟子性
善之言雖曰擴前聖所未發然深究其義
盖本于此孟子之言固不在孔子之外也
夫性旣有理氣之分言性者兼舉而析言
之可也而孟子立言乃語理而遺氣是以
punctuated: 言性一也，有指其天命之本然者，有指其氣質之雜然者。以天命之本然者言之，性即理也，理善則性無不善矣；以氣質之雜然者言之，清濁美惡參差不齊，性亦隨之而異。此所以廑執事之問也。請申言之：人之生也，得天地之理以為性，得天地之氣以為形，是性本諸理而形本諸氣也。然理之與氣，雖有異名，實非二物。故以理而言性，則無不善；以氣而言性，此理旣墮於氣質之中，不能不隨之而有清濁美惡之異矣。孔子之「性相近」，兼其墮於氣質者言，故曰「相近」；孟子之「性善」，專以理言，故直曰「善」。孔、孟之言非不同也，各有攸當耳。且孔子傳《易》，嘗曰：「繼之者善，成之者性」矣。孟子性善之言，雖曰擴前聖所未發，然深究其義，盖本于此。孟子之言，固不在孔子之外也。夫性旣有理氣之分，言性者兼舉而析言之可也；而孟子立言，乃語理而遺氣，是以
translation_en: In speaking of human nature (xing), although it is one, some refer to the original state of the Mandate of Heaven, while others refer to the mixed state of psychophysical endowment (qizhi). Speaking of it in terms of the original state of the Mandate of Heaven, human nature is principle (li); since principle is good, human nature is never not good. Speaking of it in terms of the mixed state of psychophysical endowment, purity and turbidity, beauty and ugliness are uneven and varied, and human nature likewise differs accordingly. This is what has prompted Your Excellency's question. Allow me to elaborate on this: When a person is born, he receives the principle of Heaven and Earth to form his nature, and receives the vital force (qi) of Heaven and Earth to form his physical body; thus, nature is rooted in principle and the physical body is rooted in vital force. Yet although principle and vital force have different names, in reality they are not two separate things. Therefore, if one speaks of human nature in terms of principle, there is nothing in it that is not good; if one speaks of human nature in terms of vital force, once this principle has fallen into the psychophysical endowment, it cannot help but follow it and exhibit differences of purity and turbidity, beauty and ugliness. Confucius's dictum that "by nature people are close to one another" speaks of it in a way that encompasses its having fallen into the psychophysical endowment, and thus he says they are "close." Mencius's doctrine that "human nature is good" speaks of it exclusively in terms of principle, and thus he directly says it is "good." The words of Confucius and Mencius are not really different; each is appropriate to its own focus. Moreover, in his commentary on the Book of Changes (Yi), Confucius once said: "That which ensues from it is goodness; that which realizes it is nature." Although Mencius's doctrine of the goodness of human nature is said to have expanded upon what former sages had not yet articulated, if one deeply investigates its meaning, it is in fact rooted in this. The words of Mencius indeed do not lie outside those of Confucius. Now, since human nature has this distinction between principle and vital force, those who discuss human nature ought to bring up both and analyze them together; yet in establishing his teachings, Mencius spoke of principle while omitting vital force. For this reason…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
其言固至矣而不能破後世之惑遂使性
惡出於荀况善惡混出於楊雄而三品出
於韓愈其說紛紛靡有定論至宋張子有
天地氣質之分程子有不備不明之論然
後兼舉無遺而諸子紛紛之說皆泯矣夫
天地之性以不雜乎氣質者言其理甚明
宜無待於辨說而氣質之性則理雜乎氣
而參差不齊信有可疑如執事之慮者然
亦不外乎理氣之等差也朱子嘗謂氣質
===
之禀或不能齊所謂不齊者盖氣有清有
濁而氣之質有美有惡故其賦于人也清
濁以分智愚而美惡以分賢不肖焉是則
氣與質本一物耳非氣之外别有所謂質
也而元儒吳氏乃謂受氣於父成質於母
分而二之其論誤矣朱子又謂理只是善
氣却有惡盖理無形而氣有迹無形則無
往而不善有迹則運行之久能無清濁美
惡之殊乎人之生也性諸理而形諸氣此
punctuated: 其言固至矣，而不能破後世之惑，遂使性惡出於荀况，善惡混出於楊雄，而三品出於韓愈。其說紛紛，靡有定論。至宋張子有天地氣質之分，程子有不備不明之論，然後兼舉無遺，而諸子紛紛之說皆泯矣。夫天地之性，以不雜乎氣質者言，其理甚明，宜無待於辨說；而氣質之性，則理雜乎氣而參差不齊，信有可疑如執事之慮者。然亦不外乎理氣之等差也。朱子嘗謂氣質之禀或不能齊。所謂不齊者，盖氣有清有濁，而氣之質有美有惡；故其賦于人也，清濁以分智愚，而美惡以分賢不肖焉。是則氣與質本一物耳，非氣之外别有所謂質也。而元儒吳氏乃謂受氣於父，成質於母，分而二之，其論誤矣。朱子又謂理只是善，氣却有惡。盖理無形而氣有迹；無形則無往而不善，有迹則運行之久，能無清濁美惡之殊乎？人之生也，性諸理而形諸氣，此
translation_en: …his words were certainly supreme, yet they could not dispel the doubts of later generations. Consequently, the theory that human nature is evil came from Xun Kuang 荀況, that good and evil are mixed came from Yang Xiong 楊雄, and that there are three grades of human nature came from Han Yu 韓愈. Their doctrines were confused and varied, without reaching any settled conclusion. When we come to the Song dynasty, Master Zhang 張子 [Zhang Zai 張載] drew the distinction between the nature of Heaven and Earth and the psychophysical nature, and Master Cheng 程子 argued that speaking of one without the other is either incomplete or unclear. Only then were both aspects comprehensively addressed with nothing left out, and the confused doctrines of the various philosophers all vanished. Now, the nature of Heaven and Earth is spoken of in terms of that which is unmixed with psychophysical endowment; its principle is crystal clear and ought to require no debate or explanation. As for the psychophysical nature, however, principle is mixed with vital force (qi 氣) and is uneven and ununiform—truly giving rise to doubts, just as Your Excellency is concerned about. Yet this, too, is nothing other than the gradations and differences of principle and vital force. Master Zhu 朱子 [Zhu Xi 朱熹] once said that the endowment of psychophysical stuff cannot always be uniform. What is meant by its being ununiform is that vital force has clarity and turbidity, while the material substance (zhi 質) of vital force has beauty and ugliness; therefore, when it is endowed in human beings, clarity and turbidity distinguish the wise from the foolish, while beauty and ugliness distinguish the worthy from the unworthy. Thus, vital force and material substance are originally a single thing; it is not the case that apart from vital force there is something else called material substance. Yet the Yuan Confucian Mr. Wu 吳氏 [Wu Cheng 吳澄] claimed that one receives vital force from the father and forms material substance from the mother, dividing them into two—his argument is mistaken. Master Zhu also said that principle is simply good, whereas vital force involves evil. This is because principle has no form whereas vital force leaves traces; being formless, it is good in every respect, whereas having traces, as it circulates over a long time, how could it avoid differences of clarity and turbidity, beauty and ugliness? When a person is born, his nature is rooted in principle and his form is given by vital force; this is why…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
性之本體所以亦無往而不善也然濁者
清之變惡者美之變則氣之初也亦本清
本美矣理氣果可以二物言之耶西山蔡
氏主張氣質太過其意謂理終拗氣不轉
以之言下愚不移之徒則可矣而自是以
上之人可一委之生質而不加脩為乎了
齋陳氏又謂氣質之用狹道學之功大以
之言中人以上之人則可矣而下愚不移
之徒可轉而為聖賢乎朱子兩不以為然
===
也宜矣此皆聖賢性命之微非初學可到
然明問下及不敢以默謹述所聞如此執
事幸進而教之
第五問
馬中錫
同考試官訓導賀 批策塲正欲觀士子有
用之學連日批閱多掛一漏百殊厭人目惟此卷攟春
秋暨歷代史條答無遺且得褒貶斷例之旨足見學識
同考試官教諭朱 批史以紀事為歷代之鑒
punctuated:
性之本體所以亦無往而不善也。然濁者清之變，惡者美之變，則氣之初也，亦本清本美矣，理、氣果可以二物言之耶？西山蔡氏主張氣質太過，其意謂理終拗氣不轉，以之言下愚不移之徒則可矣；而自是以上之人，可一委之生質而不加脩為乎？了齋陳氏又謂氣質之用狹，道學之功大，以之言中人以上之人則可矣；而下愚不移之徒，可轉而為聖賢乎？朱子兩不以為然也，宜矣。此皆聖賢性命之微，非初學可到。然明問下及，不敢以默，謹述所聞如此，執事幸進而教之。

第五問
馬中錫
同考試官訓導賀批：策塲正欲觀士子有用之學，連日批閱，多掛一漏百，殊厭人目。惟此卷攟《春秋》暨歷代史，條答無遺，且得褒貶斷例之旨，足見學識。
同考試官教諭朱批：史以紀事，為歷代之鑒。
translation_en:
…is why the fundamental substance of human nature is also good in every respect. Yet since turbidity is a transformation of clarity, and badness is a transformation of fineness, at the beginning of vital force (qi), it too was originally clear and originally fine—can principle (li) and vital force really be spoken of as two separate things? Mr. Cai of Xishan [Cai Yuanding 蔡元定] laid excessive emphasis on psychophysical endowment (qizhi), his meaning being that principle ultimately cannot bend or turn vital force around. To say this of those of the lowest stupidity who do not change is permissible; but as for people above that level, can one simply leave everything to their innate endowment and apply no self-cultivation? Meanwhile, Mr. Chen of Liaozhai [Chen Guan 陳瓘] maintained that the function of psychophysical endowment is narrow while the efficacy of the Learning of the Way (daoxue) is great. To say this of people of middling ability and above is permissible; but as for those of the lowest stupidity who do not change, can they be turned into sages and worthies? That Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] disapproved of both views is fitting indeed. All these belong to the subtleties of the sages and worthies concerning human nature and destiny, which a beginning student cannot reach. Yet since Your enlightened question has condescended to reach me, I dare not remain silent; I respectfully set forth what I have heard in this manner, and hope that Your Excellency will bring me forward and instruct me.

Fifth Question
Ma Zhongxi 馬中錫
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor (xundao) He comments: In the policy-essay session we precisely wish to observe the practical learning of the candidates. Reading and commenting over several days, most essays catch one thing while missing a hundred, which truly wearies the eyes. Only this paper gathers material from the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) and the histories of successive dynasties, answering point by point without omission, and moreover grasps the purport of the principles of praise, blame, and judgment—quite sufficient to show learning and insight.
Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Zhu comments: History records events to serve as a mirror for successive dynasties. …

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
此策於君父臣子賞罰王霸夷夏隨問條對斷制明
白深得董狐之筆
考試官修撰劉批文以理為主此卷三場雄詞健
筆往往出人意表而卒能不失其理焉非功深力到者不能也
取以魁多士輿論允協矣
考試官左庶子黎批今科取士徧閱三場此卷初
場見其明易學二場見其富文學三場又見其稽古窮理
識時務之學北方學者未能或之先也遂拔出為一百三十五人
冠冕噫大行鹽車吾與爾脫之矣尚當三冬苦學一日千里以
===
一空冀北之羣
任史官者何所師惟仲尼焉師纂史事者
何所法惟春秋焉法何者山莫高於五嶽
也然五嶽雖高而人猶可升非山之至也
惟崑崙乃為山之至焉水莫深於四瀆也
然四瀆雖深而人猶可踰非水之盡也惟
滄海乃為水之盡焉仲尼之作春秋其山
之崑崙水之滄海乎故五嶽祖於崑崙則
支派有所本四瀆歸於滄海則源流有所
punctuated:
此策於君父臣子、賞罰、王霸、夷夏，隨問條對，斷制明白，深得董狐之筆。
考試官修撰劉批：文以理為主。此卷三場，雄詞健筆，往往出人意表，而卒能不失其理焉，非功深力到者不能也。取以魁多士，輿論允協矣。
考試官左庶子黎批：今科取士，徧閱三場，此卷初場見其明《易》學，二場見其富文學，三場又見其稽古窮理、識時務之學，北方學者未能或之先也。遂拔出為一百三十五人冠冕。噫！大行鹽車，吾與爾脫之矣，尚當三冬苦學，一日千里，以一空冀北之羣。
任史官者何所師？惟仲尼焉師。纂史事者何所法？惟《春秋》焉法。何者？山莫高於五嶽也，然五嶽雖高而人猶可升，非山之至也，惟崑崙乃為山之至焉；水莫深於四瀆也，然四瀆雖深而人猶可踰，非水之盡也，惟滄海乃為水之盡焉。仲尼之作《春秋》，其山之崑崙、水之滄海乎！故五嶽祖於崑崙，則支派有所本；四瀆歸於滄海，則源流有所
translation_en:
… This policy essay responds item by item to the questions regarding ruler and father, minister and son, rewards and punishments, true king and hegemon, and Chinese and barbarian. Its judgments are clear and decisive, deeply capturing the brushstroke of Dong Hu.

Examiner Liu, Senior Compiler, comments: In writing, principle is paramount. Across all three sessions, this candidate's papers feature vigorous diction and a robust brush, often surpassing expectations yet ultimately never losing sight of principle. None could achieve this without deep cultivation and consummate effort. Selecting him to stand first among the many scholars is in complete accord with public opinion.

Examiner Li, Left Mentor of the Secretariat of the Heir Apparent, comments: In selecting scholars in the current examination, having read thoroughly through all three sessions, I saw in this candidate's first-session papers his clear understanding of the learning of the Classic of Changes (Yi), in the second session his rich literary learning, and in the third session his learning in investigating antiquity, fathoming principle, and understanding current affairs. Among northern scholars, none has been able to surpass him. Accordingly, he has been singled out to crown the one hundred and thirty-five graduates. Ah! From pulling a salt cart up the Taihang Mountains, I have freed you! Still, you ought to study arduously through three winters and advance a thousand li in a day, so as to empty the herds of northern Ji of every fine steed.

Whom should those who serve as historiography officials take as their master? Only Zhongni [Confucius] should they take as their master. What should those who compile historical events take as their model? Only the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) should they take as their model. Why is this? Among mountains, none is higher than the Five Sacred Peaks; yet although the Five Sacred Peaks are high, men can still ascend them, so they are not the ultimate of mountains—only Kunlun is the ultimate of mountains. Among waters, none is deeper than the Four Great Rivers; yet although the Four Great Rivers are deep, men can still cross them, so they are not the utmost limit of waters—only the vast sea is the utmost limit of waters. Zhongni's composition of the Spring and Autumn Annals—is it not the Kunlun of mountains and the vast sea of waters! Therefore, when the Five Sacred Peaks trace their ancestry to Kunlun, their branching ranges have a foundation; when the Four Great Rivers return to the vast sea, their sources and streams have …

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
□□史而折衷於春秋則義例於是乎定
矣昔者周道衰微諸侯僭竊人欲日肆天
理日亡仲尼天理之所在不以為己任而
誰可於是假魯史以寓王法撥亂世反之
正觀其尊君父也如桓公會首止以定王
世子則殊會以褒之文公升僖於閔之上
則書躋以貶之而天倫正矣定臣子也如
國夏圍戚邑納蒯聵則序齊首惡以誅之
莒人立異姓主鄫祀則責莒滅鄫以罪之
===
而天典惇矣賞有功也如子突救衛尊曰
王人魏絳和戎蕭魚錫命而勸善詳矣罰
有罪也如宰咺歸賵斥名示貶曹伯歸京
伯討有光而懲惡嚴矣以至明王霸也如
葵丘明禁重書示美楚丘專封削爵示懲
而真偽分矣辨夷夏也如會戎于潛譏其
務外盟楚于齊惡其失道而內外別矣春
秋之為經如此蓋百王之大法萬世之準
繩也其後朱子作通鑑綱目一取法於春
punctuated: □□史而折衷於《春秋》，則義例於是乎定矣。昔者周道衰微，諸侯僭竊，人欲日肆，天理日亡。仲尼天理之所在，不以為己任而誰可？於是假魯史以寓王法，撥亂世，反之正。觀其尊君父也，如桓公會首止以定王世子，則殊會以褒之；文公升僖於閔之上，則書「躋」以貶之，而天倫正矣。定臣子也，如國夏圍戚邑、納蒯聵，則序齊首惡以誅之；莒人立異姓主鄫祀，則責莒滅鄫以罪之，而天典惇矣。賞有功也，如子突救衛，尊曰「王人」；魏絳和戎，蕭魚錫命，而勸善詳矣。罰有罪也，如宰咺歸賵，斥名示貶；曹伯歸京，伯討有光，而懲惡嚴矣。以至明王霸也，如葵丘明禁，重書示美；楚丘專封，削爵示懲，而真偽分矣。辨夷夏也，如會戎于潛，譏其務外；盟楚于齊，惡其失道，而內外別矣。《春秋》之為經如此，蓋百王之大法，萬世之準繩也。其後朱子作《通鑑綱目》，一取法於《春
translation_en:
… [If those who compile] histories find their standard of judgment in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), then the principles and precedents are thereby established.

In ancient times, the Way of Zhou declined and grew faint, the feudal lords usurped authority, human desires grew daily more unbridled, and Heavenly Principle daily perished. Since Heavenly Principle resided in Confucius (Zhongni), if he did not take it as his own responsibility, who else could? Thereupon he borrowed the history of Lu to embody the Kingly Law, bringing order out of a chaotic age and returning it to rectitude.

Observe how he honored ruler and father: for instance, when Duke Huan [of Qi] assembled at Shouzhi to establish the Royal Heir Apparent, he distinguished the meeting in the phrasing in order to praise it; when Duke Wen [of Lu] elevated the tablet of Duke Xi above that of Duke Min, he wrote "ascended" (ji) in order to censure it—and thus the natural human relationships were rectified.

In fixing the duties of ministers and sons: for instance, when Guo Xia [of Qi] besieged the town of Qi to install Kuaikui, he listed Qi first as the chief offender in order to condemn it; when the people of Ju set up someone of a different surname to preside over the sacrifices of Zeng, he held Ju responsible for extinguishing Zeng in order to convict it—and thus the Heavenly canons were upheld.

In rewarding the meritorious: for instance, when Zitu rescued Wei, he honored him by calling him a "King's Man"; when Wei Jiang made peace with the Rong and [the Marquis of Jin] bestowed gifts at the covenant of Xiaoyu [?], the encouragement of goodness was made thorough.

In punishing the guilty: for instance, when the Steward Xuan came to present funerary gifts, he was referred to by his personal name to show censure; when the Earl of Cao was sent to the capital, the hegemon's punitive expedition was glorified—and thus the chastisement of evil was made strict.

Even down to distinguishing the True King from the Hegemon: for instance, when the injunctions were proclaimed at Kuiqiu, he recorded the event repetitively to show approval; when [Duke Huan] arbitrarily enfeoffed [Wei at] Chuqiu, he omitted his title to show admonition—and thus the genuine and the counterfeit were separated.

In differentiating barbarians and Chinese: for instance, in the meeting with the Rong at Qian, he criticized [Duke Yin] for attending to external affairs; in the covenant with Chu at Qi, he detested their loss of the proper Way—and thus the internal and the external were distinguished.

Such is the Spring and Autumn Annals as a classic: it is indeed the great law for a hundred kings and the standard for ten thousand generations. Thereafter, when Master Zhu [Zhu Xi] composed the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror (Tongjian gangmu), he modeled it entirely upon the Spring…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
秋師其意不襲其詞如漢安帝嗣殤帝乃
禰和帝此漢人之謬綱目特紀殤帝之年
正位號也周世宗父柴氏乃禰郭威此世
宗之誤綱目直書周主之父光祿卿致仕
柴守禮實姓氏也此非春秋尊君父之意
乎至於宋濮安懿王歐陽脩以為當稱親
司馬光以為當稱皇伯紛紛不一作史者
宜别立殊稱書曰皇伯父某國大王論斯
定矣張留侯本為韓後乃仕漢是時韓祀
===
已絕綱目書曰留侯張良及謝病辟穀原
其心也魏武帝本夏侯氏後乃姓曹當時
事出傳聞綱目直書曹操而於分注載夏
侯氏錄其真也此非春秋定臣子之意乎
至於范魯公本臣周降於宋為中書平章
辱身無耻作史者宜書曰周降臣與馮道
同科議斯决矣陳湯康居之捷匡衡排其
挢難綱目大書矯制發兵後乃紀其封爵
不盡予也李德裕維城之績牛僧孺拒其
punctuated: 秋，師其意不襲其詞。如漢安帝嗣殤帝，乃禰和帝，此漢人之謬，《綱目》特紀殤帝之年，正位號也；周世宗父柴氏，乃禰郭威，此世宗之誤，《綱目》直書「周主之父光祿卿致仕柴守禮」，實姓氏也。此非《春秋》尊君父之意乎？至於宋濮安懿王，歐陽脩以為當稱親，司馬光以為當稱皇伯，紛紛不一，作史者宜别立殊稱，書曰「皇伯父某國大王」，論斯定矣。張留侯本為韓後，乃仕漢，是時韓祀已絕，《綱目》書曰「留侯張良」，及「謝病辟穀」，原其心也；魏武帝本夏侯氏後，乃姓曹，當時事出傳聞，《綱目》直書「曹操」，而於分注載「夏侯氏」，錄其真也。此非《春秋》定臣子之意乎？至於范魯公本臣周，降於宋為中書平章，辱身無耻，作史者宜書曰「周降臣」，與馮道同科，議斯决矣。陳湯康居之捷，匡衡排其挢難，《綱目》大書「矯制發兵」，後乃紀其封爵，不盡予也；李德裕維城之績，牛僧孺拒其
translation_en:
… the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), emulating its underlying intent without merely copying its phrasing. For instance, Emperor An of Han (Han Andi 漢安帝) succeeded Emperor Shang (Shangdi 殤帝), yet enshrined Emperor He (Hedi 和帝) as his immediate paternal ancestor (ni 禰); this was an error on the part of the men of Han, so the Outline and Details (Gangmu) specifically records the reign year of Emperor Shang in order to rectify the reigning title. Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou (Zhou Shizong 周世宗) had a father of the Chai 柴 clan, yet he enshrined Guo Wei 郭威 as his immediate paternal ancestor; this was Shizong's mistake, so the Outline and Details directly writes, "Chai Shouli 柴守禮, father of the Ruler of Zhou and retired Chief Minister of Imperial Entertainments (Guanglu qing)," in order to verify his true surname and clan. Is this not the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals in honoring ruler and father? As for Prince Anyi of Pu (Pu Anyi Wang 濮安懿王) in the Song, Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩 held that he should be addressed as "parent" (qin 親), while Sima Guang 司馬光 held that he should be addressed as "Imperial Uncle" (Huangbo 皇伯). Amidst such conflicting opinions, a historian ought to establish a distinct designation and write "Imperial Uncle, Grand Prince of Such-and-Such State," whereby the debate would be settled.

Zhang Liang 張良, Marquis of Liu (Liuhou 留侯), was originally a descendant of the ruling house of Han 韓, yet he served the Han 漢 dynasty. At that time the sacrifices to Han 韓 had already been extinguished, so the Outline and Details writes "Zhang Liang, Marquis of Liu," and later "he pleaded illness and abstained from grain," thereby pardoning him on account of his true heart. Emperor Wu of Wei (Wei Wudi 魏武帝) was originally a descendant of the Xiahou 夏侯 clan, yet he took the surname Cao 曹. Because at the time the matter rested on hearsay, the Outline and Details directly writes "Cao Cao 曹操" in the main text, while recording "of the Xiahou clan" in the interlinear notes to preserve the truth. Is this not the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals in fixing the status of subjects and sons? As for Fan Zhi 范質, Duke of Lu (Lugong 魯公), he was originally a subject of the Later Zhou, yet he surrendered to the Song and became a Joint Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery (Zhongshu pingzhang), disgracing his person without shame. A historian ought to write "the surrendered subject of Zhou," placing him in the same category as Feng Dao 馮道, whereby the judgment would be decided.

Regarding Chen Tang's 陳湯 victory in Kangju 康居, Kuang Heng 匡衡 disparaged him for fabricating authorization and courting danger [? 挢難]; the Outline and Details writes in large characters "he forged an imperial decree to mobilize troops," and only afterward records the enfeoffment of his noble title, thus not granting him full approval. Regarding Li Deyu's 李德裕 achievement at Weicheng 維城 (Weizhou 維州), Niu Sengru 牛僧孺 rejected it on the grounds of…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
失信綱目大書悉怛謀以維城來降不受
後又載怛謀追贈盡予之也此非春秋賞
有功之意乎至於李重進自以周室懿親
義不臣宋作史者並於韓通則常典明矣
薄昭戕使之討温公病其傷恩綱目書曰
有罪自殺原法以誅之也荀彧諫魏之簒
杜牧譬之教盜綱目書曰侍中光祿大夫
參軍事荀彧自殺辱其冒漢爵而失身也
此非春秋討有罪之意乎至於王安石新
===
法之禍程子雖言吾黨激成然荆舒之罪
至於亡宋作史者等於惠卿則斷例公矣
漢宣帝厲精圖治綱目詳載刑名之害治
雜霸也唐太宗躬行仁義綱目備言倫理
之玷心假仁也此非春秋明王霸之意乎
至於宋太祖心合堯舜然視文王之至德
有乖作史者推原其心姑俟混一則微旨
彰矣趙武靈用夷變夏綱目書曰趙始胡
服招騎射貶而夷狄之也魏孝文用夏變
punctuated: 失信，《綱目》大書「悉怛謀以維城來降，不受」，後又載怛謀追贈，盡予之也。此非《春秋》賞有功之意乎？至於李重進自以周室懿親，義不臣宋，作史者並於韓通，則常典明矣。薄昭戕使之討，温公病其傷恩，《綱目》書曰「有罪自殺」，原法以誅之也；荀彧諫魏之簒，杜牧譬之教盜，《綱目》書曰「侍中、光祿大夫、參軍事荀彧自殺」，辱其冒漢爵而失身也。此非《春秋》討有罪之意乎？至於王安石新法之禍，程子雖言吾黨激成，然荆舒之罪至於亡宋，作史者等於惠卿，則斷例公矣。漢宣帝厲精圖治，《綱目》詳載刑名之害，治雜霸也；唐太宗躬行仁義，《綱目》備言倫理之玷，心假仁也。此非《春秋》明王霸之意乎？至於宋太祖心合堯舜，然視文王之至德有乖，作史者推原其心，姑俟混一，則微旨彰矣。趙武靈用夷變夏，《綱目》書曰「趙始胡服招騎射」，貶而夷狄之也；魏孝文用夏變
translation_en:
… breach of good faith; the Outline and Details (Gangmu) writes in large characters, "Xidanmou surrendered with the city of Wei, and it was not accepted," and later also records the posthumous honors conferred upon Xidanmou, thereby granting full recognition to it. Is this not the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) in rewarding the meritorious? As for Li Chongjin, who regarded himself as a close relative of the house of Zhou and out of righteousness refused to serve the Song as a subject: if historians place him alongside Han Tong, then the constant norms are made clear.

In the punishment of Bo Zhao for killing an envoy, the Duke of Wen [Sima Guang] faulted it as harming familial affection; the Outline and Details writes, "having committed a crime, he killed himself," condemning him on the basis of the law. When Xun Yu remonstrated against the Wei usurpation, Du Mu likened him to someone who instructs a thief; the Outline and Details writes, "the Palace Attendant (Shizhong), Grand Master for Splendid Happiness (Guanglu Dafu), and Military Consultant (Canjunshi) Xun Yu killed himself," shaming him for falsely bearing Han titles while having compromised his personal integrity. Is this not the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals in punishing the guilty? As for the disaster of Wang Anshi's New Policies, although Master Cheng [Cheng Hao] said that our own faction provoked it into happening, yet the guilt of Jingshu [Wang Anshi] reached the point of bringing ruin to the Song; if historians rank him on a par with [Lü] Huiqing, then the precedent of judgment is impartial.

Emperor Xuan of Han vigorously strove for good governance, yet the Outline and Details records in detail the harm caused by penal law and administrative technique (xingming), showing that his governance was mixed with the way of the hegemon. Taizong of Tang personally practiced benevolence and righteousness, yet the Outline and Details fully recounts the blemishes in his human relationships, showing that in his heart he merely feigned benevolence. Is this not the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals in distinguishing the true king from the hegemon? As for Taizu of Song, his heart accorded with Yao and Shun, yet compared with the supreme virtue of King Wen there was some discrepancy; if historians trace the motives of his heart and wait until the realm was unified [before recognizing his legitimacy], then the subtle import becomes manifest.

King Wuling of Zhao used barbarian ways to transform Chinese ways, and the Outline and Details writes, "Zhao first adopted Hu dress and recruited mounted archers," demoting him and treating him as a barbarian. Emperor Xiaowen of Wei used Chinese ways to transform …

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
夷綱目書曰魏禁胡服祀孔子進而中□
之也此非春秋辨夷夏之意乎至於元世
祖威行朔漠視孝文之成功差勝作史者
審究其迹稍嚴冠履則要義明矣噫謂春
秋非山之崑崙水之滄海則綱目何以法
之而後世作史者又皆祖之歟方
今玉堂鴻筆鸞臺宿學收拾宇宙之英靈折
衷古今之信筆以成一代之書愚生何足
以知其詳姑以是復明問之萬一云耳
punctuated: 夷，《綱目》書曰：「魏禁胡服，祀孔子。」進而中□之也。此非《春秋》辨夷夏之意乎？至於元世祖威行朔漠，視孝文之成功差勝，作史者審究其迹，稍嚴冠履，則要義明矣。噫！謂《春秋》非山之崑崙、水之滄海，則《綱目》何以法之，而後世作史者又皆祖之歟？方今玉堂鴻筆、鸞臺宿學，收拾宇宙之英靈，折衷古今之信筆，以成一代之書。愚生何足以知其詳？姑以是復明問之萬一云耳。
translation_en:
… the barbarians; the Outline and Details (Gangmu) records: "Wei prohibited Hu clothing and sacrificed to Confucius (Kongzi)," elevating them and treating them as Central [States] [?]. Is this not the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) in distinguishing between barbarian and Chinese (Xia)? As for Emperor Shizu of Yuan (Khubilai Khan), whose might extended across the northern deserts, compared to the achievements of Emperor Xiaowen he was somewhat superior; yet the historiographers carefully investigated his traces and slightly tightened the distinction between cap and shoes [i.e., hierarchy between Chinese and barbarian], whereby the essential principle was made clear. Alas! If one were to say that the Spring and Autumn Annals is not the Kunlun among mountains or the vast ocean among waters, then why would the Outline and Details model itself upon it, and why would historiographers of later generations all take it as their ancestor?

At present, the great literary brushes of the Jade Hall [Hanlin Academy] and the venerable scholars of the Phoenix Terrace [Secretariat-Chancellery] gather the finest spirits of the universe and weigh the trustworthy records of ancient and modern times to complete the history of an era. How could this foolish student be worthy of knowing its details? I merely offer this to answer one ten-thousandth of Your enlightened question.

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
順天府鄉試錄後序
我
國家取士于科目餘百年矣而
其制未嘗少渝者蓋有道焉
自古昔選舉法廢君天下者
專以科目取士而其試之之
法或以詩賦或以辭學或以
===
法律書筭紛更不一至我
國家始一以經術而諸法悉罷
宜乎法立制定盡善盡美其
得人致治之盛非前代所可
及也成化甲午秋順天府鄉
試屆期府尹臣簡府丞臣川
以
punctuated:
順天府鄉試錄後序

我國家取士于科目餘百年矣，而其制未嘗少渝者，蓋有道焉。自古昔選舉法廢，君天下者專以科目取士，而其試之之法，或以詩賦，或以辭學，或以法律、書、筭，紛更不一。至我國家，始一以經術，而諸法悉罷。宜乎法立制定，盡善盡美，其得人致治之盛，非前代所可及也。成化甲午秋，順天府鄉試屆期，府尹臣簡、府丞臣川以
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination

Our dynasty has selected scholars through the examination categories for over a hundred years, and that its system has never changed in the slightest is because there is a guiding principle to it. Ever since the selection methods of antiquity fell into disuse, those who ruled the realm have relied exclusively on examination categories to select scholars; yet their methods of testing them—whether by poetry and rhapsodies, or by literary composition and erudition, or by laws and statutes, calligraphy, and mathematics—were repeatedly altered and never uniform. Only with our dynasty was everything unified under classical learning, and all those other methods were completely abolished. Fittingly, once the method was established and the system fixed, it was utterly good and utterly perfected, and the flourishing of its recruiting of talent and attainment of good governance could not be matched by former dynasties. In the autumn of the jiawu year of the Chenghua era [1474], when the time arrived for the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination, the Prefect, Your servant Jian [Xing Jian 邢簡], and the Vice Prefect, Your servant Chuan [Li Chuan 李川], reported this…

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
聞
上命臣淳典文衡而臣健亦與焉
臣等被
命謹如故事合太學及畿甸之
士凡三試之其為文非本于
經深于道者弗之取既而百
三十五人中式是皆精選也
===
臣竊惟科目以經術為重而
士之自處亦必以經術為重
何則經以載道重經術盖重
乎道也然士之於道豈可掩
襲而取之哉其必居敬以涵
養本原致知以思索義理涵
養既熟思索既深則一旦脫
punctuated: 聞。上命臣淳典文衡，而臣健亦與焉。臣等被命，謹如故事，合太學及畿甸之士，凡三試之。其為文非本于經、深于道者，弗之取。既而百三十五人中式，是皆精選也。臣竊惟科目以經術為重，而士之自處，亦必以經術為重。何則？經以載道，重經術，盖重乎道也。然士之於道，豈可掩襲而取之哉？其必居敬以涵養本原，致知以思索義理；涵養既熟，思索既深，則一旦脫
translation_en:
… reported this to the throne. His Majesty commanded your servant Chun 淳 to preside over the literary balance, and your servant Jian 健 also participated therein. Having received this command, your servants respectfully followed established precedent, gathering the scholars of the Directorate of Education and the capital region and testing them in three sessions. As for their compositions, those not rooted in the Classics and profound in the Way were not selected. In the end, one hundred and thirty-five men passed the examination; these are all choice selections.

Your servant humbly reflects that the examination system places supreme importance on classical learning, and in how scholars conduct themselves, they too must place supreme importance on classical learning. Why is this? The Classics serve to convey the Way; to value classical learning is in fact to value the Way. Yet as for a scholar's relation to the Way, how could he seize it through superficial appropriation? He must abide in reverence so as to nurture the fundamental source, and extend his knowledge so as to ponder moral principles. Once his nurturing is mature and his pondering profound, then suddenly, casting off …

title: 成化十年順天府鄉試錄
text:
然有悟而道乃在我由是而
進于誠意正心修身以推之
治國平天下斯為有道之士
科目誠得是人而用之則唐
虞三代之治可庶幾矣乃若
辭章枝葉之習律筭技藝之
末借使精通入妙然學不本
===
于身心則其人固衆人也善
圖治者將焉用之哉嗟夫鄒
魯教熄世道益降厯漢晋隋
唐士之聾瞽斯道乆矣幸而
有宋周程張朱數君子者奮
起百世之下表章于遺經以
開悟學者然而當時之君顧
punctuated: 然有悟，而道乃在我。由是而進于誠意、正心、修身，以推之治國、平天下，斯為有道之士。科目誠得是人而用之，則唐虞、三代之治可庶幾矣。乃若辭章枝葉之習，律筭技藝之末，借使精通入妙，然學不本于身心，則其人固衆人也，善圖治者將焉用之哉？嗟夫！鄒魯教熄，世道益降，厯漢、晋、隋、唐，士之聾瞽斯道乆矣。幸而有宋周、程、張、朱數君子者，奮起百世之下，表章于遺經以開悟學者。然而當時之君顧
